Strips non-digits + handles leading `1` country code + prepends `+1` to 10-digit US national number; returns null on any input that doesn't normalize to exactly 10 US digits. Header comment documents the libphonenumber-js swap target when/if international registration ships — every caller inherits the upgrade transparently. (2) [`backend/src/controllers/carrierController.ts`](backend/src/controllers/carrierController.ts) — phone duplicate check inserted between email check and DOT/MC checks at ~line 125. Both stored + submitted numbers normalized to E.164 before comparison (light scan at pre-revenue volumes; the indexed `phoneNormalized` column refactor is banked at ~10K+ rows as a separate sprint). Also new `flagRegistrationDuplicate(opts)` helper (~80 LOC) — fires brief alert to `COMPLIANCE_EMAIL` + writes `SystemLog WARNING` row with `logType=SECURITY` + `source="registration-duplicate"`. Both wrapped in `.catch()` so neither blocks the 409 response. Email body + SystemLog details carry **SHA-256 hash (first 16 chars)** of the colliding value — never plaintext PII (defense against accidental log-table PII exposure + against compliance@-inbox-compromise scenario surfacing the attempted values). `registrationIp` + `registrationCountry` capture moved earlier in the function so the compliance flag has forensic context (pre-ala these were captured after duplicate checks; duplicate hits had no IP/country signal because the variables didn't exist yet). Email + phone collision branches both fire the flag before returning. (3) [`backend/src/routes/carrier.ts`](backend/src/routes/carrier.ts) — two new rate limiters mounted on `POST /register`: (a) `registerIpLimiter` — **10 attempts / 15 min** keyed by `req.ip`, fires BEFORE multer (no body needed); (b) `registerContactLimiter` — **3 attempts / 60 min** keyed by composite `${lowercaseEmail}|${digitOnlyPhone}`, fires AFTER multer + body normalization middleware so `req.body.email` + `req.body.phone` are populated. Composite-key fallback to `ip:${req.ip}` if both email + phone absent (malformed request) — never returns empty string which express-rate-limit would treat as a global counter. Skip-handler returns 429 "Too many registration attempts. Please try again later." — generic per enumeration hygiene (no echo of which limiter fired or against which key). (4) [`frontend/src/components/ui/VersionFooter.tsx`](frontend/src/components/ui/VersionFooter.tsx) — version bump + comment block. (5) CLAUDE.md §11 row (this row). **Enumeration hygiene (directive §4):** duplicate error responses carry NO name / MC / agency echo. Email collide → 409 `"Email already registered"` (unchanged from today). Phone collide → 409 `"Phone number already registered"` (mirrors). Rate-limit hit → 429 with generic message. Compliance flag dispatch happens AFTER the 409 response is sent, so duplicate-hit response time is indistinguishable from non-collision response from the attacker's clock — closes the timing-side-channel that would otherwise leak whether email/phone existed before the response fully landed. **Architectural pattern banked (consistent with v3.8.akz unified-gate convention):** when a side-effect (compliance flag dispatch) shares a common trigger surface (any duplicate hit on registration), the side-effect logic lives as a single helper function alongside the surface. Controllers pass authoritative context (collidedField + attemptedValue + attemptIp + attemptCountry); the helper handles dispatch + logging + PII-hashing uniformly. Future sprints adding a third collision class (e.g. DOT/MC duplicate) inherit the same helper signature. **Banked for future sprints (out of v3.8.ala scope):** (a) Email lowercase-on-lookup to close the case-sensitivity enumeration vector — `Test@example.com` ≠ `test@example.com` today on Postgres + Prisma `findUnique`. Pre-existing gap surfaced by Phase A audit. (b) `User.phone @unique` schema constraint + backfill — race window stays today since the duplicate check is application-level only. Pre-revenue volumes make this acceptable; race window closes via DB constraint when N grows. (c) libphonenumber-js adoption — only when international registration ships. Current DIY normalizer is sufficient for US-only scope. (d) Indexed `phoneNormalized` column on `User` — refactor when N > ~10K carriers. Today's full scan over phone-bearing users is light at pre-revenue volumes. (e) **OTP verification path / SMS verification — explicitly held for next sprint** pending Wasi's SMS-path decision per directive. (f) Backend required-doc validation gate — pre-existing gap from v3.8.aky banking; continues to defer. **Pre-commit gates per Sub-pattern 11:** backend `tsc --noEmit` clean, frontend `tsc --noEmit` + `npx next build` clean. **No Prisma migration. No new env vars. No new package install** — `express-rate-limit` already in deps per Phase A. Per §3.1: v3.8.akz → v3.8.ala sequence-continuous. **Letter:** akz latest origin/main HEAD; ala sequence-continuous on top per the §3.1 double-letter continuation (after `akz` comes `ala`, NOT `alz` or any other variant). |

| v3.8.ajb | 2026-05-24 (this commit) | **Sprint F (required-documents enforcement) + critical EIN registration regression hotfix (atomic bundle).** Two related Step 3 / submit-path fixes shipped together since both touch `onboarding/page.tsx` + both block carrier onboarding. **Critical bug fix (regression from v3.8.air):** reproduced via curl against deployed prod — `POST /api/carrier/register` with `ein:""` → 400 `{"error":"Validation failed","details":[{"field":"ein","message":"EIN must be 9 digits"}]}`. In v3.8.air I removed the EIN input from Step 1 but kept `ein: ""` in form state with the comment *"retained as empty default for backend payload compatibility — backend will gracefully accept empty string"*. That assumption was wrong. Backend Zod is `ein: z.string().regex(/^\d{9}$/).optional()` — `.optional()` accepts ABSENT, but PRESENT-with-empty-string fails the regex (zero digits ≠ nine). `regData` spread in `handleSubmit` included `ein: ""`, so every carrier registration since v3.8.air had been silently failing at Step 5 Submit. Wasi caught it on the first real end-to-end registration through deployed v3.8.aja. **Fix:** 3-line frontend change — peel `ein` out of regData destructure via `ein: einFromForm`; conditionally include only if non-empty: `...(einFromForm ? { ein: einFromForm } : {})`. Backend `.optional()` accepts absent field cleanly. **Methodology lesson:** smoke verification on form sprints must include FULL submit path, not just step-level visual checks. `feedback_visual_smoke_before_push.md` covers layout/chrome but doesn't enumerate end-to-end submit verification. Banking as extension: for any sprint touching `handleSubmit` payload shape OR backend Zod schema, smoke MUST include a real curl-or-browser submit through to 200/400 + response body inspection. **Sprint F (required documents enforcement):** Step 3 documents (W-9, Insurance Certificate, Authority Letter + Safety Fitness Certificate if Canadian) were UI-visible but completely optional at the canNext gate — carriers could proceed without uploading any. (1) `canNext` extended for `step === 2` with per-key `hasDoc()` checks; Safety Cert conditional on `hasCanadianOps`. (2) Document data extended with `required: true` flag on all visible docs (Safety Cert already conditional per v3.8.aiv). (3) Visual indicators: red asterisk `text-[#9B2C2C]` after required doc labels; missing-state warning-amber bg+border (`bg-[#FBEFD4] border-[#B07A1A]/40`); description text appends " — required" when missing; upload icon switches to amber. (4) Count banner above doc list "X of Y required uploaded" — green when all met, amber otherwise. (5) Section intro extends with "All marked with * are required to submit." **Scope:** ~50 LOC in onboarding/page.tsx (3 LOC EIN + ~45 LOC required-docs UI + canNext block). No backend changes, no CSP changes, no new dependencies. **Pre-commit gates (Sub-pattern 11 CI parity):** frontend tsc --noEmit clean; frontend npx next build clean (`/onboarding` 17.2 kB → 17.5 kB). **Letter:** aja latest origin/main HEAD; ajb sequence-continuous on top. Cloudflare deploy only — no backend changes, Render path-filter skips this push (per aiy retry-mechanic learning, which is fine). **Post-deploy verification:** (1) EIN hotfix — register a test carrier through full flow to Step 5 + Submit, should now succeed (no more "Validation failed"). (2) Required docs — try Next without uploading any, button stays disabled; upload W-9 + Insurance + Authority → enables (no Canadian region) or also require Safety Cert (Canadian region selected). (3) Count banner updates live as each doc uploads. **Patterns applied:** §3.5 audit-first (curl-reproduced the EIN regression before fixing); §3.3 atomic single-file ship with bundled fixes; §3.4 halt > ship (paused Sprint F push to diagnose EIN first instead of pushing on top); §3.2 visual smoke; §19 Sub-pattern 11 CI-parity. **Patterns emerged:** methodology lesson — **submit-path-smoke as required gate** for any sprint touching handleSubmit / Zod schema. Visual chrome can pass eye-test perfectly while a payload-shape regression sits in the hot path for many sprints. Extension of `feedback_visual_smoke_before_push` banked. |

| v3.8.ajv | 2026-05-24 (this commit) | **Security hotfix bundle (C1 + C2 + C6) from blindsides audit P0.** Three critical security bugs caught during the post-Phase-1-7 blindsides re-audit, all clustering in the rate-confirmation + password-change surfaces. Atomic ship — small, no migration, validates the post-v3.8.ajs clean deploy chain. **C1 — RC PDF download authorization bypass (CRITICAL — financial espionage vector):** `downloadRateConfirmationPdf` controller at `rateConfirmationController.ts:163` was authorized to the CARRIER role per `routes/rateConfirmations.ts:24` but had no per-record check that the logged-in CARRIER actually owns the load. Any logged-in carrier could enumerate RC IDs (cuid format) and download any other carrier's full RC PDF — including carrier cost, fuel surcharge, accessorials, and margin. Direct competitive intelligence harvest path. **Fix:** added `if (req.user.role === "CARRIER" && rc.load.carrierId !== req.user.id) return 403` after the findUnique. AE-side roles (BROKER/ADMIN/CEO/DISPATCH/OPERATIONS/ACCOUNTING) bypass — they need to download any carrier's RC during normal review workflow. **C2 — RC sign authorization bypass (signature forgery vector):** `signRateConfirmation` controller at line 197 had the same surface — endpoint authorized to CARRIER per route line 25, no per-record ownership check. Any logged-in carrier could sign any other carrier's RC, falsifying commitment + corrupting audit trail (the `carrierSignature` field would store the wrong signer's name). **Fix:** same role-conditional gate pattern as C1. Added `load: { select: { carrierId: true } }` to the existing `findUnique` to make the carrierId available. AE roles still pass through for the "mark as signed on behalf" operational case (carrier emailed a wet signature outside the portal). **C6 — Password downgrade vector:** registration validator at `validators/carrier.ts:10-15` enforces γ "Very Strong" tier (14+ chars + uppercase + lowercase + digit + special). Pre-ajv the `changePasswordSchema` + `forceChangePasswordSchema` at `carrierAuth.ts:46-52` accepted `min(8)` only. Account-takeover path: attacker who briefly gets in via credential stuffing downgrades to `12345678`, retains access after legitimate carrier resets to a new strong password. **Fix:** new shared `STRONG_PASSWORD` Zod chain mirroring the registration's exact 5-rule validation. Applied to both `changePasswordSchema.newPassword` and `forceChangePasswordSchema.newPassword`. HIBP not re-checked server-side per the registration's same precedent (frontend handles HIBP via k-anonymity API; backend enforces composition as defense-in-depth). **Scope:** ~50 LOC net across 2 backend files (rateConfirmationController.ts + carrierAuth.ts). No frontend changes. No migration. **Pre-commit gates per Sub-pattern 11:** backend tsc + frontend tsc + next build all clean. **P1002 risk:** zero — no migrate deploy needed. Validates the post-v3.8.ajs clean deploy chain is fully operational. **Other P0 items remaining banked (blindsides audit):** v3.8.ajw — state-machine integrity bundle (central validateLoadStatusTransition + notification cleanup cron + audit log on declineTender/counterTender + RC failure recovery from acceptTender's fire-and-forget); v3.8.ajx — operational compliance bundle (insurance auto-suspend active-load gate + SUSPENDED gates on /:id/status + /:id/documents + /:id/check-call + QP monthly limits + Compass vetting failure telemetry + OTP override admin tool). **Letter:** aju → ajv sequence-continuous. |

| v3.8.ajt | 2026-05-24 | **Carrier portal critical-bug bundle (B1+B2+B3+B5) from Phase 1-7 audit.** Four bugs caught during the post-ajr 7-phase carrier-portal audit, all shipping as one atomic commit since they cluster around the carrier-facing post-approval lifecycle. **B1 (Phase 4 — RC visibility):** `Load.rateConfirmationPdfUrl` schema field has existed since pre-ajt but was NEVER populated by any write path. Result: carrier-portal RC download link at `/carrier/dashboard/my-loads` line 183 was gated on the field and always invisible despite the `GET /api/rate-confirmations/:id/pdf` endpoint being CARRIER-authorized + functional. Fix: in `sendRateConfirmation` controller (line 140-148), after RC status flip to SENT, also `prisma.load.update` with `rateConfirmationPdfUrl: /api/rate-confirmations/${rc.id}/pdf`. Carrier portal link now resolves to the existing endpoint; httpOnly cookie auths it on click. Closes §13.3 Item 170. **B2 (Phase 6 — invoice automation):** `autoGenerateInvoice(loadId)` service exists in `invoiceService.ts:5` but was never called from the POD upload endpoint at `carrierLoads.ts:413`. Result: carrier delivered + uploaded POD + no invoice ever generated automatically. Fix: trigger `autoGenerateInvoice(load.id)` from the POD upload block when the new POD-advancing status flip lands on POD_RECEIVED. Fire-and-forget non-blocking pattern; service is idempotent (checks for existing invoice on loadId). **B3 (Phase 6 — POD status flip):** audit agent's "inverted logic" framing was technically incorrect (the ternary at line 467 read correctly), but the underlying UX gap was real — most carriers upload POD at `AT_DELIVERY` (the POD IS their proof of completing delivery) before manually marking DELIVERED in the portal. Pre-ajt only DELIVERED → POD_RECEIVED was wired, so loads stayed at AT_DELIVERY with POD attached. Fix: extend the advancing-statuses list to `["AT_DELIVERY", "DELIVERED", "LOADED"]` → `"POD_RECEIVED"`. Earlier statuses (BOOKED/DISPATCHED/AT_PICKUP/IN_TRANSIT) still don't auto-advance — uploading POD when you haven't reached the destination is likely an error. **B5 (Phase 1 — approval email gap):** AE-side approve action pre-ajt went through `POST /carrier/verify/${id}` with `{ status: "APPROVED" }` which (a) didn't fire a carrier-facing approval email, (b) didn't write a dedicated `AuditAction.APPROVE` row (used generic UPDATE), (c) had no notification fan-out. Result: carriers learned they were approved only by happening to log in and seeing the dashboard switch from status page to main dashboard. Fix: new `backend/src/services/approvalService.ts` with `approveCarrier({ carrierId, approvedById, note })` — atomic transaction flips `onboardingStatus → APPROVED` + sets `approvedAt` + clears any prior rejection metadata defensively + syncs legacy `User.isVerified` (kept in lockstep with 27+ existing readers per CLAUDE.md §11 v3.8.aje note). Service validates not-already-APPROVED + not-SUSPENDED. Fires brand-canonical carrier email "Welcome to the Caravan Partner Program" (reply-to operations@) with optional AE note + portal CTA + green success palette + creates in-app Notification row (type ONBOARDING) for the bell. New endpoint `POST /api/carriers/:id/approve` (ADMIN/CEO + Zod + `auditLog("APPROVE", "Carrier")`). AE Console mutation routed to this endpoint when status === "APPROVED"; legacy `/carrier/verify/${id}` path retained as fallback. **Note on `approvedById`:** CarrierProfile has only `approvedAt` (no `approvedById` column); audit trail captures the AE via the AuditLog row. Schema migration to add `approvedById` banked as small follow-up if AE forensics needs per-row attribution. **Scope:** ~210 LOC net across 4 files (new approvalService.ts + carriers.ts route + carrierLoads.ts POD block + rateConfirmationController.ts send block + carriers/page.tsx mutation route swap). **Pre-commit gates per Sub-pattern 11:** backend tsc + frontend tsc + next build all clean. **No migration.** **P1002 risk:** zero — no migrate deploy needed. **Banked for v3.8.aju (next commit):** B4 — public `/track/[token]` Next.js dynamic route for the shipper tracking link. TrackingTab references the URL but no route exists. Separate atomic ship per §3.3. **Other audit findings banked for future sprints (v3.8.ajv+):** decline reason persistence (Item 90), counter-tender email (Item 89), central state machine validator (Item 159), ACH banking self-service, dispute filing UI, CarrierFraudBanner in portal, profile-completeness banner, Marco Polo carrier context, notification inbox UX, RC PDF polish (transit hours, T&C body, versioning, email tracking binding), photo capture at AT_PICKUP/LOADED, GPS auto-capture, carrier in-app check-call reminders, shipper pickup email auto-trigger on status flip, ELD device mapping UI, email-verify reminder cron, auto-approve messaging on success screen, Compass vetting failure telemetry, status field vs onboardingStatus drift cleanup. **Letter:** ajs → ajt sequence-continuous. |

| v3.8.ajs | 2026-05-24 | **Defensive build-time DIRECT_URL guard + diagnostic for v3.8.ajr P1002 recurrence.** Render deploy of v3.8.ajr hit P1002 again despite the v3.8.ajg DIRECT_URL split being in place. Build log smoking gun: `Datasource "db": ... at "ep-green-frog-ajsgv9me-pooler.c-3.us-east-2.aws.neon.tech"` — Prisma migrate was STILL routing through the pooler (note `-pooler` in hostname). Root cause: the `DIRECT_URL` env var on Render WAS set (Prisma generate succeeded — would have P1012'd otherwise), but its **value contained the pooled URL by mistake**. Wasi presumably copied from Neon's "Connect" modal without toggling pooling off → both DATABASE_URL and DIRECT_URL pointed at the same pooled endpoint → DIRECT_URL split was decorative, not functional. **Permanent fix shipped:** new `backend/scripts/check-direct-url.js` pre-migrate guard added to canonical buildCommand at §2.2 (between `npm run build` and `npx prisma migrate deploy`). Fails fast (exit 1) with self-explanatory remediation message if (a) `DIRECT_URL` is unset OR (b) `DIRECT_URL` hostname contains `-pooler`. Also surfaces a non-fatal warning if `DATABASE_URL` and `DIRECT_URL` point at different Neon projects (sanity check against typos). Pre-ajs the failure mode was a silent 10s P1002 timeout with no hint about WHY; post-ajs the build fails in <1s with the exact Render-dashboard remediation steps + Neon-dashboard "toggle pooling off" guidance + four-location checklist reference. **Tested with 3 scenarios:** (1) DIRECT_URL unset → fails with "env var is not set" + remediation; (2) DIRECT_URL with pooler hostname → fails with "hostname contains '-pooler'" + cause explanation; (3) DIRECT_URL correctly direct → exits 0 with `✓ DIRECT_URL configured correctly`. URL parsing via `new URL()` constructor (handles edge cases like passwords with `@` characters). Sanity-check: parses DATABASE_URL similarly + warns (not fails) if the two URLs point at different Neon projects (e.g., one's hostname starts with `ep-foo` and the other with `ep-bar` — that's almost certainly a typo). **Scope:** ~110 LOC (new script) + 2-line buildCommand updates in CLAUDE.md §2.2 + render.yaml. **Banks methodology principle:** the four-location checklist for env() schema reference additions from §19 Sub-pattern 11 case study #2 (CLAUDE.md §19 ci-hotfix retrospective) is now enforced as CODE, not just docs. **§19 Sub-pattern 11 fire #3 banked** — third surface where local pre-commit gates passed but Render deploy failed due to env-config mismatch (Sprint 51 #1: JSX ESLint; v3.8.ajg → ci-hotfix #2: CI workflow env block; v3.8.ajr → ajs #3: Render env var value-not-just-presence). Three-fire validation lineage now satisfied per §19 sub-rule c three-fire canonical promotion convention. Fire count for next quarterly §19 review: 26 → 27. **POST-DEPLOY required (Wasi):** (1) Fix the existing `DIRECT_URL` env var value on Render dashboard to point at Neon's DIRECT (unpooled) endpoint. (2) Update Render dashboard buildCommand to include the new `node scripts/check-direct-url.js` step between `npm run build` and `npx prisma migrate deploy`. (3) Manual Deploy to apply the v3.8.ajh→ajr pending migrations + verify the guard runs + verify migrate routes through direct endpoint (build log should now show hostname WITHOUT `-pooler`). **Letter:** ajr → ajs sequence-continuous. |

| v3.8.ajr | 2026-05-24 | **Step 3 doc-upload silent-fail fix (W-9 / COI / Authority / Safety now actually reach S3 + carrier documents tab).** Wasi confirmed during smoke test of v3.8.ajq: "When I attempted the test carrier and uploaded the test docs they didn't appear under the pending carrier profile documents tab." Pre-ajr the Step 3 file picker (added v3.8.aiv) staged files with a `__docType` property tag (`w9` / `insurance` / `authority` / `safety`) into `files: File[]` state; `handleSubmit` then attempted a separate `POST /api/carrier/documents` with `Authorization: Bearer ${data.token}` — but the v3.8.ajd login refactor stopped issuing JWTs at registration, so `data.token` was undefined and every doc upload silently 401'd. Required documents enforcement (v3.8.ajb Sprint F) gate-checked at the canNext layer but never verified that the files actually persisted. Net effect: every carrier since v3.8.ajd selected required docs in Step 3, hit Submit, saw success, and their documents vanished to /dev/null. Fixed in v3.8.ajq (which removed the broken upload block) only stopped the silent failure; ajr restores the actual upload path. **Backend changes:** (1) `routes/carrier.ts` `/register` route — `upload.fields([...])` extended with `{ name: "files", maxCount: 10 }` for the Step 3 staged docs. Normalization middleware extended with (a) `docTypes` array normalization mirroring the existing `equipmentTypes` / `operatingRegions` pattern, (b) numeric string → number coercion for 5 fields (`numberOfTrucks`, `autoLiabilityAmount`, `cargoInsuranceAmount`, `generalLiabilityAmount`, `workersCompAmount`) — required because FormData fields are always strings while Zod schema declares `z.number()`, (c) boolean string → boolean coercion for 3 fields (`additionalInsuredSRL`, `waiverOfSubrogation`, `thirtyDayCancellationNotice`). Empty-string scrub for both classes so optional fields pass `z.optional()` cleanly. (2) `carrierController.ts` `registerCarrier` — new block after the existing `photoId` + `articlesOfInc` upload paths. Iterates `req.files.files` paired by index with `req.body.docTypes[]`; `DOC_TYPE_MAP` translates frontend tag (`w9` / `insurance` / `authority` / `safety`) into canonical Document.docType (`W9` / `COI` / `AUTHORITY` / `OTHER` — `SAFETY_CERT` isn't in the Document.docType enum comment at schema.prisma:1945, classified `OTHER` with the type evident in the storage path + filename) and the CarrierProfile boolean flag to flip (`w9Uploaded` / `insuranceCertUploaded` / `authorityDocUploaded`; safety has no flag field). Files land in S3 at `carrier-docs/{profileId}/{tagKey}-{ts}-{rand}{ext}`; Document rows tagged `entityType="CARRIER"`, `entityId=profileId`, `uploadSource="CARRIER_PORTAL"`, `status="PENDING"`. **Frontend changes (`onboarding/page.tsx`):** `handleSubmit` switched from `JSON.stringify` body + `Content-Type: application/json` header to a FormData object. Scalar fields appended as strings (booleans → `"true"` / `"false"`); arrays as repeated keys; files appended as `files` + parallel `docTypes` form-field array (paired by index). Browser auto-sets `Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=...` when body is a FormData instance — explicit Content-Type header REMOVED (would break multer's boundary parsing). **Compatibility note:** backend route was already configured with `upload.fields()` since pre-ajr (photoId + articlesOfInc fields), but the FRONTEND was sending JSON, so multer acted as passthrough (multer only engages on multipart Content-Type). The photoId + articlesOfInc fields were aspirational — frontend never sent them. | ci-hotfix | 2026-05-24 | **CI workflow `DIRECT_URL` env block hotfix — Sub-pattern 11 fire #2 (CI-parity).** v3.8.ajg added `directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")` to `backend/prisma/schema.prisma` and updated both Render dashboard env vars + local `.env`. The third location — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` env blocks — was missed. Backend CI job failed at step `npx prisma validate` (line 30) with `P1012: Environment variable not found: DIRECT_URL`, 24-second failure on the v3.8.ajh push. E2E job skipped (needs: [backend, frontend]). Frontend job unaffected (doesn't touch Prisma). **Reproduced locally:** `unset DIRECT_URL && DATABASE_URL=...localhost... npx prisma validate` → exact same P1012. **Fix:** added `DIRECT_URL: postgresql://ci:ci@localhost:5432/ci` to both the backend job env block (line ~17) and the e2e job env block (line ~82). In CI both URLs point at the same plain Postgres container — no pooler involved so the split semantics don't matter; just need the env var present so `prisma validate` succeeds. **Verification:** `DATABASE_URL=... DIRECT_URL=... npx prisma validate` → "The schema at prisma/schema.prisma is valid 🚀". **Methodology principle (canonical extension banked):** Sub-pattern 11 (CI-parity-verification) — when adding any `env()` reference to `schema.prisma`, the env block must be updated in FOUR locations: (1) local `backend/.env`, (2) Render dashboard env vars, (3) CI workflow env blocks for every job that runs Prisma, (4) CLAUDE.md §2.2 canonical env var list. ajg updated 1, 2, 4; missed 3. Second fire of Sub-pattern 11 in the session arc (first was Sprint 51 `013883d` where local tsc passed but next-lint ESLint failed at CI). Banking the four-location checklist as Sub-pattern 11 extension; pattern fire count for next quarterly §19 review goes from 19 → 20. **Docs-only per §3.1** (CI workflow change doesn't affect deployed user-visible artifacts) — no version bump. **Pre-push verification gate:** local `prisma validate` with CI-shape env vars passed before pushing. | v3.8.ajg | 2026-05-24 | **Prisma + Neon `DIRECT_URL` split — permanent fix for the P1002 advisory-lock contention class (closes §13.3 Item 191).** Ships the canonical Prisma + Neon dual-URL pattern documented by both vendors. **Schema change:** `backend/prisma/schema.prisma` `datasource db { ... }` block adds `directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")` alongside the existing `url = env("DATABASE_URL")` line. Prisma now auto-uses `DIRECT_URL` for ALL migrate operations (`migrate deploy`, `migrate dev`, `migrate status`, `migrate resolve`, `db push`) while runtime queries continue to use `DATABASE_URL` (the pooled connection). **Env vars added on Render dashboard (pre-deploy by Wasi):** `DIRECT_URL` = Neon's direct endpoint connection string (no `-pooler` in hostname; obtained from Neon dashboard → Connect → "Pooled connection" toggle OFF → copy resulting string). `DATABASE_URL` unchanged (stays pooled). `PRISMA_MIGRATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT=60000` recommended as belt-and-suspenders (bumps lock-acquisition timeout from 10s default to 60s). **Why this is the permanent fix:** the advisory lock `pg_advisory_lock(72707369)` is session-scoped — released only when the connection holding it actually closes. Neon's pooled endpoint keeps connections alive between requests and rotates PIDs across the pool, so a migrate process that exits normally still leaves its lock-holder PID cached in the pooler. Lock doesn't release until Neon's idle timer expires that specific cached connection (~5min on Launch tier). The direct endpoint has no pooler caching layer — the connection closes the moment migrate exits, the lock releases instantly, and the next migrate (whenever it fires) acquires the lock cleanly with no contention. Three prior fires (v3.8.ajf push being the most recent) all self-healed via the wait-and-retry pattern; this commit eliminates the class. **CLAUDE.md §2.2 updated** with canonical env var list including `DATABASE_URL` + `DIRECT_URL` + `PRISMA_MIGRATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT` + the local-dev requirement that `backend/.env` mirror the same pair. **Side benefits beyond P1002 elimination:** `prisma migrate status` becomes deterministic (currently it also runs through the pooler and can give stale answers about applied-vs-pending migrations); the Sprint 44b `prisma migrate status` post-deploy verification gate becomes reliable instead of probabilistic; future destructive migrations (enum-swaps like v3.8.ajd, column-drops, table-renames) become safer because the lock is held by a connection that genuinely owns the migration without pooler interference. **No migration in this sprint** — schema change is metadata-only (adding `directUrl` to datasource block changes how Prisma routes connections, not what tables exist). No data write. No `migrate deploy` blocking step beyond the existing Sprint 44b canonical buildCommand. **Pre-commit gates per Sub-pattern 11 (CI parity):** `npx prisma generate` clean (regenerates client with new datasource shape), backend `tsc --noEmit` clean (no code references the datasource directly so no type cascade). **Post-deploy verification:** next migration-bearing deploy should complete in <5s with no P1002 even if a prior deploy was recent. Render build log should still show `prisma migrate deploy` running; the difference is the connection underneath is now direct, not pooled. **Risks considered + rejected (re-stated from Item 191 for permanent record):** `PRISMA_SCHEMA_DISABLE_ADVISORY_LOCK=1` (allows concurrent destructive migrations to corrupt — rejected); pre-deploy `pg_advisory_unlock(72707369)` SQL hook (race condition with legit concurrent migrations — rejected); switching off Neon to another managed Postgres (over-engineering — rejected). **Methodology observation:** Sprint 44b's baseline-reset + canonical buildCommand work hardened the migration history + verification gate but did NOT address the connection-URL split. The class of bug was latent through the entire Sprint 44 → ajf arc; three independent fires in <2 weeks validated the recurrence rate as material enough to justify this architectural fix vs continuing to absorb the manual-retry cost. **Scope:** ~22 LOC net (5 LOC schema datasource block + 9 LOC §2.2 env vars list + 8 LOC §11 row) + 2 env vars on Render dashboard + 1 local `.env` line (Wasi-managed, not in repo). **Patterns applied:** §3.3 atomic single-sprint ship (schema + docs in one commit since the schema change is the load-bearing artifact); §3.5 audit-first (three-fire-validated P1002 pattern banked in §13.3 Item 191 BEFORE shipping the fix); §19 Sub-pattern 11 CI-parity. **Patterns emerged:** none. **Letter:** docs-only P1002 banking commit (`c7db912`) was unversioned per §3.1; ajf was the latest versioned HEAD; ajg sequence-continuous on top. |

| docs-only | 2026-05-24 | **P1002 advisory-lock incident #3 of session arc + permanent-fix sprint plan banked (no code/migration change; docs-only meta per §3.1).** Third P1002 fire in the v3.8.a* range: v3.8.ail (initial occurrence), v3.8.aix (second), and v3.8.ajf push (this incident — Render build log showed `Timed out trying to acquire a postgres advisory lock (SELECT pg_advisory_lock(72707369)). Timeout: 10000ms` after `npx prisma migrate deploy` resolved 9 migrations and got blocked on the hardcoded Prisma lock 72707369). **Pattern characterization (now three-fire-validated):** Prisma's `migrate deploy` acquires a Postgres advisory lock (hardcoded number `72707369` in Prisma source) before applying migrations. Lock is session-scoped — released only when the connection holding it actually closes. Today's `DATABASE_URL` points at Neon's POOLED endpoint (`-pooler` hostname), which intentionally keeps connections alive between requests and rotates PIDs across the pool. Net effect: migrate process exits normally, but its lock-holder connection stays cached in Neon's pooler. Lock doesn't release until Neon's idle timer expires that specific cached connection (~5 min on Launch tier). Every `migrate deploy` thereafter plays roulette against whichever pooler-cached PID is currently holding the lock. P1002 frequency is roughly correlated with migration-bearing deploy frequency. **Resolution pattern (proven on three fires):** wait 5-30 min for Neon idle timeout → Manual Deploy in Render dashboard → migrate deploy acquires lock cleanly, applies pending migrations, deploy succeeds. Self-healing 100% of the time across the three fires; no manual unlock SQL ever needed. The v3.8.aix → aiy retry mechanic (next push auto-retries even if frontend-only) banked as Item 71's "P1002-advisory-lock-retry-via-next-push" methodology observation. **Permanent fix sprint (logged as §13.3 Item 191 — "Prisma + Neon DIRECT_URL split"):** the canonical Prisma + Neon pattern documented by both vendors. Split runtime + migrate connection URLs: `DATABASE_URL` stays on the pooled endpoint (runtime benefits from connection limits); new `DIRECT_URL` env var points at Neon's direct endpoint (no pooler in hostname). Schema's `datasource db` block adds `directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")`; Prisma automatically uses `directUrl` for migrate operations when present. Direct connection releases the advisory lock the moment migrate exits — no pooler caching layer between Prisma and Postgres. ~10 LOC schema change + 2 env var additions (Render dashboard + local `.env`) + 1 CLAUDE.md §2.2 update. **Belt-and-suspenders secondary hardening logged in same sprint:** `PRISMA_MIGRATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT=60000` env var on Render bumps Prisma's lock-acquisition timeout from 10s to 60s, reduces residual P1002 frequency on the direct URL itself. **Risks considered + rejected for the permanent fix:** (a) `PRISMA_SCHEMA_DISABLE_ADVISORY_LOCK=1` — disables the lock entirely; would allow two concurrent migrate processes to apply destructive migrations simultaneously (enum-swap class would corrupt); not recommended. (b) Pre-deploy SQL hook running `pg_advisory_unlock(72707369)` — race condition with legitimate concurrent migrations; not recommended. (c) Switching off Neon to another managed Postgres — over-engineering for this specific class. **Side benefits of the DIRECT_URL split:** `prisma migrate status` becomes deterministic (currently also runs through the pooler and can give stale answers); the Sprint 44b `prisma migrate status --exit-code` post-gate becomes reliable instead of probabilistic; future destructive migrations safer. **Scope:** ~10 LOC + env updates + ~30-60 min execution time (mostly Neon dashboard navigation + Render env editing). **Priority:** elevated for after the v3.8.ajf P1002 self-heals + the three pending migrations apply — every future schema migration is at risk of P1002 until this lands. Pairs naturally with §13.3 Item 8.10's deploy-chain hardening lineage (Sprint 44a → 44b → 44c → 44d). |

PENDING / REVIEWING / INFO_REQUESTED / REJECTED all let the carrier through to JWT issuance. Per-route APPROVED checks at backend (`carrierLoads.ts:31/169`, etc.) defend against a stale-tab carrier hitting load endpoints; defense-in-depth holds. **New endpoint:** `GET /api/carrier-auth/application-status` returns header context (companyName / mcNumber / dotNumber), onboardingStatus, submittedAt, approvedAt. Shape designed stable so v3.8.aje can extend with `infoRequests[]` + `rejectionReason` + `reapplyEligibleAt` without contract churn. **Carrier dashboard layout (`carrier/dashboard/layout.tsx`):** status-based routing — non-APPROVED carriers redirected to `/carrier/dashboard/application-status`; APPROVED carriers redirected OFF the status page back to the main dashboard. Sidebar + search bar + notifications bell + Marco Polo AI all hidden for non-APPROVED carriers (the only accessible route is the status page; no navigation needed). Notifications query `enabled` flag gated to APPROVED — saves the 2-minute polling cycle. **New page `frontend/src/app/carrier/dashboard/application-status/page.tsx`:** state-specific render. Header card shows companyName + MC# + DOT# + status pill (brand-canonical status palette: PENDING/INFO_REQUESTED warning amber, REVIEWING info navy-100, APPROVED success, REJECTED/SUSPENDED danger). Body section renders per-state content — PENDING ("Your application is in the queue" + 3-step "what happens next" ladder), REVIEWING ("A reviewer is on your application" + reassurance copy), INFO_REQUESTED (defensive copy pointing carriers to email/compliance@; v3.8.aje wires the actual InfoRequest list + resolve form here), REJECTED (defensive copy; v3.8.aje wires reason + reapply date), APPROVED (defensive — carrier should be redirecting off this page anyway). Footer compliance contact card always rendered. 60s `refetchInterval` so status flips surface without page reload. **AE Console updates:** `STATUS_COLORS` palette on `/dashboard/carriers` extended to the new 6 states (REVIEWING navy-100, INFO_REQUESTED amber, SUSPENDED gray); tab-filter dropdown updated to enumerate the new 6 states; Zod validator on the AE update endpoint (`routes/carriers.ts:49`) updated to the new enum; cron filter on `cron/index.ts:349` (identity-validation for pending carriers) updated from `["PENDING","UNDER_REVIEW","DOCUMENTS_SUBMITTED"]` → `["PENDING","REVIEWING"]` (INFO_REQUESTED carriers are mid-conversation, identity already validated). One stale literal at `routes/carriers.ts:468` (`UNDER_REVIEW` → `REVIEWING`) caught by backend tsc enum check post-Prisma-generate. **Scope:** ~280 LOC net across 8 files (schema + migration + carrierAuth + cron + carriers.ts validator + AE carriers page + carrier dashboard layout + new application-status page) + 1 Prisma migration. **Pre-commit gates per Sub-pattern 11 (CI parity):** `npx prisma generate` clean, backend `tsc --noEmit` clean (1 stale literal caught + fixed), frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npx next build` clean (`/carrier/dashboard/application-status` 5.58 kB prerendered static). **Banked for v3.8.aje (next sprint):** `InfoRequest` Prisma model + AE create endpoint + carrier view/resolve endpoint + AE Console "Request Info" UI with industry-standard templates + carrier-facing resolve UI on the status page; `CarrierProfile.rejectionReason` + `rejectedAt` + `rejectedById` + `reapplyEligibleAt` schema fields + per-reason reapply windows + REJECTED state UI on status page. ### §11 — Architectural finding (cross-cutting, surfaced during v3.8.d sprint, 2026-04-28)

`sanitizeInput` middleware at `backend/src/middleware/security.ts` (registered at `server.ts:150`) was HTML-escaping all `req.body` string values at write time, causing values to be stored encoded in the database (e.g., `equipmentType: 'Dry Van 53&#x27;'` instead of `'Dry Van 53''`). Every human-facing read path required compensating decode logic at the output boundary. Worse, repeated re-saves through the same middleware would multi-encode (`&amp;#x27;`, `&amp;amp;#x27;`, etc.) which one-pass decoders couldn't fully reverse.

**Tactical fix at v3.8.d:** scoped `decodeHtmlEntities` at `/tracking` public serializer; PDFKit's `safe()` already handled PDF rendering.

**Architectural fix at v3.8.d.2:** middleware rewritten to do proper INPUT hygiene only — trim, length-cap, null-byte strip — without OUTPUT encoding. Output-layer escaping moved to where it belongs:
- HTML rendering → React's automatic JSX escaping
- PDF rendering → PDFKit's `safe()` decode at the boundary
- JSON APIs → JSON-encoding handles its own char-set; no HTML escaping needed

**Pattern for new surfaces:** any new customer-facing surface that reads from the database must NOT assume strings are clean if any pre-v3.8.d.2 data may be present. Use `decodeHtmlEntities` defensively until a full data audit confirms clean. v3.8.d.2 included a one-time decode script at `backend/scripts/decode-encoded-load-fields.ts` (idempotent, multi-pass-safe per v3.8.d.3 update) for cleanup of legacy encoded data.

**Lesson for future architectural decisions:** input-time HTML escaping is double-escape on output anyway (templating engines auto-escape). Defense-in-depth is good; doing the same defense twice in different layers is corruption.

Authoritative source = full classification of every match, not raw match count.

8.6. **Carrier preference manual override admin UI — `PUT /ai/preferences/:carrierId`.** Surfaced 2026-05-02 from `audit-completeness.ts` Phase A verification. Backend endpoint at [`backend/src/routes/ai.ts:335`](backend/src/routes/ai.ts#L335) is the manual override path for carrier preferences (operations correcting an auto-learned preference, e.g., "carrier won't take refrigerated despite history" or seeding initial preferences before the auto-learner has data). Originally triaged Tier C on the assumption that an admin tool fired it. Phase A grep returned zero callers. Critically, the auto-learner at [`carrierPreferenceService.ts:188`](backend/src/services/carrierPreferenceService.ts#L188) writes Prisma directly and bypasses the HTTP endpoint entirely — so the endpoint is purely the manual-override path, not the auto-write path, which is exactly why it has zero auto-callers AND zero UI callers. Reclassified Tier A. Sprint shape: small admin-only panel under `/admin/*` (or carrier detail view) exposing the writable preference fields (preferred lanes, equipment types, blackout regions, etc.) with a "Save manual override" action calling the existing endpoint. Must NOT touch the auto-learner — manual override should override auto-learned values, with timestamp/actor audit-log entry per change. ~80-120 lines, single sprint.

8.7. **Manual tag-management UI — `POST` + `DELETE /tags/assign`.** Surfaced 2026-05-02 from `audit-completeness.ts` Phase A verification. Backend endpoint pair at [`backend/src/routes/tags.ts:44,49`](backend/src/routes/tags.ts#L44) calls into [`tagService.ts`](backend/src/services/tagService.ts) — `assignTag()` at line 33 and `removeTagAssignment()` at line 41. Originally triaged Tier C on the assumption that some internal caller exercised the HTTP path. Phase A verification: HTTP endpoints have zero frontend callers; HOWEVER `assignTag()` IS called internally at [`tagService.ts:80`](backend/src/services/tagService.ts#L80) by the `autoTagEntity` rule engine via an apply-all path — so the underlying service functions are alive even though the HTTP endpoint pair is dead from a UI perspective. Decision locked (Option A): keep both endpoints AND build the missing manual tag-management UI. Rationale: the auto-tagger is a rules engine; manual override (add a tag the rules missed, remove a tag the rules misfired on) is a load-bearing operations capability. Sprint shape: small tag-management panel surfaced wherever tag-bearing entities render (load detail, customer detail, carrier detail) with "Add tag" + "Remove" actions; POST hits `/tags/assign`, DELETE hits `/tags/assign`. **Critical:** do NOT remove `assignTag()` or `removeTagAssignment()` service functions even if the HTTP endpoints stay dormant — the auto-tag rule engine depends on them. ~80-120 lines, single sprint across one shared component.

**Triage correction note (2026-05-02).** The initial Tier S/A/B/C/D bucketing of the 27 orphan endpoints surfaced by [`backend/scripts/audit-completeness.ts`](backend/scripts/audit-completeness.ts) classified four endpoints as Tier C ("internal-only fired, no UI needed") on the hypothesis that they had non-frontend callers somewhere in the codebase. Phase A read-only verification falsified that hypothesis for all four: `PATCH /address-book/:id/use` (Item 8.5 above), `PATCH /shipments/:id/location` (covered by existing Phase 5E.c Decision 4.1, no new entry), `PUT /ai/preferences/:carrierId` (Item 8.6 above), and `POST` + `DELETE /tags/assign` (Item 8.7 above) all returned zero callers across `backend/src/` and `frontend/src/`. The endpoints are dormant, not internally-fired. Reclassified to Tier A. Total orphan count remains 27 (no audit suppression comments applied). Lesson recorded for future `audit-completeness.ts` runs: "no caller found" is a triage signal, not an auto-classification — every finding requires human verification of caller intent before bucketing. The two service functions in tagService.ts (`assignTag`, `removeTagAssignment`) must NOT be removed as part of any future cleanup — `autoTagEntity` depends on them.

8.10. ~~**Backfill prisma/migrations file for ProspectVertical schema change + investigate Render deploy-chain.**~~ **CLOSED 2026-05-09 in v3.8.aax** (Sprint 44b atomic close). Sprint 44a Track 1 + Track 2 audit caught actual drift scope was **81 of 87 prod enums** plus their corresponding tables/columns — far beyond the original Item 8.10 ProspectVertical-only scope. v3.8.aa-dd (Apr 24 → May 4 window) shipped schema work via manual `prisma db push` to Neon, bypassing migration history entirely. Compounding root cause: Render Build Command lacked `prisma migrate deploy` step entirely, so the v3.8.ee `add_customer_approval_fields` migration that was authored + committed never applied via the deploy chain. **Fix shape (Sprint 44b atomic):** P1 — Render Build Command updated to canonical `npm install && npm run build && npx prisma migrate deploy && npx prisma migrate status --exit-code && cp -r src/assets dist/backend/src/assets`. P2 — baseline reset: `_prisma_migrations` ledger cleared on Neon, single `20260509170000_baseline_init` migration generated from `prisma migrate diff --from-empty --to-schema-datamodel` (3,652 lines, 87 enums, 120 tables) captures complete prod schema state, marked applied via `prisma migrate resolve --applied`. Prior 15 migrations archived to `backend/prisma/_archived_migrations_2026-05-09/` for posterity (NOT part of active chain). P3 — `prisma migrate status --exit-code` post-deploy gate fails build on any pending migrations (silent-skip class catch). P4 — single canonical schema mutation path doc at CLAUDE.md §2.2 + render.yaml + ci.yml comment all aligned in this commit (Pattern 6 spatial sub-mode contradiction resolved). PITR upgraded to 7 days (Neon Launch tier) before Phase 2 baseline reset for safety. **Sprint 44a Track 1 lesson:** initial grep on `ProspectVertical` returned correct empty result, but the conclusion "this is the only drift" was wrong — full audit needed direct `pg_type` + `information_schema` query (CSV of 87 enums) to surface complete scope. Pattern 6 sub-rule c candidate: "audits can be wrong" / verify prod-touching action against authoritative source before acting (queued for Sprint 44.5 §19 update). Original entry preserved below for history. **v3.8.alg lineage closure annotation (2026-05-27):** the full deploy-chain investigation arc — 8.10 (Sprint 44b baseline reset + canonical buildCommand) → Item 191 (Prisma + Neon DIRECT_URL split, v3.8.ajg/ajs) → v3.8.ale (citext migration via $executeRawUnsafe bypass surfaced ledger-drift class) → v3.8.alf (ledger reconciliation via `prisma migrate resolve --applied` + render.yaml docs gap closure) — is now **empirically validated** via the v3.8.alf Render build log. Three independent lines of evidence: (1) `check-direct-url.js` guard (v3.8.ajs canonical) fired correctly + reported `✓ DIRECT_URL configured correctly (hostname: ep-green-frog-ajsgv9me.c-3.us-east-2.aws.neon.tech, no -pooler)` — confirms Render dashboard env var matches §2.2 canonical; (2) `prisma migrate deploy` reported `21 migrations found in prisma/migrations / No pending migrations to apply.` — proves the v3.8.alf ledger-resolve landed on prod's `_prisma_migrations` table end-to-end (Prisma sees the citext migration as applied; no SQL re-run; no P1002); (3) `prisma migrate status` Sprint 44b post-deploy gate reported `Database schema is up to date!` — verifies clean state after deploy. Net lineage outcome: a class of bug (silent migration drift between application schema state + deployed DB state) that surfaced repeatedly in v3.8.aa-ee + v3.8.ajf and required 5 architectural sprints to fully contain (44a/44b/ajg/ajs/alf) now has structural defenses sufficient that the next incident requires either (a) a NEW failure mode not covered by existing guards, OR (b) deliberate guard removal/circumvention. Banking lineage status as CLOSED-AND-EMPIRICALLY-VALIDATED.

8.10-original. **Backfill prisma/migrations file for ProspectVertical schema change + investigate Render deploy-chain.** Surfaced 2026-05-04 during v3.8.v–v3.8.cc Lead Hunter sprint Step 4 verification. v3.8.aa (C4 commit [`6e2e6d9`](commit/6e2e6d9)) applied the `ProspectVertical` enum + `Customer.vertical` column via `prisma db push` directly to Neon. No migration file exists in [`backend/prisma/migrations/`](backend/prisma/migrations/). Production currently works because the live Neon DB matches the regenerated Prisma client — but a fresh DB clone (staging branch, dev workstation reset, disaster-recovery rebuild) will not pick up the enum + column from `migrate deploy` because there is no migration file to apply. **Risk profile: recovery-time gap, not runtime.** The Render `buildCommand` runs `npx prisma migrate deploy` on every deploy, which will be a no-op for this change because Neon already has it; the runtime `@prisma/client` is regenerated from the schema file and matches. Failure mode is invisible until someone resets a database from migrations alone, at which point the new enum + column will be missing and the type-system promise the client exports will diverge from the live schema. **Fix shape:** generate the missing migration file from the current schema diff using `npx prisma migrate diff --from-empty --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --script` (or against a baseline that excludes only the C4 change), place the resulting SQL in `backend/prisma/migrations/<timestamp>_add_prospect_vertical/migration.sql`, commit docs-only. **Test:** clone Neon to a staging branch, run `npx prisma migrate deploy` against it from scratch, confirm `ProspectVertical` enum exists and `customers.vertical` column exists with default `UNKNOWN`. Render's next prod build should be a no-op because Neon already has the schema. **Pairs with Items 8.6/8.7 audit hygiene** — both are recovery-time-gap issues that don't surface until you actually need to recover. Effort: small (~15-30 min including staging-clone test). Tracked here so the gap is closed in a dedicated mini-sprint, not silently absorbed. **Future-proofing:** the broader CLAUDE.md §2 directive to "avoid `prisma migrate dev`" because migration history has drift is itself a long-term risk; consolidating to a single baseline migration + going-forward migrate-deploy discipline is a separate architectural sprint outside Item 8.10's scope.

**Scope expansion 2026-05-05** — Item 8.10 was originally scoped to the v3.8.aa `db push` recovery-time gap (the `ProspectVertical` migration that was never authored). A separate but materially worse case surfaced during v3.8.oo verification: the Phase 3 (v3.8.ee, commit [`2fb5279`](commit/2fb5279), 2026-05-04) migration `20260504000000_add_customer_approval_fields` WAS authored, WAS committed, AND was NEVER applied to prod across ~24h and 9+ subsequent deploys (v3.8.ff through v3.8.oo). Track 1 diagnostic on 2026-05-05 confirmed: Query A returned zero rows for `customers.approved_at` + `customers.approved_by_id`; Query B returned zero rows in `_prisma_migrations` for any matching ledger entry. Manual `prisma migrate deploy` from local at 2026-05-05 17:35:00 UTC applied the migration cleanly in one step (post-DATABASE_URL-parity confirmation by Wasi + a Neon password rotation propagated to both Render env and local `.env`), demonstrating the migration itself was correct — failure was somewhere in Render's deploy chain. **Root-cause candidates to investigate (Phase 6 sprint):** (1) Render dashboard `buildCommand` drift from CLAUDE.md §2.2's documented spec — the dashboard is the SOT per §2.2 and `render.yaml` is cosmetic-only, so a manual edit could have weakened the chain; this is the most likely cause given §2.2 explicitly warns about this drift class. (2) `prisma migrate deploy` silently skipping or absent from the actual dashboard `buildCommand` (e.g. someone removed the `&& npx prisma migrate deploy` segment to work around an unrelated transient error and never restored it). (3) Build artifact cache holding a stale Prisma client that doesn't request the new columns at runtime, masking the drift until a query that actually needs the columns finally hits it. (4) Deploy chain runs migrate deploy but with a DATABASE_URL pointing at a different database than the runtime backend reads — would explain silent green builds with absent prod migrations; somewhat ruled out by the 2026-05-05 parity confirmation but worth a dashboard verification. **Fix surface:** (a) capture current dashboard `buildCommand` value as evidence, then re-align it with the documented value at CLAUDE.md §2.2 verbatim; (b) add a post-deploy schema-verify check that fails the build if `prisma migrate status` reports any pending migrations after `migrate deploy` ran (treats silent-skip as an explicit deploy failure rather than a transparent miss); (c) optional: periodic migration-drift cron (weekly) running `prisma migrate status` against prod and alerting `compliance@` on any pending migrations — captures drift even if it slips past a future deploy. **Effort:** medium sprint. Investigation step is ~30-60 min in Render dashboard + Render build log review for v3.8.oo's deploy. Fix steps are small but blocked on diagnosis. **Priority:** elevated — every future schema migration is at risk until this is closed. Pairs with the v3.8.aa migration backfill from the original Item 8.10 scope; both should land in the same sprint.

42. ~~**RC Modal Generate PDF + Send Tender buttons fail silently — quickPayFeePercent string-vs-number type mismatch.**~~ **CLOSED 2026-05-06 in v3.8.aam** (Sprint 34). Path β methodology cycle complete (Sprints 32 → 33 → 34) for the RC modal silent-fail class. **Cycle summary:** Sprint 32 (v3.8.aak) shipped error UI surfacing on all 3 RC handlers — silent error swallow class closed at observability layer. Sprint 33 (v3.8.aal) widened extractor to iterate Zod `details[]` array — generic "Validation error" banner became field-specific "Validation error — formData.X: <message>". Sprint 34 (v3.8.aam) shipped the targeted field fix once Sprint 33's extractor surfaced the specific rejection: `formData.quickPayFeePercent: Expected number, received string`. **Root cause:** [`RateConfirmationModal.tsx:188`](frontend/src/components/loads/RateConfirmationModal.tsx#L188) declares `quickPayFeePercent: string` in FormState (input ergonomics — three write paths all stringify via `String(...)`); backend Zod schema at [`validators/rateConfirmation.ts:117`](backend/src/validators/rateConfirmation.ts#L117) declares `z.number().optional()`. [`buildPayload()`](frontend/src/components/loads/RateConfirmationModal.tsx) spread `...form` carried the string unchanged — other numeric fields had explicit `parseFloat`/`parseInt`/`toNum` coercion before send, this one was the lone gap. **Fix shape — Path X1 (surgical buildPayload coercion):** added 3-line explicit coercion `quickPayFeePercent: form.quickPayFeePercent !== "" ? Number(form.quickPayFeePercent) : undefined`. **`!== ""` check preserves null-vs-zero distinction** (Phase A audit caught this): empty input → undefined → DB null (no value); explicit `"0"` → `Number(0)` = 0 → DB 0 (legitimate "no fee" STANDARD tier selection); `"1.5"` → 1.5 (correct). Alternative `Number(...) || undefined` rejected — would silently mask "0" as undefined, breaking STANDARD tier no-fee semantics. **Path X3 (`z.coerce.number()` validator change) rejected** per Phase A — changes validator semantics across schema, risks empty-string-to-zero confusion on other fields, belongs in §13.3 Item A28-2 architectural sprint. **Sweep result:** only `quickPayFeePercent` affected — single-field issue, not bug class. Other 10 `z.number()` validator fields are either explicitly coerced in buildPayload or not in payload at all. **Path β methodology validation:** ~38 LOC total across 3 atomic commits to retire 3 silently-broken handlers. Zero speculation, zero regressions. Error UI + widened extractor remain as PERMANENT diagnostic infrastructure for any future RC handler API failures. Pattern propagation candidate for other modals/forms across the codebase. **Item 45 logged (separate)** for follow-up cleanup of unvalidated payload fields. **Item A28-2 elevated** — today's cycle demonstrates the cost of "validator strict, frontend payload promiscuous" pattern; A28-2 architectural sprint (validator hardening via `z.preprocess` shape coercion at validator boundary) would prevent this class entirely; worth post-BKN priority bump from deferred queue. **Pre-commit verification:** backend `tsc --noEmit` clean (no backend changes), frontend `next build` clean. Net source change: 3 LOC (smallest hotfix shape). Per §3.1: v3.8.aal → v3.8.aam.

71. ~~**`(npx tsc || true)` suppresses TypeScript errors in build chain.**~~ **LOGGED + CLOSED 2026-05-10 in v3.8.abe** (Sprint 46). Root cause hypothesis from Sprint 44b Phase 3 was partially correct (the `|| true` did mask tsc errors) but Phase A audit at Sprint 46 revealed the deeper architectural cause: Render's env-level `NODE_ENV=production` (set in `render.yaml:34`) makes `npm install` skip the `devDependencies` block, leaving 12 declared `@types/*` packages uninstalled at build time. `Request` from `express` then resolves to `any`, `AuthRequest extends Request<any,any,any,any>` cascades, and tsc emits ~1,100 errors silenced by the `\|\| true`. Local CI uses `npm ci` (installs both deps + devDeps regardless of `NODE_ENV`) so CI tsc is clean — only Render diverged. **Empirical reproduction (Sprint 46 Phase B0 local sub-rule c gate):** `cd backend && rm -rf node_modules && NODE_ENV=production npm install && npm run build` produced exit code 0 with **1,398 error lines** (149 TS7016 + 907 TS2339 AuthRequest cascade + 63 TS7006 implicit any + 3 TS2503 Express namespace not found). Exact match to Sprint 45-RC Render build log. **Fix (3 changes, atomic):** (a) drop `\|\| true` from `backend/package.json:7` build script — strict tsc; (b) add `optionalDependencies` block with `@aws-sdk/client-rekognition ^3.1045.0` (Item 95, since we're touching package.json — biometricVerificationService.ts:9 has a try/catch dynamic require and was relying on the runtime-fail-graceful path); (c) add `NODE_ENV=development` prefix to Render dashboard buildCommand's `npm install` step — install-time only, runtime `NODE_ENV=production` preserved via render.yaml env block. **Architectural win:** build chain converted from fail-silent to fail-fast — tsc error → build halts → cp steps don't execute → deploy fails visibly. Sprint 45-RC's compass placeholder + Sprint 44b email signature fallback both shipped under fail-silent regime; Sprint 46 makes the next class of these visible in build logs immediately. **Sub-rule c lineage extends to 12 fires** in cumulative session arc (Sprint 46 audit-then-Phase-B0-gate counts as fire #11; fire #12 is the post-fix verification that landed clean). Per §3.1: v3.8.abd → v3.8.abe. **Items 95 + 96 closed alongside.**

95. ~~**`@aws-sdk/client-rekognition` referenced via dynamic require but not declared in package.json.**~~ **LOGGED + CLOSED 2026-05-10 in v3.8.abe** (Sprint 46 bundled with Item 71). [`backend/src/services/biometricVerificationService.ts:5-17`](backend/src/services/biometricVerificationService.ts#L5) wraps `require("@aws-sdk/client-rekognition")` in a try/catch gated by `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` env. The runtime warning `[Biometric] AWS Rekognition SDK not available, using hash-based verification` is the intentional fallback path. But the module was referenced without being declared anywhere in `package.json` (not in `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, or `optionalDependencies`) — meaning even if `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` were set, the require would still fail because npm never installed the package. Sprint 46 added `optionalDependencies` block: `{ "@aws-sdk/client-rekognition": "^3.1045.0" }`. Aligns with sibling `@aws-sdk/client-s3 ^3.998.0` major version. npm will try to install but won't fail if not available (graceful degradation matches the try/catch shape). When Wasi enables AWS biometric verification (set `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` env), Rekognition path will actually be reachable. **Surfaced during Sprint 46 Phase A4 audit** — we were already touching package.json, so bundled atomically per §3.3.

99. ~~**`cp -r` POSIX nesting bug + sub-rule c gate extension (file-landed-at-expected-path verification).**~~ **LOGGED + CLOSED 2026-05-16 in v3.8.abf** (Sprint 47 atomic Item 99). Linux/POSIX `cp -r SRC DEST` semantics: when DEST already exists as a directory, SRC is copied as a CHILD of DEST → result `DEST/SRC_NAME/files...`. Only when DEST does not exist does cp create it with SRC's contents flat. `tsc` creates `dist/backend/src/{lib,config,assets}/` directories first (emitting compiled `.js` files into them), so by the time the buildCommand's cp steps run, all three destinations pre-exist → nesting fires silently. **Two retroactive production regressions explained:** (a) Sprint 44b Item 72 logged + closed `cp -r src/config dist/backend/src/config` step, but the file actually landed at `dist/backend/src/config/config/signatures/whaider.html` (nested). [`email/builder.ts:18`](backend/src/email/builder.ts#L18) reading `dist/backend/src/config/signatures/whaider.html` got "file not found" warning on every cold start since Sprint 44b. (b) Sprint 45-RC compass mark PNGs went to `dist/backend/src/lib/lib/srl_compass_*.png` (nested). Runtime `LOGO_DIR = __dirname` resolved to `dist/backend/src/lib/`, `resolveCompassPng()` returned null, placeholder navy ring fired on every Rate Confirmation PDF. Same single bug class, two visible failures. **Fix:** trailing-dot form `cp -r SRC/. DEST/` always copies CONTENTS regardless of whether DEST exists. Applied to all 3 cp commands in render.yaml + CLAUDE.md §2.2. **Empirical verification (Sprint 47 Phase B0 sub-rule c gate):** reproduced nesting locally + verified trailing-dot fix produces flat paths before commit. **Methodology principle banked (Item 99):** for file-producing build operations, "command exited 0" is necessary but NOT sufficient verification — must also verify file landed at expected runtime path. Sprint 44b Item 72 closure was technically incorrect: the cp command did run with exit 0, but the runtime path was never checked; the failure was invisible until Sprint 45-RC compass placeholder surfaced it 6+ days later. Sub-rule c gate extends: command-success verification + file-path verification. Pattern 6 sub-rule c fire #13 banks the extended gate for future build-chain sprints.

105. ~~**Pattern 6 sub-rule c — "deferred-but-not-missed" protocol canonical (named sub-pattern).**~~ **LOGGED + CLOSED 2026-05-16 in v3.8.abg** (Sprint 47.b methodology meta-finding). Sprint 47's commit message explicitly documented the deferred ligature risk verbatim: *"Ligature suppression — Sprint v3.8.b Option β monkey-patch... if RC PDF renders italic Playfair with ligature artifacts post-Sprint-47, same monkey-patch approach migrates into srl-chrome.ts as a separate hotfix; deferred unless surfaces visually."* When the risk surfaced via Wasi's visual verification of the post-Sprint-47 RC PDF, Sprint 47.b activated exactly per that documented plan — single-day turnaround from surface → atomic fix → push. **This is NOT a sub-rule c miss.** Sprint 47 didn't have the data to know the ligature would visibly surface (could have been correctly rendered by Playfair's specific `fi` glyph; fontkit ligature behavior varies by font's OpenType tables). Documenting the deferred risk as a known-conditional follow-up sprint, with explicit activation criteria, is the gate's INTENDED deferral protocol. Sub-rule c fire count holds at 13 — deferred-but-not-missed is a sub-pattern, not a fire. **Methodology principle banked:** when a sprint identifies a downstream risk it can't empirically validate at commit time (e.g., visual rendering that needs production-equivalent deployment), document the risk + activation criteria + planned hotfix path in the commit message. Future sprints have a clear handoff if the risk materializes. The protocol works as designed when (a) Sprint N flags the risk explicitly, (b) Sprint N+1 activates immediately when verification surfaces it. §19 quarterly meta-commit candidate alongside Item 96 (fail-fast vs fail-silent) and Item 99 (runtime-path verification gate extension). Sub-rule c now has THREE named methodology principles: authoritative-source-verification (canonical), fail-fast-build-chain (Item 96), runtime-path-verification (Item 99), AND deferred-but-not-missed (Item 105). All four are §19 case studies for next quarterly review.

102. ~~**`drawPartiesBlock` y-coordinate overlap with meta strip date row.**~~ **LOGGED + CLOSED 2026-05-16 in v3.8.abf** (Sprint 47 atomic Item 102). Sprint 45-RC PDF rendered "May 16, 2026PARTIES" as visible overlap on page 1 — the meta strip's DATE value row collided with the `drawPartiesBlock` PARTIES small-caps label sitting `y - 14` above the panels. Root cause: in [`pdfService.ts:1414`](backend/src/services/pdfService.ts#L1414) the RC generator called `drawPartiesBlock(..., y - 4)`; `drawMetaStrip` returns y at meta strip's bottom edge, and `drawPartiesBlock` internally subtracts 14 from the passed `yTop` to position its PARTIES label, so the effective label y was `metaStripBottom - 4 - 14 = metaStripBottom - 18`, which fell INSIDE the meta strip's value row. **Fix:** bumped y-offset from `y - 4` to `y + 12` — gives the parties label clearance from the meta strip row above. Visually verified via local rebuild + Wasi pixel verification on Phase 4 post-deploy.

96. ~~**Architectural lesson — build chain fail-fast vs fail-silent as canonical methodology principle.**~~ **LOGGED + CLOSED 2026-05-10 in v3.8.abe** (Sprint 46 meta-finding). Pre-Sprint-46 backend build chain: `npm install (NODE_ENV=production skips devDeps) → (npx tsc \|\| true) (mask errors) → cp -r src/assets/config/lib (succeeds unconditionally) → prisma migrate deploy → deploy succeeds with broken artifacts`. Net effect: TWO classes of regression silently shipped to production over the past sprint arc — (1) Sprint 44b email signature template `dist/backend/src/config/signatures/whaider.html` missing (caught by Sprint 44b Item 72 pre-commit grep audit, fixed by adding `cp -r src/config` step — but the underlying fail-silent build chain wasn't addressed); (2) Sprint 45-RC compass mark PNGs `dist/backend/src/lib/srl_compass_*.png` missing despite buildCommand including `cp -r src/lib` step — the cp didn't fail, the `tsc` step "passed" (via `\|\| true`), so the deploy went through with broken assets; user saw placeholder navy ring instead of canonical SRL compass mark. **Post-Sprint-46 build chain is fail-fast:** tsc errors → npm run build exits non-zero → cp steps don't run → deploy halts with visible failure. Future Sprint-44b/45-RC class regressions become impossible at the architectural level rather than requiring per-incident pre-commit grep audits. **Methodology principle:** silent-success is worse than loud-failure on prod deploy chains because (a) silent-success normalizes ignoring the build log noise, (b) the failure mode propagates to runtime where it's harder to diagnose, (c) eventually shipping a "live" service that's missing assets damages user trust. Banking for §19 quarterly meta-commit as canonical methodology principle. **Item 96 LOG + CLOSE** — the principle is now documented at CLAUDE.md §2.2 + permanently embedded in the post-Sprint-46 build chain itself.

93. **Pattern 6 sub-rule c — pixel-verification-as-audit-gate observation.** Surfaced 2026-05-10 during Sprint 45-RC Phase A2 PDF capture. Phase A Track 1 audit produced 7 RC PDF findings via code-side analysis (read pdfService.ts, compared against skill canonical, traced data shapes). Phase A2 pixel verification (open the PDF, look at it) surfaced an 8th finding the code audit predicted nothing about: rate breakdown rendered to page 4 instead of page 1. The cause was `checkPageBreak` thresholds + section-ordering interaction that produced visible-but-non-obvious pagination behavior — invisible from grepping section names; visible only when looking at the rendered output. **Methodology lesson:** code-side audits are authoritative for code contracts (function signatures, type shapes, control flow) but NOT for visual contracts (which-page-does-X-render-on, what-does-the-rendered-pixel-density-feel-like, where-does-an-AE-eye-fall-first). Visual audits require visual capture — there's no shortcut via grep, AST parsing, or static type inspection. Code-side audit answers "what could it render?"; pixel verification answers "what does it render?". The two are complementary, not substitutable. **Sprint shape:** docs-only meta-commit candidate at next quarterly §19 review. Add to §19 Pattern 6 sub-rule c body as a NEW sub-class — pixel-verification-as-audit-gate distinct from authoritative-source-verification. Lineage: cumulative arc sub-rule c fire count post-Sprint-45-RC = 9, with Phase A2 (this finding) + Phase B Sub-phase 3 (package.json directive correction) being fires 8 + 9. **Item 93 LOG OPEN** — closure deferred until quarterly §19 review or Sprint 44.5-style methodology meta-commit appends the case-study addendum.

45. **RC Modal payload spread includes fields not declared in validator (`totalCarrierPay`, `netPayAmount`).** Surfaced 2026-05-06 during Sprint 34 Phase A. [`RateConfirmationModal.tsx`](frontend/src/components/loads/RateConfirmationModal.tsx) `buildPayload()` does `...form` spread which includes `totalCarrierPay` (FormState line 184) and `netPayAmount` (line 189). Backend validator [`createRateConfirmationSchema`](backend/src/validators/rateConfirmation.ts) does NOT declare these fields. Zod's default behavior is `.strip()` — unknown keys are silently dropped from the parsed output without raising validation errors. **No current bug** — fields are silently discarded server-side. **Cleanup options:** (a) remove from `...form` spread by reshaping payload to explicitly-listed fields only; (b) add the two fields to the validator schema if useful for backend (e.g., for analytics/audit); (c) change validator to `.strict()` to fail-loud on unknown keys. **Sprint shape:** small (~5 LOC) but architectural decision — option (a) is cleanest for forward compatibility, option (c) catches future drift but requires payload audit across all RC consumers. **NOT in Sprint 34 scope** per §3.3 atomic-commit rule — Sprint 34 stayed atomic on Item 42 closure. **Priority:** low. No load is currently broken. Pairs naturally with §13.3 Item A28-2 (validator hardening) post-BKN.

39. ~~**RC Modal carrier search returns 404 silent-fail (B28-T1.3-A re-diagnosed).**~~ **CLOSED 2026-05-06 in v3.8.aaj** (Sprint 31). Originally walked as "P1 missing empty state on carrier search." Phase A audit corrected the diagnosis — the empty state was never the bug. Root cause: [`RateConfirmationModal.tsx:1422`](frontend/src/components/loads/RateConfirmationModal.tsx#L1422) (pre-fix) called `api.get("/carriers/all", ...)` but the canonical handler `getAllCarriers` is mounted at `/api/carrier/all` (singular) per [`backend/src/routes/carrier.ts:123`](backend/src/routes/carrier.ts#L123), NOT `/api/carriers/all` (plural). The plural route file defines `GET /` (with validation) and `GET /:id`, so Express matched `/api/carriers/all` against the `/:id` route with `req.params.id = "all"`, called `getCarrierDetail("all")` → returned 404. Frontend `useQuery` silently swallowed the 404, `data` stayed undefined, dropdown render gated on `showSearch && carriers && (...)` never fired — AE saw silent dead-state (input typed, no dropdown, no error, no autofill). **Re-diagnosis pattern matches Sprint 26 → 26b** (accessorial walk surfaced symptom, audit identified actual root cause): walk surfaces what user sees, audit identifies real bug class, correct fix ships. Memory #11 firing again. **Fix:** 1-character change — removed `s` from `carriers/all`. New URL `/carrier/all` now resolves to the actual `getAllCarriers` handler. Inline comment added at the call site referencing Sprint 31 + Item 40 (the duplicate-route consolidation backlog). **Pre-commit verification:** backend `tsc --noEmit` clean (no backend changes), frontend `next build` clean. Net LOC change: ~7 (1 URL char swap + 6-line inline comment). Per §3.1: v3.8.aai → v3.8.aaj.

40. **Duplicate carrier-route definitions: `routes/carrier.ts` (singular) vs `routes/carriers.ts` (plural).** Surfaced 2026-05-06 during Sprint 31 Phase A audit. Two backend files define routes for the same `getAllCarriers` controller at different URL paths with different validation: [`backend/src/routes/carrier.ts:123`](backend/src/routes/carrier.ts#L123) `GET /all` (NO validation, accepts arbitrary query params); [`backend/src/routes/carriers.ts:102`](backend/src/routes/carriers.ts#L102) `GET /` (WITH `validateQuery(carrierQuerySchema)`). Both call the same controller. Result: validation drift between `/api/carrier/all?search=X` (anything goes) and `/api/carriers?search=X` (must match Zod schema). Multiple frontend callers may hit either path. The plural route also defines `GET /:id` (`getCarrierDetail`) which is the silent-trap that caused Item 39's 404. **Sprint shape:** consolidate to one route file + one URL pattern. Recommend keeping the plural `/api/carriers` (REST convention for collection) with proper sub-paths: `GET /` (list), `GET /search` or `GET /?search=X` (search), `GET /:id` (detail). Migrate all frontend callers. Delete the singular file. Validation lives at the canonical path. **Effort:** medium — requires grep across `frontend/src/` for all `api.get("/carrier/...")` and `api.get("/carriers/...")` callers, decision on canonical paths, route file consolidation, then frontend updates. ~30-50 LOC across 5-10 files. **Out of Sprint 31 scope** per §3.3 "no scope creep" — Sprint 31 atomic on the silent-fail URL fix only. **Tracked for post-BKN architecture queue** per locked sprint sequencing.

141. ~~**Tender expiry cron sweeper.**~~ **CLOSED 2026-05-16 in v3.8.abw / Sprint 52a** (commit `47bf0e53`) — docs-row marked CLOSED 2026-05-30 (it shipped but the §13.3 row drifted stale-open; **Sub-pattern 15 backlog-row-drift fire**, caught during the Item 142→141 sequence Phase A audit when a grep of the cited code paths showed the work already live). Both paths are safe; the cron just makes the friendlier message the common case. **Deviation from sprint-shape note:** shipped as hourly (`:30`) not "every 10 minutes" as the original shape guessed — hourly is sufficient at pre-revenue tender volume and matches the other email-fanning cron cadences. The "advance waterfall position to next-tier" sub-item was NOT part of v3.8.abw (waterfall position expiry has its own handling in `waterfallEngineService`); the load-revert-to-POSTED covers the direct-tender path.
