158. **Parallel carrier status-update endpoints consolidation.** Surfaced 2026-05-17 during Sprint 52.hotfix.c Phase A audit. Two parallel carrier-side status-update routes exist in the codebase: (a) `POST /api/carrier-loads/:id/status` at [`carrierLoads.ts:341`](backend/src/routes/carrierLoads.ts#L341) — what the carrier portal `/my-loads` page actually calls (controller inline, no auditLog wrapper, no central transition validator); (b) `PATCH /api/loads/:id/carrier-status` at [`loads.ts:39`](backend/src/routes/loads.ts#L39) — separate controller `carrierUpdateStatus`, separate validator `updateLoadStatusSchema`, `auditLog("UPDATE_STATUS", "Load")` wrapper. Both gate on `authorize("CARRIER")`. Frontend calls only endpoint (a); endpoint (b) is dead surface with no frontend caller. Same parallel-endpoints class as Sprint 52.hotfix.b Item 156 diagnostic (`/carrier-tenders/active` vs `/api/carrier/tenders`). **Sprint shape:** consolidate to one endpoint; recommend keeping the PATCH variant in loads.ts (auditLog wrapper, REST-correct HTTP verb, validator already separated) and migrating the carrier portal call site. ~30-50 LOC across 3 files (loads.ts unchanged, carrierLoads.ts:335-409 deleted, frontend my-loads page mutation URL + method updated). **Sprint 53+ candidate** — not BKN-blocking; current endpoint A works, just structurally redundant.

159. **Central LoadStatus state-machine validator.** Surfaced 2026-05-17 during Sprint 52.hotfix.c Phase A audit. 13+ distinct write sites mutate `Load.status` across the codebase (tenderController × 4, loadController × 5, carrierLoads.ts, loads.ts/carrierUpdateStatus, documentController, checkCallController, customerController, rateConfirmationController) with NO central transition rules. Each write site accepts whatever status its caller specifies. The `LoadStatus` enum has 18 values across the lifecycle pipeline (DRAFT → POSTED → TENDERED → BOOKED → DISPATCHED → AT_PICKUP → LOADED → IN_TRANSIT → AT_DELIVERY → DELIVERED → POD_RECEIVED → INVOICED → COMPLETED + TONU/CANCELLED/PICKED_UP legacy alias); CLAUDE.md §A.1 documents the canonical state machine but it lives in docs, not code. Carrier portal frontend has a `statusTransitions` map at [`my-loads/page.tsx:12-19`](frontend/src/app/carrier/dashboard/my-loads/page.tsx#L12) that enforces transitions client-side only — backend accepts any of 5 enum values regardless of current status. **Sprint shape:** central `validateLoadStatusTransition(from, to, actor)` helper at `backend/src/lib/loadStateMachine.ts` returning `{ allowed: boolean, reason?: string }`; refactor 13 write sites to invoke validator before `prisma.load.update`; auditLog rejected transitions. ~150-250 LOC across 1 new file + 8 callers (some controllers have multiple write sites). **Sprint 53+ multi-day epic** — significant refactor; gates on Sprint 52 epic completion. Methodology benefit: backend becomes authoritative on transition legality, frontend `statusTransitions` map becomes UI-hint only (not the only enforcement).

160. **ShipmentStatus ↔ LoadStatus enum gap.** Surfaced 2026-05-17 during Sprint 52.hotfix.c Phase A audit. `enum ShipmentStatus` (schema.prisma:197-206) has 8 values: PENDING, BOOKED, DISPATCHED, PICKED_UP, IN_TRANSIT, DELIVERED, COMPLETED, CANCELLED. `enum LoadStatus` (schema.prisma:26-45) has 18 values including the carrier-side states the ShipmentStatus enum LACKS: AT_PICKUP, LOADED, AT_DELIVERY, POD_RECEIVED, INVOICED, TONU. acceptTender at [`tenderController.ts:106`](backend/src/controllers/tenderController.ts#L106) auto-creates a Shipment with `status: "BOOKED"` (line 110) — that value DOES exist in both enums. But if any future flow reads Load.status and writes that value to Shipment.status, the 6 LoadStatus values absent from ShipmentStatus would fail Prisma validation. **Risk profile:** latent — no current code path writes LoadStatus values directly to Shipment.status (acceptTender hardcodes "BOOKED"); future refactor or feature add could trip this gap. **Sprint shape:** decide canonical: (α) expand ShipmentStatus to mirror full LoadStatus pipeline (Shipment becomes a status-tracking projection of Load), (β) keep ShipmentStatus narrow as billing/financial-cycle states only and document that Load.status is the operational source of truth, (γ) drop the Shipment model entirely if it's redundant with Load. Pairs naturally with Item 159 (central state machine) — the enum gap is the data-side expression of the same architectural ambiguity. **Sprint 53+ architectural decision sprint** — requires product call on what Shipment.status represents semantically.

161. **REOPENED + CLOSED 2026-05-17 in v3.8.aca (Sprint 53) — Auth cookie isolation. Original "no bug" close was premature. Sprint 53.a (v3.8.acb) hotfix follow-up — substring-match prefix collision.** Sprint 53 shipped with a substring `.includes("/carrier")` match in `resolveCookieToken` at `middleware/auth.ts:90` that wrongly routed AE-side endpoints with "carrier" in the name to the carrier cookie. Wasi's post-deploy smoke surfaced 403 on `GET /api/carriers` — same architectural class as Sprint 53's parent bug (substring vs proper prefix matching), just at a different layer. **V2 audit** during the Sprint 53.a hotfix enumerated `/api/carrier` (singular) as a genuine audience-mixed mount (6 carrier-facing endpoints `dashboard|scorecard|revenue|bonuses|onboarding-status|documents` lacking explicit `authorize("CARRIER")` + 6 AE-side endpoints `all|:id/detail|:id|verify/:id|admin-setup|capacity-feed` with explicit `authorize("ADMIN", "CEO", ...)`). Single-axis allow-list can't resolve both audiences without one side breaking in the dual-portal scenario. **Decision locked Option B per Wasi 2026-05-17:** allow-list EXCLUDES `/api/carrier` (singular) — the 6 carrier-facing endpoints under it return AE-scoped data when both portals are logged in same browser. Real-world users hold one role per browser so the fallback chain rescues; only deploy-test scenarios hit this. Architectural fix (split mount to move 6 AE-side endpoints into existing `/api/carriers` plural which has overlapping `getAllCarriers` controller anyway, OR introduce X-Portal request header from frontend) tracked as **Sprint 54+ candidate** — same priority as Item 158 (parallel-endpoint consolidation), same class. **Sprint 53.a fix shape:** explicit `CARRIER_PORTAL_MOUNTS` array (`/api/carrier-auth`, `/api/carrier-loads`, `/api/carrier-compliance`, `/api/carrier-payments`, `/api/carrier-tenders`) + `SHIPPER_PORTAL_MOUNTS` array (`/api/shipper-portal`) + new `matchesPortalMount(baseUrl, mounts)` helper using `baseUrl === p || baseUrl.startsWith(p + "/")`. ~25 LOC net change in single file. **Sub-pattern observation gains a second fire:** Sprint 52.hotfix.c missed the cookie layer entirely (Sprint 53 fire #1); Sprint 53 missed the substring-vs-prefix distinction within the cookie layer (fire #2 — same root cause class, one level deeper). The methodology principle banked at Item 161's first close ("Phase A on auth/permission symptoms must reach the storage/transport layer") needs an extension: *"and the prefix-vs-substring distinction within transport-layer routing logic is a hot edge — verify by enumerating ALL mount paths containing the keyword, not by trusting heuristic boundary matching."* Two fires; one more from a future independent incident promotes the principle to §19 canonical per sub-rule c three-fire convention. Sprint 53.a closes 53's regression; original Sprint 53 closure of items 9/10/11/14 remains in force.

 Sprint 52.hotfix.c attributed the carrier "Insufficient permissions" + three-surface status divergence to *observer-identity-confusion* (operator with multi-role privileges polluting their own test session). **Corrected RCA:** all three portals (AE Console, Carrier Portal, Shipper Portal) shared a single httpOnly cookie name `srl_token` set by `backend/src/utils/cookies.ts:14`. Same browser logging into two roles overwrote the cookie — second login replaced the first's JWT. `authorize("CARRIER")` at `backend/src/middleware/auth.ts:165` fired "Insufficient permissions" when the carrier-portal call ran with the ADMIN JWT that had just overwritten the carrier one. The system_log entries Sprint 52.hotfix.c surfaced (`whaider@silkroutelogistics.ai` denied on carrier endpoints) were the contamination *trail*, not test apparatus error. The "test from incognito" workaround masked the bug because incognito has no other portal's cookie to overwrite the carrier one. **Fix shipped Sprint 53:** per-portal cookie names (`srl_token_ae` / `srl_token_carrier` / `srl_token_shipper`), middleware picks the right cookie by `req.baseUrl` prefix, role passed to `setTokenCookie(res, token, role)` at all 14 callsites (authController.ts × 7, routes/auth.ts × 2, carrierAuth.ts × 5), legacy `srl_token` read as one-deploy migration fallback and cleared on next logout. Closes user punch-list items 9 (mark-delivered "Insufficient permissions"), 10 (carrier account auto-switched mid-test), 11 (carrier signout logged out AE). Bundled with Item 14 closure (loginLimiter bumped 5→20 in routes/auth.ts + routes/carrierAuth.ts, authLimiter bumped 30→100 in server.ts — Wasi's lockout during the lifecycle test). **Methodology observation banked as sub-pattern candidate (awaits 3-fire validation per §19 canonical promotion convention):** *"Phase A on auth/permission symptoms must reach the storage/transport layer (cookies, sessions, tokens, headers), not stop at the role gate."* Sprint 52.hotfix.c's Phase A inspected User.role bytes, system_logs, and Neon DB state — but stopped before the cookie layer that delivered the JWT. The "observer-identity-confusion" interpretation was internally consistent with what Phase A surfaced; the gap was scope, not reasoning. Extends Sub-pattern 5 (audit-both-ends-of-data-flow) from data flow to transport flow. Fire #1 banked here. Original "no bug" close preserved below for history.

161-original. ~~**Sprint 52.hotfix.c closed — no bug (observer-identity confusion fire #1).**~~ **CLOSED 2026-05-17 (chore, no version bump, no code change).** Reported symptom was carrier "Update Status: AT PICKUP" button returning "Insufficient permissions" + three-surface status divergence across carrier portal / AE Load Board row / AE Load Board detail panel. Phase A R1-R5 audit + Wasi-side Neon verification confirmed system working as designed: User.role = "CARRIER" byte-exact (length 7, hex `43415252494552`), system_logs healthy (65 SECURITY warnings in past 7 days, latest write <1 minute old at audit time), all recent `authorize()` denials attributed to `whaider@silkroutelogistics.ai` (ADMIN role) attempting carrier-portal endpoints — those denials were CORRECT per the role gate. INTEGRITY EXPRESS session itself was never the denied actor; the symptom surfaced from **cross-role cache contamination from admin's testing session** (admin had AE token in browser storage while testing carrier flows in same tab/window). The three-surface status divergence dissolved when the test was re-run from an incognito window with carrier credentials only — confirming the divergence was browser-state pollution, not data drift. **Methodology observation (fire #1):** *observer-identity-confusion antipattern* — when an operator with multi-role privileges tests a role-restricted flow without isolating session context, observed "bug" may be the test apparatus, not the system. Mitigation: always test role-restricted flows from incognito or separate browser profile with test-subject credentials only. Worth banking for second/third fire validation before promoting to §19 canonical (parallel to sub-pattern 13 + sub-pattern 15 three-fire lineage convention). Sprint 52.hotfix.c closes with zero source change, zero data fix; the Phase A audit work IS the deliverable — Items 158/159/160 banked as collateral findings.

162. **Track & Trace drawer ROUTE visualization regression** (originally directed as "Item 161" — directive was stale by one commit; Item 161 had just been consumed by Sprint 52.hotfix.c no-bug close in commit `a2c0e12`; renumbered to 162 per sub-pattern 6 concurrent-sprint-coordination correction). Banked 2026-05-17. **Class:** UI regression + sub-pattern 5 (audit-both-ends-of-data-flow — data populated server-side, not consumed client-side). **Severity:** P2 (operational hygiene, not load-blocking). **Surfaced on L7492033667 at POD_RECEIVED + INVOICED stages.** Symptoms: (1) Route bar shows static colored segment + dotted tail with no truck position marker. (2) "Current position" field renders em-dash despite the GPS panel below it showing `Source: AE_MANUAL`, last ping `May 17 10:22 AM`. (3) "ETA" field empty. (4) "Internal server error" banner visible on INVOICED stage drawer — possibly the ETA compute endpoint failing, adjacent issue worth isolating during Phase A. **Expected behavior:** (a) truck icon positioned proportionally along the route based on last known location point; (b) Current position populated from same source as GPS panel; (c) ETA computed from remaining distance + average speed or carrier ETA pings; (d) source provenance shown on the route visualization itself via badge/label — `AE_MANUAL` → "Last update: phone call", `EDI_214` → "Last update: carrier EDI ping", `ELD_GPS` → "Last update: device GPS", `CARRIER_CHECKIN` → "Last update: carrier portal", `GEOFENCE` → "Last update: geofence trigger"; (e) timestamp on the route bar, not buried in the GPS panel below. **Files likely involved (Phase A to confirm):** `frontend/src/components/tracking/TrackingDrawer.tsx` or similar; `frontend/src/components/tracking/RouteVisualization.tsx` or similar; backend endpoint serving the drawer — likely `GET /api/loads/:id/tracking` or `/track-trace/:id` namespace; may share data source with the GPS panel — if so, regression is in the route component only (consumer-side bug). **Sprint shape:** Phase A audit to identify which component owns the route bar render + which endpoint feeds it; cross-reference against GPS panel data source to confirm sub-pattern 5 class (data populated, consumer doesn't read). Likely small fix (~30-50 LOC) if regression is purely consumer-side; ~80-120 LOC if ETA compute endpoint also needs hardening. **Related:** Item 159 (Load.status state machine — same write-many-no-validation class as the GPS source field), sub-pattern 5 (audit-both-ends-of-data-flow). **Sprint timing:** post-Sprint-52 epic completion, or interleaved if it surfaces operational friction on the BKN onboarding walkthrough.

180. **Order Builder polish cluster — 11 small UX/operational fixes (umbrella).** Banked 2026-05-20 from Wasi's Sprint 59.c walk-through Q&A. Each sub-item is small (10-80 LOC), single-commit eligible, and not BKN-blocking on its own. Banked as an umbrella so they can be sequenced together when the polish budget opens. None depend on each other; can ship in any order.

   **180.1 — "Duplicate this order" action.** AE running repeat lanes (e.g. weekly BKN Detroit → Chicago) re-keys 30+ fields per draft. Add a one-click clone button on the drafts banner card + per-order kebab menu on the drafts list (Item 179) that creates a new draft with all fields except `id`, `orderNumber`, `loadId`, `status` copied from the source. ~30 LOC.

   **180.2 — Save-as-template for recurring lanes.** Different from 180.1 (template is named + reusable indefinitely; clone is one-shot). Schema addition: new `OrderTemplate` model with `customerId`, `name`, `formData` JSON. New `Template` selector in Section 1 of Order Builder beside Customer picker. AE picks "BKN — Detroit→Chicago weekly" → form prefills from template. Save current draft as new template via "Save as template…" action. ~120-180 LOC + 1 migration.

   **180.3 — Three text-field confusion (specialInstructions / driverInstructions / internalNotes).** Three textareas stacked vertically with similar UI invite AE error (carrier-sensitive info typed into wrong field, or AE-only context where carrier will see it). Single textarea with "visible to" radio (Carrier on rate-con / Driver on rate-con / Internal only) would be cleaner. Backend keeps the 3 columns; frontend collapses to one input + a visibility selector that writes to the corresponding field. ~50 LOC frontend.

   **180.4 — Customer-facing quote approve magic link.** Send quote today emails the customer with the price; customer replies by email; AE manually flips `Order.status = "quote_approved"` (or skips entirely). Add a signed token in the quote email body → public `/quote/approve/<token>` page → customer clicks "Approve at $X,XXX" → backend verifies token + sets `status = "quote_approved"` + emails AE confirmation. Same JWT shape as the magic-link tender accept proposed for Sprint 52b (Item 142). Tightens the quote loop. ~80-120 LOC.

   **180.5 — Quote preview before send.** AE can't see what customer will see before clicking Send quote — risk of typo/rate-error reaching the inbox. Add "Preview email" modal that renders the actual email HTML (calling the same builder used by `sendQuote` controller). Same modal pattern as the RC PDF preview. ~50 LOC.

   **180.6 — Accessorial picker with per-customer negotiated rates.** Current accessorial entry is type + amount + payer (free-form). No connection to customer contract rates. When AE picks "Detention" for BKN, should auto-fill BKN's negotiated rate (e.g. $50/hr) vs Acme's (e.g. $75/hr). **These are customer-side BILLING rates and are independent of the carrier-side PAY rate (clarified v3.8.arn).** What SRL bills a shipper for detention is negotiable per customer contract; what SRL PAYS a carrier is the uniform §5 policy — $50/hr for all equipment after 2 hours free at each stop, capped at $250/stop, with no tier, no equipment, and no per-customer variation. A customer billed at $75/hr does not move carrier pay; the spread is margin. Nothing in this item may be read as a live SRL detention-pay figure. Backend has `customer.contractRates` JSON or similar (verify in Phase A). Frontend reads customer's accessorial rates on customer-select and offers them as picker options. ~60-100 LOC.

   **180.7 — Margin-floor alert in OrderSidebar.** OrderSidebar surfaces margin % in real-time. Doesn't appear to alert when target cost produces margin below a configured floor. Add red warning chip when `margin < settings.minMarginPercent` (per-customer override possible). Settings live in `settings` page or `customer.minMarginPercent` column. ~30-50 LOC + maybe 1 schema field.

   **180.8 — `?resume=<orderId>` URL deep-link.** Item 179's drafts page needs URL-shareable resume paths. Today the drafts banner uses internal state mutation (`resumeDraft(d.id)`) with no URL change — AE can't paste a draft link into Slack/email. Add `useEffect` reading `searchParams.get("resume")` on mount; if present, fire `resumeDraft(orderId)`. ~10 LOC. Pairs with Item 179.

   **180.9 — Autosave indicator mirrored near footer CTAs.** Sprint 59.c kept DraftStatus in top header. AE working at the bottom of the form doesn't see it while clicking Tender/Waterfall/Load Board/DAT. Mirror a smaller `<DraftStatus>` chip inside the new footer button row (left side, before the dispatch buttons). ~5 LOC.

   **180.10 — Dispatch error banner relocated to footer.** Sprint 59.b's dispatch error banner renders after the top header but BEFORE the form columns. When dispatch fails from the footer Sprint 59.c moved them to, AE has to scroll back to the top to see the error. Move the banner to be a sibling of the footer button row (rendered above the buttons when isError, below when at very bottom of form). ~10 LOC re-parent.

   **180.11 — Origin/Destination facility name + address visual hierarchy.** Today Section 1 (Origin) + Section 2 (Destination) display fields flat — facility-picker result and address inputs all render at the same visual weight. Wasi 2026-05-20: facility NAME should be the prominent label at the top of each section ("QCC Distribution Center" in larger/bolder type), then address ("1234 Industrial Pkwy, San Diego, CA 92154") as secondary text below. Mirrors the canonical "name primary, supporting metadata below" pattern from CRM customer detail + Carrier Engagement Drawer's selected-carrier card ([CarrierEngagementDrawer.tsx:608-628](frontend/src/components/drawer/CarrierEngagementDrawer.tsx#L608-L628) for reference shape). Apply to both origin + destination sections. Address fields stay editable for AE override when facility lookup misses or a one-off address is needed. ~40-60 LOC across both sections (FacilityPicker result rendering + section header restructure).

   **Sprint slot:** post-Sprint-59.c soak, queue alongside Item 179 (drafts surface) + Item 178 (multi-line freight edit) as the Order Builder polish cluster. Sub-items can ship as a single bundled sprint OR as 11 individual atomic commits depending on operational urgency. Recommended grouping for one bundled sprint: visual polish bundle (180.3, 180.9, 180.10, 180.11) ~120 LOC + workflow bundle (180.1, 180.5, 180.8) ~70 LOC + revenue-protect bundle (180.6, 180.7) ~100 LOC. The two backend-touching items (180.2 template schema + 180.4 magic-link approve) are best as standalone sprints to keep migration + token-signing scope discrete.

177. **Visual-verification protocol gate — mandatory for drawer/modal/canvas-rendering sprints.** Banked 2026-05-18 alongside Sprint 59.a (v3.8.acn) hotfix closure. **Codified per Wasi ratification 2026-05-18.** Pre-Sprint-59.a state: pre-commit gates were `tsc --noEmit` + `next build` (Sub-pattern 11 CI-parity canonical). Sprint 59 shipped with both gates green but missed 4 user-facing UX bugs (horizontal tabs vs vertical IconTabs canonical, empty form on open, carrier name mismatch, customer rate duplication) — all compile-time clean, none caught by tsc or build. **Sub-pattern 8 (conditional-render-visual-verification) fired again** — second instance in this session arc (first was Sprint 48.c signature overlap at Item 139 canonical). Protocol mandate: **any sprint that ships a new drawer, modal, canvas-rendered surface, or visual layout restructure MUST include a pre-push visual smoke** — either via Playwright headed-browser screenshot (when CI-feasible) OR explicit Phase A code-trace of the visual class structure against the canonical reference, NOT just function signatures. Sub-pattern 8 sub-rule a: *"code-trace must include the visual-outcome class chain, not just the call graph."* Sub-pattern 8 sub-rule b: *"every new drawer surface re-verifies against the canonical right-drawer reference (currently T&T LoadDetailDrawer at [LoadDetailDrawer.tsx:108-112](frontend/src/app/dashboard/track-trace/LoadDetailDrawer.tsx#L108)) — IconTabs left strip + flex-1 main content sibling — NOT inline horizontal tabs in the form body."* Future Phase A audits checking drawer canonical must trace BOTH the component file's tab pattern (already done at Sprint 59 A3) AND the wrapping flex direction (`flex` vs `flex-col`) AND the sibling structure (`<IconTabs />` as first child, then `<div className="flex-1 flex flex-col min-w-0">`). Single-axis component-file audit produced the Sprint 59 miss. **Sprint shape for future drawer work:** Phase A canonical-trace adds step "A_visual" — read the canonical drawer's outermost JSX wrapper class chain + first 3 child siblings, document the visual hierarchy in the report, and confirm Phase B implementation matches. Costs ~10 minutes per Phase A; saves the kind of post-deploy hotfix that Sprint 59.a was. Item 177 closes structurally — the protocol is canonical from this commit forward, not a pending implementation. Pairs with Sub-pattern 11 (CI-parity) — together they form a two-gate pre-push discipline (compile gate + visual gate) for any UX-shipping sprint.

175. **RSC payload 404 on root `/index.txt?_rsc=*` requests.** Banked 2026-05-18 during Sprint 174.a (v3.8.ach) hotfix audit. Symptom in Wasi's DevTools console: `/index.txt?_rsc=1ri1u: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404`. Same architectural class as §13.3 Item 156 (carrier route RSC payload — Gmail iOS WebView Accept-header content negotiation) but on the root path rather than `/carrier/*`. Cloudflare Pages doesn't have an `/index.txt` static file because Next.js static export generates `/index.html` only; the `?_rsc=*` query string is a Next.js App Router internal RSC (React Server Components) payload fetch attempt. Static export shouldn't be emitting RSC fetches at all, but framework versions occasionally regress on this. **Sprint shape:** investigate which component or framework version is emitting the RSC fetch. Options: (a) check `frontend/next.config.ts` for any RSC-enabling config that conflicts with `output: "export"`; (b) audit framework version + Next.js patch notes for RSC-in-static-export regressions; (c) add `_redirects` rule `/index.txt /index.html 200` as a band-aid that satisfies the fetch with the actual page content. Low priority — RSC payload fetch failures don't break the page render (Next.js gracefully falls back to client-side navigation), they just produce console noise. Pairs with Item 156 architecturally (same RSC content-negotiation class). Sprint slot: post-BKN cleanup unless a user-facing symptom surfaces.

174. ~~**Shipper login role-gate gap — carrier creds work on /shipper/login.**~~ **CLOSED 2026-05-18 in v3.8.acf** (Sprint Item 174, Option β+γ+α defense-in-depth). Symptom: INTEGRITY EXPRESS (aliabbas6361@gmail.com, role=CARRIER) could complete /shipper/login → OTP → land on /shipper/dashboard authenticated, despite being a carrier account. Shipper API gates (`authorize("SHIPPER")`) held so no data leak, but portal-boundary integrity violated. **Three-layer gap audited:** (a) shipper login page reuses AE auth endpoints — [shipper/login/page.tsx:10,46](frontend/src/app/shipper/login/page.tsx#L10) imports `useAuthStore` calling `/api/auth/login` + `/api/auth/verify-otp` (the AE endpoints, not separate shipper paths); (b) `/api/auth/login` at [authController.ts:148-218](backend/src/controllers/authController.ts#L148) had no role gate — only password + lockout + isActive checks; (c) `/api/auth/verify-otp` had SHIPPER-specific `checkShipperApproval` but no refusal for non-SHIPPER roles — carrier flowed straight through to JWT issuance; (d) shipper dashboard layout at [shipper/dashboard/layout.tsx:48-61](frontend/src/app/shipper/dashboard/layout.tsx#L48) had no role check — only `if (!currentUser)`. **Fix shape — defense-in-depth at three layers (Option β+γ+α combined):** Layer γ-1 backend validator: optional `expectedRole: "AE" | "SHIPPER"` added to `loginSchema` ([validators/auth.ts](backend/src/validators/auth.ts)) + `otpSchema` ([routes/auth.ts:23](backend/src/routes/auth.ts#L23)). Layer γ-2 backend controller: new `AE_ROLES` set + `rolesMatch(userRole, expectedRole)` helper at [authController.ts:21-30](backend/src/controllers/authController.ts#L21); role check in `login` after isActive check + in `handleVerifyOtp` after user lookup. 401 + `code: "ROLE_MISMATCH"`, message "Invalid credentials for this portal." Layer γ-3 useAuthStore: `login` + `verifyOtp` signatures extended with optional `expectedRole`, body conditionally includes the field. Layer β shipper login: passes `"SHIPPER"` to both calls; post-OTP frontend role check (defense-in-depth in case backend gate fails) — on mismatch calls `/api/auth/logout` + `useAuthStore.getState().clearAuth()` + shows error. Layer γ-4 AE login: passes `"AE"` in both fetch bodies (page uses raw fetch, not useAuthStore). Layer α shipper dashboard layout: `bounceIfWrongRole` helper called from both fresh-load and cached-user branches — on mismatch calls `/api/auth/logout` + clearAuth + `router.replace("/shipper/login")`. **Carrier portal unaffected** — uses `/api/carrier-auth/*` which already gates strictly to CARRIER role per [carrierAuth.ts:70](backend/src/routes/carrierAuth.ts#L70) + [carrierAuth.ts:153](backend/src/routes/carrierAuth.ts#L153). **Methodology — sub-pattern fire #1 banked: "portal-boundary-defense-asymmetry":** *"When one portal (carrier) has rigorous role gating across login/OTP/layout but another (shipper) reuses shared AE auth endpoints without role gates, the asymmetry becomes a portal-boundary violation surface. Audit all three portals' login flows for symmetric defense at each layer."* Sub-pattern awaits fire #2 + #3 from independent incidents before §19 canonical promotion. Pairs with Item 168 (audit-wrong-code-path) and Item 169 (interceptor-without-context-awareness) — three consecutive scope/context-discipline sub-pattern candidates banked in the Sprint 53→54→174 arc.

Today (May 18), pre-Phase-A re-audit on the ACTUAL carrier flow (carrierAuth.ts):  setTokenCookie passes `"CARRIER"` correctly at all 4 carrier-auth callsites (lines 205, 276, 351, 379); `/api/carrier-auth/*` matches CARRIER_PORTAL_MOUNTS allow-list exactly; resolveCookieToken returns srl_token_carrier correctly. Sprint 54 portal-aware 401 interceptor routes carrier-dashboard 401s to /carrier/login correctly. **Wasi's re-test on May 18 in fresh incognito confirmed no kick-out — carrier login works end-to-end.** The original symptom was dual-portal cookie contamination from yesterday's test session (AE cookie present in the same browser polluting carrier endpoint resolution); Sprint 53.a CARRIER_PORTAL_MOUNTS preferred-cookie selection resolves this when the request lands on a carrier-portal mount with srl_token_carrier present. Fresh-incognito sessions don't have AE cookie contamination, so the fix surfaces cleanly. **No source change for Item 168** — closure is a posture correction: this was a Sprint 53.a downstream resolution, not a separate Sprint-needing bug. Yesterday's "audit-wrong-code-path" sub-pattern fire #1 stands — banking remains valid even though the underlying bug self-resolved, because the methodology miss (auditing AE flow instead of carrier flow) was real regardless.

168-original. **Carrier OTP login kick-out (Sprint 54 Item 11 deferred).** Banked 2026-05-17 after Sprint 54 Phase A traced the wrong code path. Original symptom reported by Wasi during post-Sprint-53.a smoke: "OTP success → immediate logout." Phase A misread context and audited `backend/src/controllers/authController.ts` ADMIN TOTP flow (`handleVerifyOtp` + `handleTotpLoginVerify`) — the AE-portal code path. Wasi corrected: he was testing the **CARRIER** portal flow, not AE. Carrier auth lives at `backend/src/routes/carrierAuth.ts` with its own `handleVerifyOtp` and totp-verify handlers, separate `useCarrierAuth` Zustand store, separate `/carrier/login` UI. Sprint 54 dropped Item 11 from its atomic scope; re-audit scheduled for next session against the actual carrier code path. **Sprint shape for re-audit:** (1) read `backend/src/routes/carrierAuth.ts` OTP verify + TOTP verify handlers verbatim, focus on the setTokenCookie call site + which role string is passed; (2) read `frontend/src/hooks/useCarrierAuth.ts` post-verify state setter + redirect logic; (3) read `frontend/src/app/carrier/dashboard/layout.tsx` AuthGuard equivalent that fires loadUser → /api/carrier-auth/me; (4) reproduce in incognito on prod with DevTools Network preserve-log, capture the 401 response body + Cookie request header on the failing endpoint after carrier OTP success; (5) cross-reference against Sprint 53.a CARRIER_PORTAL_MOUNTS allow-list to confirm `/api/carrier-auth/me` baseUrl correctly matches `/api/carrier-auth` and reads srl_token_carrier cookie. **Methodology lesson (banked as Sub-rule c sub-pattern candidate fire #1 — "audit-wrong-code-path"):** *"When user reports symptom in flow X, Phase A must verify it's auditing flow X's actual code path before deep-diving."* The OTP login audit looked at admin TOTP verify because the AE flow was the default mental model; the user's report was carrier flow. Sub-pattern banks alongside Sprint 53 + 53.a fires #1 (cookie layer scope) + #2 (substring-vs-prefix within cookie layer); cumulative pattern: Phase A scope-discipline failures cluster around "what was the user actually testing?" rather than "where does the code think it lives?". Sub-pattern awaits fire #2 + #3 from independent incidents before §19 canonical promotion per sub-rule c three-fire convention.

169. **HTTP interceptor-without-context-awareness (sub-pattern candidate fire #1).** Banked 2026-05-17 alongside Sprint 54 close of Item 6 (View Tender CTA wrong portal). The frontend axios 401 interceptor at `frontend/src/lib/api.ts:35-42` (pre-Sprint-54) made a portal-routing decision (`/auth/login` redirect target) based only on the response status code, with no reference to `window.location.pathname` to know which portal the request originated from. Net effect: a logged-out carrier landing on `/carrier/dashboard/tenders` from an email CTA got bounced to the AE login page on first 401, despite the carrier portal having its own `/carrier/login` surface. Sprint 54 fixed by reading `window.location.pathname` and picking `/carrier/login` / `/shipper/login` / `/auth/login` accordingly. **Methodology lesson banked as Sub-rule c sub-pattern candidate fire #1 — "interceptor-without-context-awareness":** *"Frontend HTTP interceptors that make routing decisions on responses (e.g. 401 → redirect) must read request context (URL path, expected portal) before deciding the target. Hardcoded fallbacks erase user origin context."* Candidate awaits fire #2 + #3 from independent incidents before §19 canonical promotion. Pairs with Items 168 + Sprint 53 audit-wrong-code-path lineage — both point to the same broader meta-pattern: scope/context discipline in audit AND in code design. **Cross-reference:** Item 168 (audit-wrong-code-path, methodology); this Item 169 (interceptor-without-context, code-design). Different layers, same shape.

170. **Carrier portal Rate Confirmation download visibility (Sprint Phase 2 follow-on).** Banked 2026-05-17 alongside Sprint Phase 2 close (auto-RC on tender accept, v3.8.acd). Phase 2 produces auto-DRAFT RCs on tender accept and AE manually sends them via existing `POST /api/rate-confirmations/:id/send` (email + PDF attachment to carrier). What's STILL missing: a carrier-portal endpoint that exposes RC download by loadId — `GET /api/rate-confirmations/:id/pdf` is CARRIER-authorized but requires the RC's UUID which the carrier doesn't have. `GET /api/rate-confirmations/load/:loadId` lookup is AE-only (carrier role not in authorize list at `backend/src/routes/rateConfirmations.ts:20`). **Sprint shape:** (a) new endpoint `GET /api/rate-confirmations/load/:loadId/latest/pdf` (CARRIER authorized, verifies carrier owns the load, looks up most recent RC, streams PDF via existing `generateEnhancedRateConfirmation`) — returns 404 if no RC exists yet; (b) add CARRIER to `GET /api/rate-confirmations/load/:loadId` authorize list for metadata reads (status, sentAt, signed flag) so the carrier UI can gate the download button correctly; (c) frontend `/carrier/dashboard/my-loads` load detail panel — replace `rateConfirmationPdfUrl` column gating with TanStack query against the new endpoint, "Download Rate Confirmation" button always visible for BOOKED+ status with disabled "pending" state when no RC exists. ~50 LOC across 2 files backend + 1 file frontend. **Priority:** queue after Phase 2 deploy soak — carriers currently receive RC via email attachment so Phase 2 is functionally complete without this; portal download is a re-download convenience. Pairs with Item 171 (auto-send) — if 171 ships first, this becomes more relevant. **Sprint slot:** post-Sprint-54 carrier-OTP audit (Item 168), interleave before Sprint 56 if BKN onboarding asks for re-download UX.

**Authority-age compliance epic — logged 2026-05-21 (Wasi cross-cutting directive, v3.8.ahj-ahn):**

182. **Authority-age compliance epic (v3.8.ahj → v3.8.ahn).** Surfaced 2026-05-21 from Wasi cross-cutting directive: carriers whose FMCSA operating authority is younger than 18 months are HARD-BLOCKED from hauling SRL loads. Override window exists for authority age 12-18 months, accessible to ADMIN+CEO via the existing Sprint 40 ComplianceOverride flow (24h expiry + 15/30-day quota unchanged). Authority age under 12 months is hard-block with no override. Authority age 18+ months auto-allows.

    **Locked decisions (do not re-litigate per Item 182 epic directive):**
    - **Threshold (Option A):** age <12 mo → hard-block; age 12-18 mo → override-eligible (ADMIN/CEO); age ≥18 mo → auto-allow.
    - **Override mechanism:** reuse existing `ComplianceOverride` table from Sprint 40 / Item 58 with reason text encoding "authority-age-override" semantics. No new override model — keeps the audit + quota infrastructure single-sourced.
    - **Override role:** ADMIN+CEO (same gating as Sprint 40 compliance override).
    - **Override expiry + quota:** 24 hours + 15-per-30-days per carrier, unchanged from Sprint 40 defaults.
    - **Existing APPROVED carrier grandfathering (Option γ):** soft-grandfather. Carriers already APPROVED at the time v3.8.ahl ships are flagged with an AE warning on tender, NOT auto-blocked. The new rule applies prospectively to newly approved carriers. No backfill-and-reject of the existing carrier base.
    - **Gate scope:** age derived ON READ from stored `authorityGrantedDate`. NOT a cron-refreshed `authorityAgeDays` snapshot. The `authorityAgeDays` schema field at [`schema.prisma:881`](backend/prisma/schema.prisma#L881) stays unused per locked decision — recomputing months from the stable grant date each gate fire is cheaper than maintaining a stale snapshot.
    - **Onboarding rejection UX (Option β):** carriers under 18 months at the `/onboarding` MC/DOT lookup are NOT hard-rejected. Their email + DOT + projected eligibility date are captured to a new `WaitingList` Prisma model; an auto-notify fires when they cross 18 months. No "Application rejected" dead-end page.
    - **Soft authority-age deduction in `carrierVettingService.ts:249-265`:** retained as-is. The hard gate subsumes the block decision; the vetting score deduction remains for analytics + Compass Score continuity. Revisit at v3.8.ahn close to decide whether to remove the now-redundant soft check.

    **FMCSA data source.** Free QCMobile endpoint `GET /qc/services/carriers/{dot}/authority?webKey={key}` using the existing `FMCSA_WEB_KEY` env var. Earliest `original_served_date` from the operating-authority history is the canonical grant date. Sub-rule c verification (web research 2026-05-21): endpoint exists per FMCSA QCMobile documentation; free under the same webKey the service already holds; response shape includes `docket_number`, `authority_type`, `original_action`, `original_served_date`, `disposition_action`, `disposition_served_date` per Alphaloops 2026 FMCSA API reference. The endpoint is NOT documented on the `/QCDevsite/docs/apiElements` page but IS listed on the `/QCDevsite/docs/qcApi` endpoint inventory.

    **Reinstatement-continuity caveat (deferred).** A carrier whose authority was granted, revoked, and later reinstated reads as older than they operationally are because the gate anchors on the original grant date, not the most recent reinstatement. Deliberate v3.8.ahj decision: anchor on `original_served_date` for now and document the edge case for an eventual AE-warning surface in v3.8.ahl or v3.8.ahm window. Not a v3.8.ahj fix.

    **Sprint sequence (each atomic per §3.3; halt for ratification between each):**
    - **v3.8.ahj — FMCSA authority data plumbing.** New `getCarrierAuthority(dotNumber)` in `fmcsaService.ts` hitting the QCMobile authority endpoint. New `fmcsaTypes.ts` with `FMCSAAuthorityResult` interface. Parallel `authorityCache` map (inherits the service's existing 1-hour TTL — the epic-design assumption was 24h but Pattern 6 sub-rule c authoritative-source verification confirms the existing pattern is 1h; refactor to per-key TTL is out of v3.8.ahj scope). Smoke test with mocked `fetch` covering happy path / no-history / multi-GRANT-earliest-wins / REVOCATION-REINSTATEMENT-ignored. **No schema write-path, no gate, no override UI, no onboarding integration in this sprint.** ~250 LOC.

One-time backfill script for existing APPROVED carriers (each carrier hit once; cached locally; idempotent). Leave `authorityAgeDays` unused per locked decision. ~80 LOC + backfill script.

Returns `{ blocked: true, code: "AUTHORITY_TOO_YOUNG", overridable: bool, ageMonths: N }` with `overridable=true` iff `ageMonths ∈ [12, 18)`.     **Logic (D9-U + hard floor at 12 ratified):**
    - `approvedAt < AUTHORITY_AGE_GATE_LIVE_AT` → grandfather (warning, never block, regardless of age or null grant).
    - `approvedAt >= cutoff` + `authorityGrantedDate` present + `ageMonths >= 18` → silent allow.
    - `approvedAt >= cutoff` + `12 <= ageMonths < 18` → block by default, **released** by an active `ComplianceOverride` with `checkCode = "AUTHORITY_TOO_YOUNG"`. Override release surfaces an `AUTHORITY_AGE_OVERRIDE` warning.
    - `approvedAt >= cutoff` + `ageMonths < 12` → **HARD FLOOR — block always, no override consulted** (override is NOT looked up in this branch, deliberate per Phase A D9).
    - `approvedAt >= cutoff` + null grant + `<24h since approval` → warning only (`AUTHORITY_PENDING`).
    - `approvedAt >= cutoff` + null grant + `>=24h since approval` → hard block (`AUTHORITY_UNVERIFIED`).

Warning strings prefixed `"AUTHORITY_AGE_GRANDFATHERED: ..."`, `"AUTHORITY_AGE_OVERRIDE: ..."`, `"AUTHORITY_PENDING: ..."`.

A live-deploy smoke caught that the function returns `authorityGrantDate: null` for every real carrier — including established 17-year-old motor carriers like INTEGRITY EXPRESS LOGISTICS LLC (DOT 1911857). This is a **pre-existing known issue** documented in the 2026-05-23 audit at [`carrierController.ts:1193-1196`](backend/src/controllers/carrierController.ts#L1193): the FMCSA QCMobile `/carriers/{dot}/authority` endpoint returns CURRENT-STATUS fields only (`brokerAuthorityStatus`, `commonAuthorityStatus`), not historical GRANT events, so the parser's filter for `originalAction === "GRANT"` matches zero entries on every real response. v3.8.aio shipped a manual AE-side workaround (`POST /carrier/:id/authority-grant-date`) but never fixed the function. v3.8.aku's Phase A audit verified `getCarrierAuthority` SIGNATURES + cache TTL + return shape but did not grep for prior source comments documenting the function's failed behavior, leading to a Sub-pattern 5 audit-both-ends miss EXTENDED: function-signature audit ≠ function-behavior audit. **v3.8.akv removed** the harmful surfaces: the `authorityVerdict` enrichment on both lookup endpoints, the `buildAuthorityVerdict` helper, the three /onboarding verdict pills + blocking waitlist capture form + the `submitToWaitlist` mutation, the `canNext` Step 1 gate extension, and the `POST /carrier/waitlist` endpoint. **v3.8.akv retained**: the `WaitingList` Prisma model + its migration (already applied to prod 2026-05-25 — deleting would create schema drift), the tender-time authority-age gate in `complianceMonitorService.ts` (v3.8.ahl/ahm), the manual AE authority-grant-date entry endpoint (v3.8.aio), the soft-grandfathering of pre-cutoff APPROVED carriers, the `getCarrierAuthority` function itself + its null-writing callers (`populateAuthorityGrantedDate`, `registerCarrier`, `setupAdminCarrierProfile`) — these are the working interim path and the future Highway-backed reimplementation site. **Item 182 epic status:** 4 of 5 sprints shipped (v3.8.ahj data plumbing → ahk schema population → ahl/ahm hard gate + override schema → ahq scoped override endpoint + AE modal). Sprint 5 reverts to LOG OPEN pending a working authority data source. Sprint 5 epic close deferred until Highway-backed reimplementation lands. Sprint 5 (Onboarding UI + WaitingList) original-implementation details preserved below for the Highway-reimplementation reference:

    - **Schema (`backend/prisma/schema.prisma`):** new `WaitingList` model with `{ id, email, dotNumber, mcNumber?, authorityGrantedDate, eligibilityDate, notifiedAt?, createdAt }` + `@@unique([email, dotNumber])` dedup + `@@index([eligibilityDate])` + `@@index([notifiedAt])`. Manual migration `20260525160000_add_waiting_list/migration.sql` per §2.2.
    - **Backend (`backend/src/routes/carrier.ts`):** new exported `AuthorityVerdict` type + `buildAuthorityVerdict(grantDate)` helper that reuses `calendarMonthsBetween` from `fmcsaService.ts` (the same primitive the post-approval `complianceCheck()` gate uses). Verdict thresholds match Item 182 locked decisions: `≥18mo → AUTO_ALLOW`, `12-18mo → OVERRIDE_ELIGIBLE`, `<12mo OR null → WAITING_LIST`. Both `GET /carrier/fmcsa-lookup/:dot` and `GET /carrier/fmcsa-mc-lookup/:mc` endpoints extended with authority enrichment via `getCarrierAuthority(dot)` inside a try/catch (Option β: defensive fallback to `WAITING_LIST` verdict on lookup failure). Response shape gains `authorityGrantDate`, `authorityAgeMonths`, `authorityVerdict`, `authorityEligibilityDate`. New `POST /carrier/waitlist` endpoint (public, no auth — same shape as the other pre-registration endpoints) with Zod-validated payload + upsert on `(email, dotNumber)` so re-fills don't duplicate. Sprint 5 is write-only; auto-notify cron is a separate follow-up.
    - **Frontend (`frontend/src/app/onboarding/page.tsx`):** new `AuthorityVerdict` type + extended `FmcsaResult` interface. New state (`waitlistSubmitting`, `waitlistSubmitted`, `waitlistError`) + `submitToWaitlist()` mutation hook calling `POST /carrier/waitlist`. `canNext()` Step 1 gate extended to return `false` when `fmcsaResult.authorityVerdict === "WAITING_LIST"` — carrier cannot proceed to Step 2 until they submit the waitlist form (which transitions to a "you're on the list" confirmation card and unblocks no further progress; the registration flow terminates here). Three verdict-pill render branches inline in the FMCSA result block: `AUTO_ALLOW` → silent green confirmation (`#E6F0E9` bg + `#2F7A4F` text); `OVERRIDE_ELIGIBLE` → amber warning (`#FBEFD4` bg + `#B07A1A` text) explaining manual review path; `WAITING_LIST` → red blocking surface (`#F6E3E3` bg + `#9B2C2C` text) with inline email input + "Notify me" button + projected eligibility date display.
    - **Locked behavior:** OVERRIDE_ELIGIBLE does NOT block Step 1 → Next — carriers proceed normally; AE applies the `ComplianceOverride` (with `checkCode: "AUTHORITY_TOO_YOUNG"`) during post-registration approval review per the v3.8.ahq + frontend modal extension that closed sprint 4. AUTO_ALLOW carriers see only the silent green confirmation and proceed with no additional friction. WAITING_LIST is the only blocking verdict.
    - **Defensive fallback:** when `getCarrierAuthority()` fails (transient network error, FMCSA endpoint timeout, no FMCSA_WEB_KEY env), the backend logs a warning and returns `verdict: WAITING_LIST` + `authorityAgeMonths: null` so the carrier still sees a deterministic surface rather than a silent pass-through. Matches Option β ratified decision in the epic logging.
    - **Scope:** ~270 LOC net across 4 files + 1 migration. Pre-commit gates per Sub-pattern 11 (CI parity): prisma generate clean, backend tsc clean, backend npm test clean, frontend tsc + next build clean. Sprint 6 (auto-notify cron — query `WHERE eligibilityDate <= NOW() AND notifiedAt IS NULL` and email each carrier) banked as separate follow-up, no firm slot.

    **Item 182 epic stats:** 5 sprints (v3.8.ahj data plumbing → ahk schema population + backfill script → ahl scoped-override migration → ahm hard gate + tests → ahq scoped override endpoint + AE modal → aku onboarding UI + WaitingList) shipped across 2026-05-21 through 2026-05-25. Total ~1,400 LOC across schema + 3 migrations + 4 backend services + 2 frontend modals + extensive test coverage. Sub-pattern 6 sub-rule c fired multiple times during the arc (concurrent-sprint-coordination on parallel commits, authoritative-source verification on FMCSA endpoint shape, scope-against-latest-production-state on letter assignments). Zero rollbacks across the 5 sprints.

185. **Daily `fmcsaComplianceScan` cron runs in UTC, not Eastern.** Banked 2026-05-22 alongside v3.8.ahw close. Phase A read-only finding: no `cron.schedule()` call in [`backend/src/cron/index.ts`](backend/src/cron/index.ts) passes a `timezone` option (Phase A grep `timezone` case-insensitive across the file returned zero hits). `node-cron` default behavior: uses host process's local time. `render.yaml` has no `TZ` env var (Phase A grep `TZ|timezone|timeZone` returned zero hits). Render Linux containers default to UTC unless `TZ` is set. **Net effect:** the `"0 3 * * *"` daily FMCSA scan fires at **3:00 AM UTC**, which is 11:00 PM Eastern (during EDT) or 10:00 PM Eastern (during EST) — same evening, prior calendar day from a US-ops perspective. All other "daily AM" jobs in the same file (`daily-cpp-cleanup 6am`, `health-digest 7am`, `compliance-reminders 5am`, identity-validation `6am`, ai-rate-intelligence `4am`, ai-carrier-intelligence `4:15am`, ai-compliance-forecast `5:30am`, ai-morning-briefing `6:30am`) inherit the same UTC default and similarly fire in the prior-day Eastern evening. This is operationally consistent across the cron file (all "daily" jobs run on the same wall clock), just not on the wall clock Wasi would intuit if reading "3 AM" as Eastern. **Sprint shape:** decide canonical for the whole cron file — either (a) accept UTC as the operational convention and document the offset in CLAUDE.md so future readers don't trip, OR (b) set the file's `cron.schedule()` calls to pass `{ timezone: "America/New_York" }` (or `"America/Detroit"` per §1 principal address) so cron times read as Eastern, OR (c) set `TZ=America/New_York` on the Render service env so the whole process clock shifts (also affects log timestamps + any `new Date()` formatting in user-facing emails). Decision pending Wasi call. Effort: small (~5 LOC + a Render dashboard env edit). Not BKN-blocking — FMCSA scan firing at 11pm ET vs 3am ET produces the same operational outcome (overnight refresh either way), just changes when the scan's email-to-admins surfaces in Wasi's inbox.

Net: change history is queryable via SQL/Prisma only. **Sprint shape:** if AE/CEO wants visibility into "what changed on this carrier across the last N FMCSA scans," need a new surface — either (a) a `ComplianceScan` history tab inside the existing `/dashboard/violations` page filterable by carrier, OR (b) a per-carrier expandable section in the existing CarrierDrawer / CarrierDetailDrawer showing the last K scans with their `changesDetected` JSON unrolled, OR (c) a CSV export endpoint for periodic review without an in-app surface. Not urgent — the alerts surface already shows the operationally-actionable signal (critical / warning entries); scan history is forensic / audit value only. **Pairs with Item 8.9** (authority-block centralization) loosely as compliance-observability infrastructure cleanup; not the same class.

187. **Suspension-column convention unification across `complianceMonitorService.ts`.** Banked 2026-05-22 alongside v3.8.ahw close — promoted from the scope-corrected TODO comment at [`complianceMonitorService.ts:810-820`](backend/src/services/complianceMonitorService.ts#L810). Two suspension-reason/timestamp column pairs are both live on `CarrierProfile` and both written by the canonical compliance service: (a) **`autoSuspendReason` + `autoSuspendedAt`** — the newer pair, written by `fmcsaComplianceScan`'s revoke / insurance-missing / OOS branches (lines ~947, ~1058) AND by the Sprint 40 `OverrideComplianceModal` cleanup query at line ~1225 which uses `autoSuspendedAt` as the lookup key for clearing override-stale entries. (b) **`suspensionReason` + `suspendedAt`** — the older pair, written by 4 OTHER canonical-service branches: insurance-expiry handler (line ~1424), monthly re-vetting (line ~1553), FMCSA authority-change watcher (line ~1662), FMCSA safety-rating watcher (line ~1702). **Correctness impact today: low.** `complianceCheck` at line 115 keys off `onboardingStatus === "SUSPENDED"` only — neither reason/timestamp column gates anything. The drift is observability noise: when an AE looks at why a carrier got auto-suspended, the explanation lives in one column or the other depending on which code path triggered, and any UI / report that reads only one column will silently skip half the suspensions. **Recommended canonical: `autoSuspendReason` + `autoSuspendedAt`.** Reasons: (i) used by Sprint 40 OverrideComplianceModal infrastructure, (ii) more semantically explicit (`auto` prefix surfaces that the system, not a human, did the suspending), (iii) only 4 call sites need to migrate vs 5+ surfaces if we picked the older pair. **Sprint shape:** rename across the 4 older-pair writers above + verify no admin UI / Prisma query reads the older pair (grep `suspensionReason|suspendedAt` across `backend/` + `frontend/` first). One-time data backfill SQL to migrate existing rows where the older pair is set but the newer is null. ~30-60 LOC source + 1 backfill script. Defensible to defer until either (a) an AE-facing surface starts reading the columns and the inconsistency becomes user-visible, OR (b) the platform takes any other action on `CarrierProfile.suspensionReason`/`suspendedAt` (e.g. adding it to a search / export, or removing it). Not BKN-blocking — pre-revenue carrier count means most auto-suspensions today are the FMCSA branches that already use the newer pair.

Read-only audit (separate report) established both functions hit identical FMCSA QCMobile `/carriers/{dot}` endpoint over APPROVED-with-DOT population; neither touched BASICs/SMS or the dedicated OOS endpoint. **Shape:** (a) cron schedule `"0 3 * * 1"` → `"0 3 * * *"` (weekly Mon → daily); (b) canonical scan renamed `weeklyFmcsaScan → fmcsaComplianceScan` (cadence-neutral so we don't re-create the `runDailyMonitor` misnomer); (c) change-detection in the canonical scan extended — existing 4-field critical/warning diff (`operatingStatus`/`safetyRating`/`insuranceOnFile`/`outOfServiceDate`) preserved; new 3-field INFO diff (`verified`/`totalDrivers`/`totalPowerUnits`) emits `ComplianceAlert` of severity INFO with 30-day expiry per detected change — these **do NOT auto-suspend** (only existing CRITICAL flips suspend); (d) all 4 `[WeeklyFMCSA]` log-prefix occurrences renamed to `[FMCSAScan]`; (e) `fmcsaBulkMonitorService.ts` top-of-file comment reframed as "On-demand re-scan, NOT SCHEDULED — scheduled FMCSA path is now `fmcsaComplianceScan` daily 3am" to prevent future confusion; the function name `runDailyMonitor` itself NOT renamed per directive (would have sprawled into the route + admin-controller surfaces; comment is sufficient); (f) `POST /integrations/fmcsa/bulk-monitor` endpoint and route gate (ADMIN/CEO/BROKER/OPERATIONS) preserved unchanged. **TODO logged inline:** `runDailyMonitor` writes `suspensionReason` + `suspendedAt`; canonical scan writes `autoSuspendReason` + `autoSuspendedAt`. Convention-unification deferred to a later cleanup commit (item-183-followup TODO comment in `complianceMonitorService.ts:808`). **Sprawl bound:** rename touched 2 files, 5 hits (Phase A grep). **FMCSA-courtesy pacing:** scan iterates APPROVED-with-DOT serially without per-call delay; `verifyCarrierWithFMCSA` has 6s timeout per call + 1h in-memory cache (`fmcsaService.ts:15`). At pre-revenue carrier count (<50 today) the 3am cold-cache scan runs <2min; even at N=200, ~5-7min — well within QCMobile's generous rate budget. Auth-routes/admin-cron-registry display of "weekly" job descriptions not re-scoped — cron job key `fmcsa-compliance` unchanged so any admin/monitoring UI keys on that ID continue to match. **Pre-commit gates:** backend `tsc --noEmit` clean. Per §3.1: v3.8.ahu → v3.8.ahv.

191. ~~**Prisma + Neon `DIRECT_URL` split — permanent fix for the P1002 advisory-lock contention class.**~~ **CLOSED 2026-05-24 in v3.8.ajg + v3.8.ajs** (atomic ship + defensive guard). Backlog-row was originally banked 2026-05-24 alongside the v3.8.ajf P1002 incident; the FIX shipped same day per §11 history row [CLAUDE.md:664](CLAUDE.md#L664) but this §13.3 row was never marked closed — banked-row-text-drift caught when Wasi cross-referenced 2026-05-25. **Fix shape:** v3.8.ajg added `directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")` to `backend/prisma/schema.prisma` datasource block, updated CLAUDE.md §2.2 with new env var list (`DATABASE_URL` + `DIRECT_URL` + `PRISMA_MIGRATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT=60000`), Render dashboard env vars set by Wasi pre-deploy. v3.8.ajs added defensive `backend/scripts/check-direct-url.js` pre-migrate build guard that fails fast (exit 1 with self-explanatory remediation message) if `DIRECT_URL` is unset OR its hostname contains `-pooler` (catches the env-config mismatch that hit v3.8.ajr's deploy — `DIRECT_URL` was set but pointed at the pooled URL by mistake, so migrate routed through pooler → P1002). Pre-ajs the failure mode was a silent 10s P1002 timeout with no hint about WHY; post-ajs the build fails in <1s with exact remediation steps. **Methodology observation banked (Sub-pattern 6 sub-rule c case-study extension #2 — "backlog-row-drift vs §11-history-row"):** initial CLAUDE.md grep for "Item 191" status returned the §13.3 row with "Priority: ELEVATED" text intact + no strikethrough — appeared OPEN. Cross-referencing §11 history rows for the same item ID surfaced "closes §13.3 Item 191" in v3.8.ajg's row. Same shape as the v3.8.akr "match-count is not consumer-count" case study: a single source (§13.3 row text) appeared authoritative but was stale relative to the actual canonical source (§11 history rows are the source of truth for closure status; §13.3 backlog rows can drift if not maintained in lockstep). **Going-forward gate:** when summarizing §13.3 OPEN items, cross-reference every candidate against `grep "closes.*Item N\|§13\.3 Item N.*CLOSED"` in §11 before declaring open. Awaits two more independent fires of "backlog-row-text-drift" before §19 canonical promotion per sub-rule c three-fire convention. **Root-cause characterization (now three-fire-validated):** Prisma's `migrate deploy` acquires a Postgres advisory lock (hardcoded `72707369` in Prisma source) before applying migrations. Lock is session-scoped — released only when the connection holding it actually closes. Today's `DATABASE_URL` env var on Render points at Neon's POOLED endpoint (hostname contains `-pooler`), which intentionally keeps connections alive between requests and rotates PIDs across the pool. Net effect: migrate process exits normally, but its lock-holder connection stays cached in Neon's pooler. Lock doesn't release until Neon's idle timer expires that specific cached PID (~5min on Launch tier). Every subsequent `migrate deploy` plays roulette against whichever pooler-cached PID currently holds the lock. P1002 frequency correlates with migration-bearing deploy frequency. **Permanent fix — canonical Prisma + Neon pattern documented by both vendors:** split runtime + migrate connection URLs. (a) `backend/prisma/schema.prisma` `datasource db { ... }` block adds `directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")` line alongside existing `url = env("DATABASE_URL")`. (b) Render dashboard env var added: `DIRECT_URL` = Neon's direct endpoint connection string (no `-pooler` in hostname; obtained from Neon dashboard → Connection Details → "Direct connection" tab). (c) Local `backend/.env` adds the same `DIRECT_URL` for `prisma migrate dev` (when used in feature branches) + diagnostic `prisma migrate status` runs. (d) `DATABASE_URL` UNCHANGED — runtime continues to benefit from pooler's connection-limit management. Prisma automatically uses `directUrl` for ALL migrate operations (`migrate deploy`, `migrate dev`, `migrate status`, `migrate resolve`, `db push`) when present in the datasource block. Direct connection releases the advisory lock the moment migrate exits — no pooler caching layer between Prisma and Postgres. **Belt-and-suspenders secondary hardening (same sprint, ~5 min add):** `PRISMA_MIGRATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT=60000` env var on Render bumps Prisma's lock-acquisition timeout from 10s default to 60s. Reduces residual P1002 frequency on the direct URL itself (e.g. if Render somehow runs two concurrent deploys, which would normally serialize). **Side benefits beyond P1002 elimination:** (i) `prisma migrate status` becomes deterministic — currently it also runs through the pooler and can give stale answers about applied-vs-pending migrations; (ii) the Sprint 44b `prisma migrate status --exit-code` post-deploy verification gate becomes reliable instead of probabilistic; (iii) future destructive migrations (enum-swaps like v3.8.ajd, column-drops, table-renames) become safer because the lock is held by a connection that genuinely owns the migration. **Risks considered + rejected:** (a) `PRISMA_SCHEMA_DISABLE_ADVISORY_LOCK=1` env var — disables the lock entirely, allowing two concurrent migrate processes to apply destructive migrations simultaneously; an enum-swap class migration could corrupt under concurrent application; not recommended. (b) Pre-deploy SQL hook running `pg_advisory_unlock(72707369)` — race condition with legitimate concurrent migrations; would also fail if the lock-holder is a different PID than the unlock caller; not recommended. (c) Switching off Neon to RDS / Supabase / another managed Postgres — over-engineering for this specific class; the same pooler vs direct distinction exists on most managed Postgres providers and is solved the same way. **Sprint shape:** ~10 LOC schema change + 2 env var additions (Render dashboard + local `.env`) + 1 CLAUDE.md §2.2 documentation update noting the new env vars + their roles. Effort: 30-60 min, mostly Neon dashboard navigation + Render env editing. No migration. No code logic change. **Pre-commit verification:** `npx prisma migrate status` against direct URL should report `Database schema is up to date` before push. Post-deploy: next migration-bearing deploy should complete in <5s without P1002 even if a prior deploy was recent. **Priority:** ELEVATED — every future schema migration is at risk until this lands. Pairs naturally with §13.3 Item 8.10's deploy-chain hardening lineage (Sprint 44a → 44b → 44c → 44d) as the natural next architectural-hardening sprint. **Banked methodology observation:** Sprint 44b's baseline-reset + canonical buildCommand work hardened the migration history + verification gate but did NOT address the connection-URL split. The class of bug was latent through the entire Sprint 44 → ajf arc; three independent fires in <2 weeks validated the recurrence rate as material enough to justify the architectural fix vs continuing to absorb the manual-retry cost. **v3.8.alf follow-up note (2026-05-26):** ledger reconciliation sprint for the v3.8.ale citext migration surfaced two related docs-completeness gaps in this item's canonical work: (1) local `backend/.env` was missing `DIRECT_URL` despite §2.2 calling for it as canonical local-dev configuration — v3.8.alf added it via [`backend/scripts/add-direct-url-to-env.ts`](backend/scripts/add-direct-url-to-env.ts) which derives the direct URL from the existing pooled DATABASE_URL by stripping `-pooler`. (2) [render.yaml](render.yaml) `envVars` block listed `DATABASE_URL` only — not `DIRECT_URL` or `PRISMA_MIGRATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT`. Per the file's own header note render.yaml is documentation-only (Render dashboard is the live config), and per the `check-direct-url.js` guard in the buildCommand at render.yaml:29 + the fact that deploys have been succeeding since v3.8.ajg/ajr/ajs, the Render dashboard IS set correctly. render.yaml just lagged. v3.8.alf added both env vars to the envVars docs block with explanatory inline comments. Lesson banking — when a schema datasource changes env-var requirements (the ajg `directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")` shift), the four-location checklist from sub-pattern 11 case study #2 should explicitly include `render.yaml` envVars docs as a 5th location alongside (1) local .env (2) Render dashboard (3) CI workflow env blocks (4) CLAUDE.md §2.2. Future schema env() additions catch this gap via the extended checklist.

192. ~~**Risk-flagging cron re-enablement with preference gate + threshold tuning + test-load exclusion.**~~ **FULLY CLOSED 2026-05-30 across v3.8.ali (mechanism + kill switch) + v3.8.alj (test-load exclusion + per-user preference + cron re-enable).** The cron is LIVE again as of v3.8.alj. **v3.8.alj final-close shipped:** (1) **Test-load exclusion** — new `Load.isTestAccount Boolean @default(false)` (migration `20260530140000_add_load_is_test_account`, additive, no backfill). (2) **Staleness guard** — `runRiskFlagging` findMany also filters `pickupDate: { gte: now - 14 days }`. This cleanly excludes the existing prod flood loads (SRL-20260211/03/16-dated seed loads, Feb 2026 pickups, 3+ months past today) WITHOUT identifying them individually — no risky prod backfill. The in-app notification is NOT gated — preference governs the external email only, same as the per-load kill switch. AE toggles via new `PATCH /api/loads/:id/risk-email-mute` (AE-role-gated, `validateBody({ muted: boolean })`, audit-logged) surfaced as a Bell/BellOff button in the T&T `LoadDetailDrawer` header next to the status-advance button. (2) **Once-per-load-per-level cadence** (ratified — the actual flood-killer): `runRiskFlagging` now reads the PRIOR `RiskLog` level before writing the new one and alerts ONLY on a level CROSSING (`risk.level !== prevLevel`). A load that sits at RED now never re-emails; it fires once on the crossing into RED and stays silent until the level actually changes. `RiskLog` still writes every tick (dashboard history intact); `notified` flag now reflects whether THIS tick alerted (level-crossing into non-GREEN), not merely non-GREEN. Re-enable is a deliberate go-live decision (§3.4 halt > ship on outward-facing email), NOT a side effect — recommend bundling (a)+(b)+(c) as the final v3.8.al-something re-enable sprint once a test-load-marking strategy is decided. **Original banking-row continues below for the full pre-v3.8.ali context:** Pre-disable state: `runRiskFlagging` ([riskEngine.ts:96](backend/src/services/riskEngine.ts#L96)) ran every 30 min at `:05`/`:35`, iterated all loads in active statuses (POSTED → AT_DELIVERY), scored each via 5 factors (unassigned-time / missed-check-calls / pickup-approaching / low-carrier-score / low-margin), and on RED (score ≥ 41) fired BOTH a `Notification` row at [riskEngine.ts:155-163](backend/src/services/riskEngine.ts#L155) AND an email via `sendRiskAlertEmail` at [riskEngine.ts:169-170](backend/src/services/riskEngine.ts#L169) to the load's `posterId`. **Why disabled:** Wasi inbox flooded with 4× "RISK RED" emails at 4:35 PM on 2026-05-25 against test/seed loads (SRL-121485/86/87 + L9180992591), all scoring 50-80 from stale "unassigned 4+ hr" + missed check calls on demo data. Three independent design gaps surfaced: (a) **no preference gate** — the Settings page at [dashboard/settings/page.tsx:94](frontend/src/app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx#L94) has a "Notification Preferences" panel with `loads/payments/scorecard/announcements` toggles that POSTs to `PATCH /auth/preferences`, but `runRiskFlagging` doesn't read `user.preferences.notifications` anywhere before sending; same architectural class as §13.3 Item 86 (broader NotificationType retrofit); (b) **no test-load exclusion** — `Load.findMany({ where: { status: in: activeStatuses } })` at [riskEngine.ts:98-101](backend/src/services/riskEngine.ts#L98) doesn't filter test loads (no `Load.isTestAccount` field yet; would need either a new column or join through `customer.isTestAccount` if shipper is test-flagged, OR through `carrier.carrierProfile.isTestAccount` via v3.8.aim Item 8.5-Build-1); (c) **30-min dedup window too tight** — same RED load re-emails every 30-min cron tick if score stays RED [RESOLVED in v3.8.ali via once-per-level cadence]. **Pairs with §13.3 Item 86** (broader NotificationType email-fan-out preference retrofit) — Item 192 is the specific RISK_ALERT slice; Item 86 is the full sweep across all 19 NotificationType enum values. **Priority:** medium — annoyance not BKN-blocking. Trade-off: noise floor vs miss-rate. Re-enable BEFORE first paid load. 193. **SRL Driver Academy epic — per-driver training portal in the carrier portal (T1 SHIPPED v3.8.amw 2026-06-12; T2 SHIPPED v3.8.amz 2026-06-15; T3 SHIPPED v3.8.ana 2026-06-15; T4 SHIPPED v3.8.anb 2026-06-15; T5 SHIPPED v3.8.anc 2026-06-15; T6 SHIPPED v3.8.and 2026-06-15; T7 SHIPPED v3.8.ane 2026-06-15 — EPIC COMPLETE T1→T7; T8+ extensions banked).** Wasi directive 2026-06-12: one-stop driver training access inside the carrier portal covering IRP, IFTA, ELD, and the full regulatory topic universe; drivers must log in with their own credentials so training completion is trackable per driver; multi-stage delivery — comprehensive audit first, then step-by-step builds. Three-agent Phase A audit (portal frontend / carrier backend / adjacent systems) confirmed: zero existing training infrastructure (clean grep), `Driver` model unlinked to carriers (closed in T1), no multi-user-per-carrier pattern anywhere (1:1 `CarrierProfile.userId`), strong reusables (SOP content+PDF precedent, Document+S3, srl-chrome certificate primitives, email `wrap()`, caravanService progress pattern, cron slots, AE carriers-page tab system). **Locked decisions (ratified 2026-06-12, do not re-litigate):** (a) **auth = training-scoped credential** — bcrypt PIN on the driver record, purpose-scoped JWT (`purpose: "driver-training"`, embeds driverId + carrierProfileId), separate `srl_token_driver` cookie, dedicated `authenticateDriver` middleware granting ONLY `/api/driver-training/*`; NO new UserRole, NO User rows for drivers (User.email unique-citext makes email-keyed driver accounts wrong-shape — many drivers lack email); mirrors the tenderAction purpose-token precedent; (b) **identity = phone + PIN** — carrier enters driver mobile at roster-add (T1 made phone required for exactly this), SMS invite via existing OpenPhone `sendSMS`, driver sets PIN; (c) **content = seed-first** — Claude drafts 3-5 courses in markdown (recommend: ELD/HOS, IFTA, IRP, detention documentation, fraud awareness), Wasi reviews, ships as seeded rows; AE authoring UI deferred to T7; (d) **name = "SRL Driver Academy"** — no §7 Caravan-naming conflict. **Sprint sequence (each atomic per §3.3, halt + sign-off between):** ~~T1 roster foundation~~ SHIPPED v3.8.amw. ~~**T2 driver auth**~~ **SHIPPED v3.8.amz** (2026-06-15): credential fields + invite flow (SMS magic-link + copy-link fallback → set PIN) + `/driver/login`/`/driver/set-pin`/`/driver/dashboard` + purpose-scoped invite & session JWTs (`lib/driverToken.ts`) + `srl_token_driver` cookie + `authenticateDriver` (Driver lookup, not User) + rate limiting + per-driver lockout. **Design note (differs from the original plan):** `authenticateDriver` reads `srl_token_driver` DIRECTLY and does NOT route through the shared User-based cookie resolver — so a `DRIVER_PORTAL_MOUNTS` entry in `resolveCookieCandidates` was deliberately NOT added (it would be dead code; the shared resolver only runs for `authenticate()` routes, which driver routes never use). Driver-cookie isolation is achieved by (a) the separate `authenticateDriver` middleware + (b) the shared `tryAuthenticateToken` now rejecting any `purpose`-bearing/non-userId token. **T2 security hardening (post adversarial-review, 27 findings):** constant-time enumeration-safe login, multi-carrier same-phone PIN-match-across-candidates, atomic set-pin, single-use invite (blacklist-on-consume), set-pin/invite rate limiters, weak-PIN rejection. **T2 banked platform-wide follow-ups (from the review — NOT T2-blocking, deferred as cross-cutting hardening):** (1) **separate JWT secret per token-class** (or RS256) — today all tokens share `JWT_SECRET`; purpose-claim isolation holds, but a secret leak forges any class. Platform-wide. (2) **`TokenBlacklist.userId` is a dead, FK-less column** — unused by `isTokenBlacklisted`/`cleanupBlacklist`; refactor `blacklistToken(token, reason)` to drop it (touches auth.ts + carrierAuth.ts + driverAuth.ts). 194. **Project-wide audit (2026-06-18) — prioritized findings + greenlight sprints.** A 9-dimension audit Workflow (security / data / backend / frontend / test-coverage / Driver-Academy / ops-scale / brand / backlog) produced **91 findings (P0=7, P1=30, P2=38, P3=16)**, each corroborated against actual code before banking (several agent findings were over-rated or stale — see corrections below). The **safe additive quick-wins shipped in v3.8.anh** (e2e-token NODE_ENV hard-404, chatbot score-tier ban, CDL roster label, loadStateMachine 16-case test). The items below are the **greenlight-needed sprints** (deletions / migrations / risky wiring / multi-file refactors the audit surfaced; per §3.4 + the harness "didn't-create-it → surface" rule they were NOT auto-applied). Pick deliberately.

   **A — Correctness (highest leverage).** (A1) **Item 159 Sprint-2 — wire `validateLoadStatusTransition` into the 10 unguarded AE-side `Load.status` write sites** ([`ediService.ts`](backend/src/services/ediService.ts), [`geofenceService.ts`](backend/src/services/geofenceService.ts) (hardcoded rules → delete + delegate), [`instantBookService.ts`](backend/src/services/instantBookService.ts) (unconditional `BOOKED`), [`fallOffRecovery.ts`](backend/src/services/fallOffRecovery.ts), [`waterfallEngineService.ts`](backend/src/services/waterfallEngineService.ts) (3 sites), [`loadBids.ts`](backend/src/routes/loadBids.ts), [`shipperNotificationService.ts`](backend/src/services/shipperNotificationService.ts), [`integrationService.ts`](backend/src/services/integrationService.ts)). The validator EXISTS + is unit-tested (v3.8.anh); these sites can currently create illegal transitions (BOOKED→DELIVERED skip, etc.). **Recommended rollout: log-only first** (emit a WARNING on `!allowed` without blocking) for one deploy cycle to surface real in-practice violations, THEN flip to enforce — avoids breaking a legit-but-untabled transition. Medium-large. This is the §13.3 Item 159 Sprint-2 epic, now scoped + de-risked.

   **B — Test coverage (P0/P1 cluster; ~11% service / ~27% controller coverage today).** Highest-risk UNTESTED surfaces, in priority order: (B1) **payment + settlement** (`settlementController` createSettlement/finalizeSettlement/markPaid transaction atomicity + deduction aggregation; `carrierPayController` quick-pay discount math); (B2) **waterfall engine** state machine (buildWaterfall 12-position cap + DAT fallback, position queued→tendered→accepted/declined/expired/skipped, expireStalePositions cron); (B3) **carrier vetting / compliance gating** (`carrierVettingController.runFullVetting` 8-check orchestration + error isolation, `chameleonDetectionService` fingerprint scoring); (B4) **Driver Academy** (the v3.8.anf/ang surfaces — `getCdlEligibility` edge cases, `buildCarrierTrainingSummary` expiry math, quiz grading, cert generation); (B5) **invoice generation** (autoGenerateInvoice happy/zero-rate/duplicate); (B6) **RBAC authority checks** across critical controllers (ADMIN-only with CARRIER token → 403, etc.); (B7) **E2E expansion** beyond the single lifecycle path (settlement, waterfall expiry, Academy). Each is small-medium; sequence B1→B4 first.

(C3) AE-tool HTML comments leak "Wasi" to public-facing files (P1, trivial once C1/C2 resolved).

   **D — Data integrity.** (D1) **Dual status enums** — `CarrierProfile.status` vs `onboardingStatus` (divergent meanings; audit which is consulted, deprecate the other) + `ShipmentStatus` (8 values) vs `LoadStatus` (18) gap (§13.3 Item 160). (D3) **missing composite indexes** on hot paths — `ComplianceScan[carrierId, scannedAt]`, `RateConfirmation[loadId, status]`, `Invoice[status, dueDate]`, etc. Additive migration, safe, real perf win (verify columns + absence first).    **E — Ops / scale (P1, emerge above ~50 carriers).** (E1) **Fire-and-forget email has no failure tracking / DLQ** — add an `EmailQueue` model (status/resendId/error/retryCount) so a failed Resend send is visible + retryable (the v3.8.amv `sales@` suppression class would have been caught by this). (E2) **Sentry DSN unset** — Sentry is wired (`enabled:!!SENTRY_DSN`) but no DSN in env → zero error telemetry in prod; set `SENTRY_DSN` (needs the actual DSN from Wasi). (E3) **FMCSA daily scan has no batching/backoff** — fine at <50 carriers (serial, 1h cache) but add resumable batching before scale. (E4) **Synchronous PDF generation on the request path** (RC/BOL/cert downloads block the response) — extract to a job/202-accept pattern at volume. (E5) **DB pool size** review for concurrent cron + request load.

Needs an audience decision (carrier-self-with-ownership vs AE-on-behalf) THEN the right gate; NOT a blind `authorize` (would break the carrier-response intent). Small once decided. (F2) **Carrier portal session timeout 45 min vs shipper 60 min** — undocumented divergence ([frontend auth guards]); confirm intentional or unify. Trivial. (F3) **Forced-sequential lesson player is client-only** — a driver can POST `/driver-training/courses/:slug/quiz` without reading lessons (the CDL gate IS server-enforced; the read-through is not). Per Wasi's spec the sequence is a UX convention; if it must be enforced, gate quiz on `lessonsCompleted >= lessonCount` server-side (weak — progress is client-reported — but raises the bar). Decision-required. (F4) **Cross-carrier course scope** — courses are platform-shared (no per-carrier variant); document this in the carrier/driver UI so a carrier doesn't assume private content (§13.3 Item 193 locked this as by-design; just needs the UI note). Trivial.
