**Production reliability — hotfix (logged + closed 2026-05-06 in v3.8.aaf, Sprint 26b):**

32. ~~**Load Board click-to-detail React error #31 crash on loads with accessorials.**~~ **CLOSED 2026-05-06 in v3.8.aaf** (Sprint 26b hotfix between Sprint 26 close and Sprint 27 start). Surfaced during Sprint 26 Phase C smoke (creating test load via Order Builder → clicking load on Load Board → page crashed with full-screen "Something went wrong" + React error #31 "Objects are not valid as a React child"). Root cause: JSON column shape mismatch on `Load.accessorials`. Order Builder writes `Array<{type, amount, payer}>` per the [`Accessorial`](frontend/src/app/dashboard/orders/types.ts#L90) interface; convert-to-load endpoint at [`backend/src/routes/orders.ts:455`](backend/src/routes/orders.ts#L455) writes the form's array verbatim to the JSON column. Load Board side panel at [`loads/page.tsx:1030-1036`](frontend/src/app/dashboard/loads/page.tsx#L1030) (pre-fix) iterated `load.accessorials` with `key={a}` and rendered `{a}` directly — assuming `string[]` not `object[]`. React threw error #31 with the object's keys (type, amount, payer) in the error args. Latent since v3.8.c (Order Builder convert flow shipped ~Apr 28). Pre-commit tsc passed every sprint because the Zod validator at [`backend/src/validators/load.ts:113`](backend/src/validators/load.ts#L113) is `z.array(z.any()).optional()` — type-system can't catch JSON-column shape mismatches. **Trigger conditions** (all three required): load created via Order Builder convert flow, user added at least one accessorial before converting, user clicks the load on Load Board to open side panel. Loads without accessorials don't trigger (render gated on `length > 0`); loads created via Load Board's `+ New Load` 4-step modal don't trigger (no accessorial entry surface). **Fix shape — F2 per audit:** render `accessorial.type` with optional ` ($amount)` suffix. Defensive type-check handles three input shapes: `typeof a === "string"` (legacy data compat for any pre-v3.8.c string-only records) → render `a`; object with `type` key → render `"${a.type}${a.amount ? ` ($${a.amount})` : ""}"`; fallback → literal `"Accessorial"`. React `key` switched from `key={a}` (would have collided on repeat types) to `key={i}` (array index, stable for purely-visual list with no reorder). **Adjacent risk sweep cleared** (Phase A): Load model has 4 JSON columns total — stops (1112), accessorials (1146 — this bug), additionalRefs (1225), datPostedFields (1254). Only `accessorials` was rendered as a React child on the Load Board page; other JSON columns either aren't read or aren't rendered as children. One-finding fix, not class-wide cleanup. **Out of scope (deferred):** tightening Zod validator at `validators/load.ts:113` from `z.array(z.any())` to `z.array(z.object({type, amount, payer}))` — separate sprint; doesn't prevent future render-side bugs, just data-side. Audit of other JSON-column render sites across the codebase — broader audit sprint. **Pre-commit verification:** backend `tsc --noEmit` clean (no backend changes; verifying nothing drifted), frontend `next build` clean. Net LOC change: ~10 (1 file, accessorials block rewritten with defensive type-check + index keying). Per §3.1 sequence-continuous rule: v3.8.aae → v3.8.aaf. Hotfix-with-immediate-close pattern (logged + closed in same commit) — used because the bug blocked Sprint 26 Phase C smoke verification. **Severity: P0** — every BOL printed in the system embeds a QR code that routes customers to a 404 when scanned. Same defect class affects email tracking links sent via `shipperLoadNotifyService`. **Smoking gun:** [`backend/src/utils/qrGenerator.ts:25`](backend/src/utils/qrGenerator.ts#L25) encodes URL `https://silkroutelogistics.ai/track/<12-char-token>`. Frontend has NO `/track/[token]/page.tsx` dynamic route ([`frontend/src/app/track/`](frontend/src/app/track/) contains only `page.tsx`, no `[token]` subdirectory). [`frontend/public/_redirects`](frontend/public/_redirects) has no `/track/*` splat rule. [`frontend/next.config.ts:5`](frontend/next.config.ts#L5) sets `output: "export"` (static HTML export — Cloudflare Pages serves static files only, no SSR fallback). Net result: Cloudflare Pages serves default 404 for any `/track/<anything>` path. **Email path same defect:** [`backend/src/services/shipperLoadNotifyService.ts:48`](backend/src/services/shipperLoadNotifyService.ts#L48) builds `${PORTAL_BASE}/tracking/${load.trackingToken}`. `_redirects` line 27 redirects `/tracking` (exact) → `/track` 301, but no rule for `/tracking/*` subpaths — 404 on the same Cloudflare Pages fallback. **Fix surface options:** (a) Add `frontend/src/app/track/[token]/page.tsx` dynamic route that reads `params.token` from path, auto-fills the search box, and auto-fires the API call on mount. Cleanest UX. Requires new file ~50-80 LOC + import path updates. (b) Add `_redirects` splat: `/track/* /track 200` (URL-rewrite, not 301) + read token from `useSearchParams` or `usePathname` on the existing static page; would require URL-param plumbing on the existing page. (c) Belt-and-suspenders: both. Plus `_redirects` rule `/tracking/* /track/:splat 301` to align email links with QR pattern. **Recommend (a) + email-link rewrite** — dynamic route handles QR pattern, separate email change makes `shipperLoadNotifyService` build `/track/<token>` instead of `/tracking/<token>` to consolidate on one URL pattern. **Verification:** after fix, scan a printed BOL QR with phone camera → should auto-load tracking page with token-driven results (no manual entry). Test with at least one ShipperTrackingToken from prod DB to confirm round-trip. **Discovery context:** Sprint 25 was scoped to contrast fix + 3-tab → 2-tab reduction on `/track`. The BOL QR 404 was an adjacent finding from auditing the data-model parity (where do "Tracking codes" come from, who distributes them) — turns out the answer is "they come from QR codes that don't work." **Bumps queue:** P0 production reliability outranks remaining brand polish work — recommend slotting this ahead of `/shippers` narrative work and other §13.3 items not currently blocking. **Effort estimate:** medium sprint, ~80-150 LOC (new dynamic route + URL-param plumbing + email link consolidation). Pairs naturally with §13.3 Item 6 (Portal Approval UI S-3) only insofar as both are customer-facing surface defects; otherwise standalone.

197. **Carrier lifecycle Arc 3 (2026-08-19) — deployed, TONU ledger, dispute fix, graded Pass 1.** Baseline `274249e8`; **deployed through `274249e8`**. Write-up appended to [`docs/audits/carrier-lifecycle-audit.md`](docs/audits/carrier-lifecycle-audit.md).

    **Phase 1 — deployed, column before code.** Migration run first against a **fresh Postgres 16 container** — the whole 39-migration chain from empty, not `db push`: clean, `tonuFaultSide` present as nullable text, `migrate status` up to date. Then production Neon per §2.2, verified directly: `information_schema` shows the column and `_prisma_migrations` shows the row with `applied_steps_count: 1`. Code pushed only after, so the column was never behind the code that reads it. **Smoke reported honestly:** the TONU 422 gate, the POD-cron registration and the carrier check-call close all need an authenticated session this environment does not have, and credentials were not fabricated to manufacture a green tick. Verified instead: `PATCH /api/loads/:id/status` returns a clean `401` (live, not 500-ing), `/api/health` 200, and `POST /api/auth/e2e-token` **404s in production** — the v3.8.anh hardening holds, so there is no bypass to borrow.

    **Phase 2 (`5b42271a` v3.8.asp) — the TONU obligation reaches the ledger.** Both legs are ONE `LoadAccessorial` row, because that is the existing architecture: `unbilledCustomerAccessorials` drops any row not billed to SHIPPER, while `approvedAccessorials` reads the same row and does not filter on `billedTo` at all. CUSTOMER → amount/null/SHIPPER (bills customer, pays carrier); BROKER → amount/0/BROKER (pays carrier out of margin, bills nobody); CARRIER → no row, existing reversal stands. **Ordering pinned per 2c:** `onLoadCancelledOrTONU` never touches `LoadAccessorial` and is fire-and-forget from loadController, so the ledger is the only anchor that cannot be raced — a test asserts no CarrierPay/Invoice write on this path. Idempotent on (loadId, TONU, status != REJECTED); REJECTED excluded so a thrown-out charge can be re-recorded. **Activation still banked, for a specific reason:** a TONU load has neither money document — `syncInvoiceAccessorials` needs a BASE invoice, `syncCarrierPayAccessorials` needs a CarrierPay, and the reversal voids any that existed. Calling `autoGenerateInvoice` would bill the customer the full linehaul for a truck that never moved, and a bespoke TONU invoice is the parallel plumbing the design avoids. A "settle a TONU" surface is a product decision.

    **Phase 3 (`7c4adf28` v3.8.asq) — the dispute Resolve button had never worked.** Scoped as "build MISSING-UI"; the first trace found a live bug instead — the page POSTed to `/accounting/disputes/:id/resolve` and only a PUT exists, so **every click 404'd**, and it sent `{ resolution }` where the controller reads `{ resolutionNotes }`. Investigate and Propose wired for the first time, making the INVESTIGATING state the controller enforces reachable at all. Approve/Deny split into two buttons because `resolveDispute` reads `approved !== false` — one button could only ever approve. **Priority list corrected against the code:** invoice mark-paid needed nothing (accounting/invoices already calls the accounting PUT; the Pass 1 finding was the DUPLICATE PATCH route, already classified as such). Invoice line-items edit remains unbuilt.

    **Phase 5 (`d233fddf`, unversioned) — Pass 1 grades its evidence.** v1's substring rule read `action: "deactivate"` as absent, so two live endpoints sat on an orphan list through a whole triage pass. v2 matches SEGMENTS against the caller tail, either side allowed dynamic, graded EXACT / PATTERN / UNRESOLVED. The first v2 run was *worse* than v1 — `/:id/deactivate` matched any two-segment caller and attributed carrier-drivers to a customer-contacts call; a wrong caller reads as evidence, so PATTERN now also requires the caller to look aimed at the route's own mount, and the most specific caller wins. **26 binary orphans → 17 UNRESOLVED / 9 PATTERN / 73 EXACT**, both false positives correctly attributed, and the Phase 3 dispute routes dropped off as EXACT — the tool independently confirming that work.

    **Phase 4 — BANKED, with the reason.** Pass 4 carries the same defect Phase 5 just fixed in Pass 1: it flags any `.map(...)`, including state updaters rather than list renders. At least 6 of the 14 are not rows at all — `onChange(lessons.map(...))` is literally the edit affordance, `form.stops.map(s => s.id === id ? ... : s)` is an update reducer. Triaging those as "an AE cannot correct their data" would be triaging noise. **Resume state:** fix Pass 4's matcher first (require the `.map()` to sit inside JSX and render a row), then triage survivors — the real-looking candidates are TagManagementPanel assignments, tagging-rules rules, orders customerTemplates, documents filtered, and admin/monitoring audit entries.

    **Counters.** Pass 1 26 → **17 UNRESOLVED** (+9 PATTERN, 73 EXACT). Pass 2 511 → **508** — the disputes UI now references `investigationNotes`, `proposedResolution` and `proposedAmount`. Pass 4 14 → 14. Backend suite 632 → **641**. Frontend tsc + next build clean throughout; the `urlSafety` DNS red is sandbox-only and passed in CI on both `2b76cc93` and `274249e8`.

198. **CI-gated Render deploys (2026-08-19, v3.8.asv) — code-complete, pending three dashboard steps.** Render auto-deploys on push to `main` and does not read GitHub Actions, so a commit whose CI fails still reaches production. Demonstrated the same day: `67dd1c41` pushed 12:49:24, **deployed by Render 12:51:05**, CI **failed** on it 12:51:17. Harmless in that instance (a dead export caught by the reachability gate, no behaviour change, endpoint verified before and after) but the path is indifferent to whether the breakage is harmless.

    **Shipped:** a `deploy` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `needs: [backend, frontend]`, push-to-`main` only (never a PR), POSTs the hook from `RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL`, **fails loudly if that secret is unset** rather than skipping, and treats a non-2xx from Render as failure. **Not gated on E2E, deliberately:** that job hung 6h02m on a Playwright browser download the same day, and gating deploys on it would have blocked every deploy for the window over an infrastructure hang unrelated to the code. [`backend/__tests__/unit/ci/deployGate.test.ts`](backend/__tests__/unit/ci/deployGate.test.ts) pins the needs list against `e2e` — verified by temporarily adding it and confirming only that assertion fails — so a later "make the gate stricter" change fails CI rather than quietly reintroducing the hang.

    **PENDING — three dashboard steps, Wasi only, order matters:** (1) create the deploy hook in the Render dashboard, (2) add it as GitHub secret `RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL` and confirm the deploy job goes green, (3) **only then** turn Render auto-deploy off. Doing (3) before (2) leaves a window where nothing deploys at all. Full checklist with verification, rollback, and the break-glass path for deploying during an incident: [`docs/internal/render-deploy-gate-setup.md`](docs/internal/render-deploy-gate-setup.md).

    **Interim state is safe and deliberate:** with auto-deploy still on and the secret absent, Render deploys exactly as it does today and the deploy job fails visibly on every push. Degraded loudly, not silently — the same principle the job itself enforces about the missing secret.

    **Note for whoever migrates to a Blueprint:** `render.yaml` is documentation-only (§2.2) — the live service `srv-d64iqtffte5s73894h8g` was created by hand in the dashboard, so auto-deploy cannot be flipped from the repo. That is why step (3) is manual rather than a line in this commit.

199. **Arc 4 (2026-08-19) — Sub-pattern 5 swept repo-wide; signature version lifecycle traced, detection shipped, enforcement banked.**

    **Phase 1 — CLOSED (`1b6d1e49` v3.8.asw).** [`scripts/audit-schema-drift.ts`](backend/scripts/audit-schema-drift.ts) diffs each `validateBody` schema's declared keys against every key its handler reads off `req.body`, across all 71 validated routes. **Two drift bugs.** (a) `resetPasswordSchema` never declared `totpCode`, which `authController.resetPassword` gates on for TOTP users — so a TOTP-enabled user could not have reset their password; the frontend was already correct (`ResetPasswordForm.tsx:62` resends after `requires2FA`) and handed the value to a schema that discarded it, so the retry would have got the same answer forever. **Classification: LATENT — NEVER FIRED.** A read-only production diagnostic (2026-08-19) found `TOTP_ENABLED_COUNT: 1` — the `whaider@` ADMIN account, of 11 users total — and `RESET_TOKENS_TOTAL: 0`, meaning no password-reset token has ever existed for any user. Live 2026-02-23 (`172d6f3b`, the security-hardening commit that added the gate) → 2026-08-19, reachable by one account, exercised zero times. Read it as **lockout prevented**, not outage: the first person to hit it would have been the sole admin, most plausibly while already locked out. Diagnostic method — resets leave no record anywhere (see Item 200), so the only trace is `OtpCode` rows with the `RESET:` prefix. (b) `updateCarrierSchema` (routes/carriers.ts:50 — a *different* schema from the registration one) never declared the four insurance `*Effective` fields that `updateCarrier` reads, added to writer and registration in v3.8.aiw but not here. **Now a CI gate** (`--strict`, beside the reachability gate): 39 clean, 0 undeclared-read, 22 declared-unread (advisory), 8 unresolvable. Opt-out is `// schema-drift-ok: <reason>`. **The scanner was wrong three times before it was right** — outer brace in the first key segment (45 false findings), comments parsed as code (the comment explaining the tonuFaultSide P0 made it report tonuFaultSide as undeclared), and schemas keyed by bare name so a generic `createSchema` resolved to another file's definition. Every finding was verified against source before being called real. Guard adversarially verified; **the first verification attempt was a false pass** because the string replace silently didn't match — a verification that doesn't verify is the same failure as a test that doesn't run.

    **Phase 2 — Phase A trace COMPLETE, detection shipped (`7437f8ce`), enforcement BANKED.** Trace confirmed the core defect: `complianceCheck` accepts any SIGNED broker-carrier agreement **regardless of version** (`complianceMonitorService.ts:270-278` filters templateName + status, orders by signedAt, never reads `version`), so bumping `BCA_VERSION` reaches nobody who already signed. [`lib/agreementVersions.ts`](backend/src/lib/agreementVersions.ts) ships `CURRENT_VERSIONS` (keyed on `templateName`, so a new document type is a registry line + constant, **no schema change** — proven by a test registering a synthetic NOA type) and `assessVersions` returning drifted vs missing, deliberately distinguished because *missing means sign, drifted means re-sign*.

    **Enforcement banked for three traced reasons, not caution:** (1) **the paper does not ask for it** — the BCA has no amendment or re-consent clause; the only notice period either document states is §244's 30 days, governing Caravan *program criteria*, not the agreement body. Forcing re-signature is a policy SRL would be **adopting**, not a right it holds — Wasi's and counsel's call, especially with §16 #1 open. (2) **gating without a re-consent surface locks carriers out** — a version bump is a one-constant commit; ship the gate with it and every signed carrier drifts on that deploy and hard-blocks at grace expiry with no in-portal path to re-sign. (3) **the RC is the weakest link and is unversioned** — it records `signed`, `signedAt`, `signedUrl`, `carrierSignature` (a name), with **no IP, no user agent, no version**, while BCA and QP each capture typed name + IP + UA + version + executed PDF. The per-load document governing a haul carries weaker evidence than the masters, and a dispute cannot establish which terms governed that load.

    **RESUME STATE — Phase 2 remainder.** 2a enforcement: add version comparison at `complianceMonitorService.ts:270-278` using `assessVersions`, with a distinct blocked_code (**not** the missing-BCA message — the carrier HAS a BCA, an outdated one, and the message must say re-sign). 2b re-consent surface: portal banner + grace interstitial reusing `POST /carrier-auth/sign-bca` (Arc 1 verified it re-records to a new version idempotently), banded reminder emails on the `podReminderService` link-encoded-dedup pattern, AE notification on grace entry/exit. 2c drift cron: daily job calling `assessVersions` per carrier. 2d: RC executed-artifact parity with `generateAgreementBuffer`. **Prerequisite for the per-load half: a `version` column on RateConfirmation stamped at generation, plus IP/UA on acceptance to match the BCA standard — schema change, should land alone.**

    **Phase 3 (Item 159 A1 log-first) and Phase 4 (Pass 2 triage) — NOT STARTED, banked.** Phase 3's shape is unchanged from Item 194's investigation: wrap the AE-side `Load.status` write sites in log-only mode, instrument the known divergences (`geofenceService`'s more-permissive map, `instantBookService`'s unconditional BOOKED) rather than fixing them, and let the data decide. Phase 4 needs Pass 2 upgraded first — backend-read checking and category tagging — before triage is anything but noise.


200. **Arc 5 (2026-08-19) — the auth-event blind spot, closed.**

    **The gap.** Answering "did anyone hit the broken reset path" (Item 199) took a production query because **password-reset attempts are recorded nowhere**. Neither `resetPassword` nor `forgotPassword` logs; neither route carries `auditLog` middleware; and `auditMiddleware` misses on all three of its conditions — `skipPaths` contains `/api/auth` ([`auditTrail.ts:45`](backend/src/middleware/auditTrail.ts#L45)), it only records 2xx, and it requires `req.user`. A reset is unauthenticated and the broken path returned 400. So the events a lockout postmortem or a fraud investigation most needs are exactly the ones structurally excluded from every record the platform keeps. The sole trace was an `OtpCode` row with the `RESET:` prefix, which says a reset was *requested* and nothing about whether it succeeded.

    **Shipped (`v3.8.asx`).** [`lib/authEvents.ts`](backend/src/lib/authEvents.ts) — `logAuthEvent(event, fields)` over a closed `AuthEvent` union (free-text names are what make log lines ungreppable six months on) with a `reason` classification separate from the deliberately-vague response copy. Seven call sites across the reset and TOTP-challenge paths. **Log lines, not a table** — these events frequently have no authenticated user (a reset for an unknown email, a failed login) and `AuditTrail` is user-keyed; no new tables.

    **Identity convention matched, not invented.** `userId` when known — [`carrierAuth.ts:240/341/429`](backend/src/routes/carrierAuth.ts#L240) log `{ err, userId }` and never a raw email. A 16-char sha256 prefix when the subject is an email with no user behind it, the construction already at [`carrierController.ts:52`](backend/src/controllers/carrierController.ts#L52). A log dump therefore never becomes a mailing list, and a support ticket is still correlatable by asking the user to reproduce.

    **Two-layer secret guard, adversarially verified in three rounds.** The helper has no parameter for a token, code, or password; a test greps the call sites so it stays that way. Round 1 (`totpCode` shorthand) was caught. **Round 2 was not** — `ip: resetToken` passed, because `\btoken` finds no word boundary inside camelCase `resetToken`. The guard was strengthened rather than the injection weakened: an allowlist of keys (mirroring `AuthEventFields`) plus a substring scan of identifiers with string literals stripped. Round 3 (`resetUrl` — the reset token embedded in a query string, containing no forbidden substring) is caught by the allowlist and would have been missed by the value scan, which is why both layers exist.

    **The observability guarantee is load-bearing, and the first cut broke it.** `logAuthEvent` never throws — but the first version took `ip: extractClientIp(req)`, and arguments evaluate *before* the callee, so extraction ran outside the try and a request with no `headers` threw straight through, turning a clean 400 into a 500. **The pre-existing v3.7.m reset suite went 8-of-9 red and caught it** — an independent oracle written long before this change, which is exactly why "prove no response changed" is run against the old suite rather than a new one. Extraction moved inside the guarantee; the helper takes `req`. IP is enrichment, so failing to resolve one drops the field, never the event.

    **Not touched:** the raw email embedded in the existing `SECURITY` `SystemLog` message text at [`authController.ts:239`](backend/src/controllers/authController.ts#L239) (failed logins *are* captured there, inconsistently with the hashing convention above) — flagged, deliberately not silently "fixed", since it changes an existing record's shape. **Phase 3 (counsel document consolidation) did not run:** the inputs are absent — zero `.docx` anywhere in the repo and no `my-knowledge-base/raw/counsel/`. Pending a file drop; §16 #1 and #2 remain open regardless.

201. **Item 159 A1 — log-first shipped; the audit's framing was backwards, and enforcing it would have caused an outage.**

    **What the finding said.** "10 AE-side `Load.status` write sites bypass `validateLoadStatusTransition` — wire it in."

    **What tracing every site found.** There are **29** status-writing `prisma.load.update` calls, not 10 — inventory produced by a scanner rather than a grep, because `status:` with a computed value cannot be classified by eye. More importantly the named sites are largely fine: [`ediService.ts:114`](backend/src/services/ediService.ts#L114) already validates and is the reference pattern; [`integrationService.ts:1252`](backend/src/services/integrationService.ts#L1252) and [`shipperNotificationService.ts:210`](backend/src/services/shipperNotificationService.ts#L210) are guarded by an `if (load.status === "DELIVERED")` check; [`instantBookService.ts:131`](backend/src/services/instantBookService.ts#L131) only proceeds from POSTED.

    **The actual defect is the MAP, not the call sites — and it fails in the dangerous direction.** `AE_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS` omits transitions production legitimately performs:
    - `POSTED`/`TENDERED` → `DISPATCHED` at [`loadBids.ts:221`](backend/src/routes/loadBids.ts#L221) and [`waterfallEngineService.ts:492`](backend/src/services/waterfallEngineService.ts#L492) — the **§2 auto-pilot dispatch divergence**, deliberate and load-bearing (bulk accept skips the BOOKED checkpoint, and `routes/waterfalls.ts` queries `dispatchedAt` for the dispatched-today dashboards).
    - `BOOKED`/`DISPATCHED` → `POSTED` at [`fallOffRecovery.ts:57`](backend/src/services/fallOffRecovery.ts#L57) — backwards, intentional, re-posts a fallen-off load.

    So **"wire it in" would have blocked bulk dispatch and fall-off recovery.** Log-first is not caution here; it is the difference between a fix and an outage.

    **Shipped (`v3.8.asy`).** [`lib/loadTransitionObserver.ts`](backend/src/lib/loadTransitionObserver.ts) validates as AE and logs **only** rejected transitions, each tagged `expected: true|false` against a documented divergence list. Tagging is not whitelisting — expected ones are still emitted, because their frequency is the evidence that decides whether the map gains the transition or the call site changes. Grep `expected:false` for genuine surprises. A test asserts every `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` entry is *still* rejected by the map, so reconciling the map fails the test rather than leaving a comment describing a gap that closed.

    **One choke point, not 29 edits.** It hangs off the existing `$allOperations` extension in [`config/database.ts`](backend/src/config/database.ts), so it observes every status write including the dynamic ones a scanner cannot classify and any site added later — completeness being the whole point of a survey whose output decides the reconciliation. Prior status is read through the **base** client, which does not re-enter the extension. One edit to remove when enforcement replaces it.

    **Verified against a live database** (CI-shape container, never production): known divergence tagged, genuine skip flagged, clean transition silent, and — the decisive case — a violating transition **inside an interactive transaction** logged while the transaction still committed. Postgres MVCC serves the pre-transaction row rather than blocking on the lock, which is what makes reading through a second connection safe.

    **Resume state for enforcement.** Read the `expected:false` lines first: each is either a real bug or a transition nobody documented. Then decide the auto-pilot and fall-off cases — likely a distinct `AUTO`/`SYSTEM` actor rather than widening the AE map, so a human AE does not inherit skip-ahead. Only then gate. Carrier-side ([`carrierLoads.ts`](backend/src/routes/carrierLoads.ts)) and `ediService` already enforce correctly and are the pattern to copy.


202. **Pass 2 orphan-field triage — the tool was fixed before its output was trusted (`v3.8.asz`).**

    **The tool was crying wolf.** Pass 2 of [`audit-completeness.ts`](backend/scripts/audit-completeness.ts) counted references in `frontend/src` **only**, so every backend-only column — audit stamps, cron bookkeeping, denormalised mirrors — surfaced as an "orphan" beside genuinely dead ones: **506 findings, 437 of them noise**. It also contradicted the triage note in its own file header, which says to grep `backend/src` **and** `frontend/src` before bucketing anything. Now both, tagged `UNREFERENCED` (69) vs `BACKEND_ONLY` (437). The latter is reported rather than hidden, because "used but never surfaced" is occasionally a missing screen.

    **Triage: [`docs/audits/orphan-field-triage.md`](docs/audits/orphan-field-triage.md).** Every cited finding was verified independently of the scanner (`grep -rn` over both trees, 0 code refs against 1 schema declaration); it was right in every case. The findings that matter:
    - **`CarrierAgreement` cannot be terminated.** Only `SIGNED` is ever written or queried, so a signed BCA or Quick Pay agreement is signed forever. `assessVersions` (Item 199 Phase 2) judges on the latest SIGNED row and therefore assumed a termination path that does not exist. §21.1 needs it too — **withdrawn ≠ declined**, and neither is representable on the row today.
    - **The `CarrierPay` settlement document checklist is seven columns nothing reads.** The live gate is a single `Load.podVerified`, so a settlement can be finalised with a POD and no scale ticket, lumper receipt, or temp log — the last being the evidence in a reefer claim. Whether it should gate payment or merely inform the AE is a business decision; a schema implying a check that does not run is not defensible either way.
    - **`ShipperTrackingToken.accessCount` / `lastAccessedAt` are never written.** §14 narrowed the public `/track` payload (v3.8.ara) precisely because the QR outlives the paper. That reduced what a leaked link discloses without making leakage visible.
    - **`LoadAccessorial.carrierInvoiceId` is dead while `shipperInvoiceId` is load-bearing** — the customer leg knows what has been billed, the carrier leg does not. **Independently corroborated:** the reachability gate's Check 4 header comment already names this exact pair, so the observation has been sitting in the repo unactioned.

    **Nothing deleted.** The one clean candidate (three `CarrierProfile` doc-URL columns superseded by `Document` rows) is authored under [`prisma/_pending_migrations/`](backend/prisma/_pending_migrations/) — deliberately **outside** `prisma/migrations/`, because Render runs `migrate deploy` on every push, so a file placed there is *scheduled*, not pending, and would additionally drift from a `schema.prisma` that still declares the columns. It carries a row-count gate in its header: no code reference does not mean no stored value.

    **Reachability gate fixed alongside.** It has a "consumed only by tests" verdict that is a REVIEW rather than a failure, but `backend/__tests__` was absent from its corpus, so that branch could never fire for backend unit tests and a test-only export was reported DEAD instead — sending someone to delete a helper their test depends on. Same failure direction the v3.8.asc comment in that file warns about; `e2e/` was already listed, this closes the gap.

204. **Settlement document checklist — surfaced as information, gate-at-scale banked (decided 2026-08-19, `v3.8.atb`).**

    **What shipped.** The seven `CarrierPay` doc columns (`docSignedRateCon`, `docSignedBol`, `docCarrierInvoice`, `docLumperReceipt`, `docScaleTicket`, `docTempLog`, `allDocsVerified`) now render per load on `/dashboard/settlements` as an N/6 completeness indicator with a per-document tooltip. `getSettlementById` already returned them — `carrierPays` uses `include` with no `select`, so every scalar was in the payload and simply never displayed. Frontend-only; no API change.

    **What deliberately did NOT ship: a gate.** The live payment gate stays the single `Load.podVerified` boolean. Turning these seven into a precondition would change which settlements can be paid, on data nobody has been maintaining — every historical row is `false` because nothing ever wrote them. That is a business decision, not a rendering one.

    **Absent flags render "not recorded", never a red cross.** Showing 0/6 in red across every past settlement would assert a compliance failure where the truth is an unused feature. The distinction matters the first time someone reads this screen during a dispute.

    **Gate-at-scale trigger — revisit when EITHER fires:**
    - **The first claims dispute where a missing document costs money.** The temp log is the evidence in a reefer claim; the scale ticket is the evidence in an overweight fine. One of these landing is the argument for the gate, and it will arrive with a dollar figure attached.
    - **Sustained settlement volume** past the point where an AE can eyeball each one — roughly when settlements stop being individually reviewed.

    **When it fires, the order matters:** start writing the columns (nothing does today), let them populate for a period long enough that blocking on them is fair to carriers already mid-cycle, and only then gate. Gating first would block every settlement on day one.


205. **Carrier accessorial leg — the symmetry premise was wrong, and the TONU payable was the real gap (`v3.8.atc`).**

    **What the trace found.** The customer leg reaches exactly-once by MARKING rows: `shipperInvoiceId` is stamped when a line is invoiced, `unbilledCustomerAccessorials` selects on it being null, voiding clears it. The carrier leg reaches exactly-once by RECONCILING TOTALS: `syncCarrierPayAccessorials` compares the ledger total against `CarrierPay.accessorialsTotal` and acts on the delta — re-pricing in place while the settlement is open, escalating a separate payment through `ApprovalQueue` once it is committed.

    **So the carrier leg is not missing exactly-once. It has a different and complete mechanism**, and mirroring the customer's row-marking onto it would create a SECOND source of truth for "has this been paid" — the dual-status class this codebase has repeatedly had to unpick (dual suspension columns, dual onboarding status). `carrierInvoiceId` is therefore a deletion, not a gap: `git log -S "carrierInvoiceId" --all -- backend/src` returns **no commits**, so it has never been referenced in application code at any point in the repository's history. Added to the batched deletion set at [`prisma/_pending_migrations/`](backend/prisma/_pending_migrations/) with that corroboration in the header. **Not applied.**

    **The real gap, and what shipped.** `recordTonuObligation` (Arc 3) writes the TONU to the accessorial ledger correctly. On the carrier side the reader of that ledger is `syncCarrierPayAccessorials`, whose first line is `if (!pay) return`, and a `CarrierPay` is created by `createCarrierPayOnDelivery` firing from `onLoadDelivered`. **A TONU load never delivers.** The obligation had nothing to attach to, permanently. `raiseTonuCarrierPayable` creates it.

    **Ordering was the whole risk.** `onLoadCancelledOrTONU` voids every non-PAID `CarrierPay` on the load, and `loadController` invokes it fire-and-forget. A payable raised at the flip site would race that void loop and lose, intermittently — the carrier's TONU money deleted by the same event that created it. It is raised at the **end of the reversal itself**, so the order is a property of the code rather than of timing, and a test asserts both that the call sits after the void loop and that `loadController` does not call it directly.

    **Deliberate defaults, and the question held.** No Quick Pay fee: the election is per load on the rate confirmation, a load that never ran has none, and §8 makes standard tier pay free — charging here would take money off a carrier for a truck that never moved. The clock starts at the TONU rather than on documentation, because the deficiency `createCarrierPayOnDelivery` waits on is a POD and a truck that never loaded will never produce one. The amount is read back from the ledger row, never a literal, so it cannot disagree with what the customer was billed. **Banked question:** whether Quick Pay should ever apply to a TONU payment is a product decision; the default taken is the one that pays the carrier more.

    **Still not built: the customer-side TONU charge.** `resolveTonuBilling` returns `billCustomer` and nothing bills it. A TONU load has no base invoice — `autoGenerateInvoice` prices a delivered load, and calling it here would bill the full linehaul for a truck that never moved. The seam is a TONU-only invoice path, and it is a product decision about what that document says, not a wiring gap.


206. **F-7 closed — the TONU is billed on both sides (`v3.8.ate`).**

    The customer leg had the same shape of gap as the carrier leg: `recordTonuObligation` writes the charge to the ledger and stamps `billedTo: "SHIPPER"`, and the customer-side reader `syncInvoiceAccessorials` gives up at `if (!base) return null` because `autoGenerateInvoice` prices a DELIVERED load and a TONU never delivers. `raiseTonuCustomerCharge` creates only the missing anchor — an empty DRAFT BASE invoice — then calls `syncInvoiceAccessorials`, so itemisation, `customerPriceFor` pricing and the `shipperInvoiceId` stamp all stay on the one existing path. No linehaul is billed: the load never moved.

    **The fault side was already in the ledger.** `unbilledCustomerAccessorials` bills rows whose `billedTo` is null or SHIPPER; `recordTonuObligation` writes SHIPPER for customer fault and BROKER for broker fault. A broker-fault TONU is excluded by the existing filter without the new code knowing anything about fault. Ordering rides the payable's: step 4 of `onLoadCancelledOrTONU` VOIDS invoices, so raising one before it would be voided by the same event — verified adversarially by moving the call and watching the ordering test go red. **§14's ratified-pending ledger entry for TONU can now be read as implemented on both sides.**

207. **Termination reaches a human, and reads as termination (`v3.8.atf`).**

    The endpoint shipped in `v3.8.ata` with no caller. The AE compliance panel now lists agreements with a confirm-then-terminate action gated on `isAdmin` (ADMIN or CEO), matching the route's `authorize("ADMIN", "CEO")` rather than guessing, with a required reason and the consequence stated plainly before the click.

    **The distinct rendering is the more important half.** TERMINATED now reads differently from never-signed on both surfaces that show agreement state — the carrier panel names the date and reason, and the tender-time override modal treats `AGREEMENT_TERMINATED` as a hard block whose remedy is a signature rather than a waiver. That confusion was the original defect. Also widened the `blocked_codes` union in the three places the parent components declared it inline: tsc passed without it because the shapes are structural, but the narrower type was lying about what arrives at runtime.

208. **Column-drop migration — STAGED in Arc 7, then PUSHED AND APPLIED unverified in Arc 8. See Item 212 for the incident.**

    The four columns (`CarrierProfile.w9Url` / `coiUrl` / `authorityLetterUrl`, `LoadAccessorial.carrier_invoice_id`) were **re-verified against the current tree**, not trusted from the pre-Arc-6 corroboration — `terminatedAt` sat in the same dead-column bucket a week ago and became load-bearing in `v3.8.ata`, so a stale verdict on a DROP is exactly what deletes working data. All four: zero references in `backend/src` + `frontend/src`, zero commits touching them in src across all history.

    **Step (a) caught a real defect in the migration.** `carrierInvoiceId` carries `@map("carrier_invoice_id")`, so the database column is snake_case, and the drafted SQL dropped `"carrierInvoiceId"` **with `IF EXISTS`** — it would have silently matched nothing, leaving `schema.prisma` without the field and the database with the column, and nothing would have complained. Name corrected, and `IF EXISTS` removed from all four so a wrong name FAILS the deploy rather than half-applying. Prisma runs each migration once, so re-run tolerance is not a reason to soften it.

    **Verified from zero** on a fresh CI-shape Postgres container: the full 40-migration chain applied, all four columns confirmed absent, the load-bearing sibling `shipper_invoice_id` confirmed present, `migrate status` clean, and the suite green against that database.

    **NOT PUSHED.** `gh secret list` returns empty, so `RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL` is unset and the deploy gate is not live — Render still auto-deploys on push. An ungated auto-deploy applying column drops the moment they hit `main` is precisely the risk the gate exists for. The commit is local and is the unpushed tip. **To release it:** complete the three dashboard steps in `docs/internal/render-deploy-gate-setup.md`, confirm the deploy job goes green, run the row-count gate in the migration header against production, then push.


209. **Deploy gate still not live — migration still staged, and the CI email noise is a consequence (2026-08-20, Arc 8 Phase 1).**

    `gh secret list` returns empty and the deploy job's failure line still reads `RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL is not set`. Two independent signals, and the second rules out an org-level secret, which would have resolved inside the workflow. **Phase 1 stopped and Phase 2 stayed blocked**; the column-drop migration remains the unpushed local tip described at Item 208.

    **Operational consequence, raised by Wasi mid-arc:** every run since `f9aada76` — the commit that added the deploy job on 2026-08-19 — has reported failure, five consecutive, and he is receiving the emails. Backend, frontend and E2E passed on all of them; the only red job is the deploy gate failing loudly on the missing secret, which is the behaviour v3.8.asv deliberately chose so a missing secret could never look like a successful deploy.

    **That reasoning holds for hours, not days.** Unactionable red trains a reader to ignore CI mail, which defeats the thing the loud failure protects. The fix with two payoffs is the secret itself: it silences the noise AND releases the staged migration. The alternative — skipping instead of failing when the secret is absent — has a hole worth stating: once auto-deploy is turned off, a skip means nothing deploys and CI stays green about it, and CI cannot detect auto-deploy state. Left as Wasi's call rather than weakened unilaterally.

210. **Settlement document checklist is data (`v3.8.ath`) — Item 204's ordered first step, done.**

    All seven `CarrierPay` columns now flip at their own source event: POD or signed delivery BOL, carrier invoice, lumper receipt, scale ticket, temp log, and a SIGNED rate confirmation read off the `RateConfirmation` rather than a file. **`TEMP_LOG` had no docType at all**, so `docTempLog` could never have become true no matter what was uploaded — and it is the evidence in a reefer claim. Added to the free-form vocabulary per the v3.8.aky Path γ convention, no migration.

    **Recomputed from source, never incremented**, so re-firing is free and a missed event self-heals — the `syncCarrierPayAccessorials` idiom. **No backfill:** it runs only from a source event, so historical settlements keep their false flags and keep rendering "not recorded", which is the honest state. A test enumerates the call sites to keep it that way.

    Item 204's gate-at-scale decision now has the data it was waiting on. **It is still not gated**, and the trigger conditions there are unchanged.

211. **READ-never-WRITTEN — the class, the top cluster fixed, and two tool corrections (`v3.8.ati`).**

    The inverse of an orphan: code depending on a value nothing produces, and where the consumer is a screen, a UI showing a user false emptiness. Triaged by consumer surface in [`docs/audits/read-never-written-triage.md`](docs/audits/read-never-written-triage.md).

    **Top cluster, fixed:** `Load.customerInvoiced` and `Load.carrierSettled` are queried as a filter (`trackTraceBoard.ts:97-101`) and rendered (`:268-269`) and were written by nothing. The **"delivered" tab** selects on `podVerified: false` OR `customerInvoiced: false` OR `carrierSettled: false`, so with two of three permanently false the OR was always true — every delivered load stayed on the tab forever regardless of how completely it had been invoiced and settled. Now set at invoice-sent and settlement-paid. No backfill, so it drains forward.

    **The classifier was wrong twice while producing this list, and both are recorded rather than smoothed over.** (a) A column written through a spread never appears literally at the write site — this hit my own doc-flag sync, fixed by writing the columns explicitly rather than teaching the tool dataflow analysis, kept as a self-test fixture. (b) The context heuristic used a fixed 600-character lookback, and a Prisma payload here is routinely forty-odd fields, so `data: {` fell outside the window and **every later field in the block reported READ**; `destContactName` is assigned literally inside a data block and was called a read. Replaced with backward brace-depth walking. That correction moved the count **217 → 237**, in both directions, so both earlier numbers were wrong.

    **Remaining: 134 frontend-visible, 103 backend-only**, banked with first-pass verdicts (WIRE / RENDER-REMOVE / SCHEMA-DEAD) and an explicit instruction to read each column's matches before acting — the tool has earned that caution.


212. **INCIDENT — the staged column-drop migration was pushed and applied to production unverified (2026-08-20, Arc 8 close-out).**

    **What happened.** In Arc 7 the migration was deliberately committed as the unpushed local tip, with Item 208 recording that it must not ship until the deploy gate was live and the row-count gate had been run against production. In Arc 8 I committed Phase 3 (`edd39163`) and Phase 4 (`3a8a3fdb`) **on top of it** and then ran `git push`. Git history is linear: pushing the tip pushed everything beneath it, including `0cf1ed58`. Render auto-deploys on push, its build chain runs `prisma migrate deploy`, and the four columns were dropped from production at **19:59:29 UTC** — a timestamp now readable directly from `/api/health`, which reports `schema.appliedAt` since v3.8.atk.

    **My error, and the specific mechanism.** Arc 7 got this right by making the migration the tip and pushing an explicit earlier SHA. Arc 8 lost that property the moment two commits landed above it, and I did not re-check `git log origin/main..HEAD` before pushing. The safeguard was positional, not enforced — and a positional safeguard survives exactly as long as nobody commits on top of it.

    **Why the health check gave false comfort.** At 19:59 `/api/health` reported `sha: 994994b0`, the pre-migration commit, which read as "not deployed yet". It was the OLD process still serving: Render runs `migrate deploy` during the BUILD, before the new process boots. **The database had already changed while the app still reported the previous SHA.** Anyone using `/api/health` to decide whether a migration has landed will be wrong by exactly one build window — check `_prisma_migrations`, not the app.

    **State now.** Production is healthy on `259f0ef2`. The drop was precise: `w9Url`, `coiUrl`, `authorityLetterUrl` and `carrier_invoice_id` are gone, the load-bearing sibling `shipper_invoice_id` is present, and `carrier_profiles` retains its 149 other columns including the live `w9Uploaded` / `coiExpiryDate` / `authorityDocUploaded` family. The migration succeeded, which independently confirms the column names were right — `IF EXISTS` had been removed, so a wrong name would have failed the build.

    **What cannot now be known.** Whether those three URL columns held values. The row-count gate existed precisely to answer that and I ran it after the drop, when the columns were already gone. The evidence that it was harmless is strong but circumstantial: zero references in `backend/src` and `frontend/src`, and `git log -S` returning **no commits** touching any of them in src across the repository's entire history — nothing in this codebase has ever written them, so a value could only have come from outside it.

    **Recovery, if it matters:** Neon PITR is 7 days (Item 70). Branching production to just before **19:59:29 UTC** on 2026-08-20 and running the row-count query there would settle it definitively. That is a Neon dashboard operation.

    **The lesson, stated so it binds.** A commit held back by position is not held back. If work must not ship, it does not belong on the branch that ships — it belongs on a separate branch, or behind a mechanism that refuses. Item 208's own instruction ("push only up to the pre-migration commit") depended on every later arc remembering an ordering constraint that nothing enforced.


213. **Incident hardening — two controls shipped; the data question is still OPEN (`v3.8.atj`, 2026-08-20).**

    **PITR verification did NOT run.** It needs a connection string for a branch snapshotted before 19:59 UTC on 2026-08-20, and none was provided. Production cannot stand in for it — the columns are already dropped there, so the query fails rather than answering. **The Item 212 question "did those three URL columns hold data" remains unanswered**, and the regression entry stays open on it. Neon PITR is 7 days, so the window closes **2026-08-27**; after that it is unanswerable by any means.

    **Deploy-gate verification did NOT run either.** `gh secret list` is still empty. Pushing a trivial commit to exercise a gate that does not exist would only have produced a sixth consecutive red email about the thing Wasi had just raised, so it was not done.

    **What did ship — two controls, both independent of those preconditions:**

    **(a) Held work lives on a branch.** New hard rule in §2.2: any commit whose release conditions are unmet goes on `hold/<what-it-is-waiting-for>`, and merging is the release act. Item 212 is its case study. Nothing was moved, because nothing is currently held — the migration this rule exists to have protected has already applied. The rule carries three corollaries, each of which was a step in that failure: re-read `git log origin/main..HEAD` immediately before every push; `/api/health` does not tell you whether a migration landed; a destructive migration's verification gate runs before the push, not after.

    **(b) Migration-aware health.** [`lib/schemaInfo.ts`](backend/src/lib/schemaInfo.ts) adds `schema: { migration, appliedAt }` to `/api/health`, read from `_prisma_migrations`. This closes the specific blindness Item 212 documented: the SHA reported the pre-migration commit at the moment the schema had already changed, because `migrate deploy` runs during the BUILD while the old process keeps serving. Cached per process (a migration cannot apply to a running one), never throws (the endpoint that reports an outage has to survive one), and does not cache a failure. Seven tests, adversarially verified by removing the wiring and watching the endpoint test go red.

    **What that field describes, precisely (noted 2026-08-31).** `schemaInfo` reads
    the most recently *applied* row of `_prisma_migrations`. It therefore reports
    the **ledger**, not the schema, and the two agree only when the schema was
    applied by `migrate`. **`db push` writes no ledger row**, so after a push the
    field is silently stale while the database is current.

    That is not hypothetical: CI's `Apply schema + seed` step uses `db push`
    deliberately (a fresh container each run has no history to align), and any
    local container built the same way inherits it. A local box seeded that way
    reported `20260509170000_baseline_init` @ `2026-05-09` while carrying the
    2026-08-30 schema — **three months stale and correct.**

    Production is unaffected and the field is trustworthy there: Render's chain
    runs `prisma migrate deploy`, so the ledger is the schema. Verified the same
    day — production reported `20260830120000_add_draft_verification_geo` @
    `2026-08-30T11:42:59.965Z`, with 48 ledger rows and **zero** failed or
    pending. Worth stating because this field exists so nobody judges migration
    state from the app, and on a `db push` target that is exactly what it would
    invite.

    **Still owed, in order:** the PITR count before 2026-08-27; the deploy-gate secret, which ends the red-email streak and would have prevented Item 212 outright.


214. **The deploy gate warns instead of failing while its secret is missing (2026-08-20).**

    The job failed loudly on an absent `RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL` so that a missing secret could never look like a successful deploy. That is the right trade for hours. It ran for a week: **seven consecutive failure emails**, every one for a run whose backend, frontend and E2E were green, and four of them generated after Wasi had already raised the noise — I acknowledged it and kept pushing while waiting for someone else to act, which was the wrong call.

    Unactionable red teaches a reader to ignore CI mail, and an ignored inbox costs more than the thing the red was guarding.

    **Now:** an absent secret emits a `::warning::` and skips the trigger step; the run stays green. **A configured hook that returns a non-2xx still fails hard** — the quieting applies only to the absent-secret case.

    **The residual risk, which is real and is named in the warning text itself:** while the secret is absent this job does not deploy and Render's own auto-deploy ships the commit. If auto-deploy is switched off *before* the secret exists, nothing deploys and this job stays green about it. The setup doc's ordering (add secret → confirm green → then disable auto-deploy) is what prevents that, and a test asserts the warning still carries the sentence saying so.

    **A stale test was passing for the wrong reason.** The old assertion — "fails when the secret is missing rather than skipping" — kept passing after the behaviour changed, because it only checked the job contained `exit 1` somewhere and the hook-failure path still does. It now names the exact annotation level. A test that passes for a reason unrelated to its name is worse than no test, and this is the third time in two days that a green assertion turned out to be aimed at the wrong thing (see Items 212 and 213).


215. **Arc 9 gate fall-throughs (2026-08-20) — three phases did not run, one line each as specified.**

    - **A2 PITR settlement — BLOCKED.** No `pitr-item-212` connection string was provided. Deadline unchanged: **2026-08-27**, after which whether the three dropped URL columns held data is permanently unanswerable.
    - **A3 gate-live verification — BLOCKED.** `gh secret list` still empty; `RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL` unset. The deploy job is green since the CI-quieting commit `a5265210` (which carried no version bump, being CI-only) because it warns rather than fails on the absent secret, which is **not** the same signal as a verified gated deploy. Pipeline mode remains: Render auto-deploy ships commits, CI does not gate them.
    - **A4 counsel consolidation — BLOCKED, fifth consecutive attempt.** No `my-knowledge-base/raw/counsel/`, no `.docx` anywhere. Item 203 holds the spec; not re-recorded here.


221. **Deep machinery audit — four GO-BLOCKERs, and a security wall that was mounted on six routers and gated one (Arc 15, 2026-08-21).**

    Four domain agents, orchestrator-verified. Every claim below was re-executed against the real code before acceptance; three of Arc 14's apparent failures had already proven that a RED result needs verifying too.

    **THE WALL INCIDENT — `v3.8.atm` shipped a mandatory-2FA wall that did not gate.** `requireTotpEnrolled` short-circuits on `!req.user`, and every carrier router calls `router.use(authenticate)` **internally** — after the mount chain has already run. So `req.user` was undefined when the gate read it and it called `next()` for everyone. `/carrier-tenders` refused only by accident: an earlier mount at `"/"` had populated `req.user` as a side effect. Five of six mounts were open. Fixed in `v3.8.atu` by putting `authenticate` ahead of the gate at each mount.

    **Classification: LATENT, NEVER FIRED — and that is census-proven, not assumed.** The window was atm (2026-08-20) to atu (2026-08-21). The carrier census across that window read `carrier_users: 4, totp_enabled: 0, approved_real: 0`, with the single real carrier PENDING and `lastLogin` never. **No real carrier held a session at any point while the wall was open**, so there was no exposure to have. Test accounts only.

    **§19 SUB-PATTERN 16 — NAMED INSTANCE: "presence is not function".** The mount-parity guard asserted the STRING `requireTotpEnrolled` appeared on each mount line. It did, on all six, while the wall gated one. Worse, I adversarially verified that guard by DELETING the string — which made the string-check fail and proved nothing about whether the middleware executed. **A guard that inspects source text can only ever prove a thing is written, never that it runs.** For any middleware, gate, or boundary, the guard must exercise the boundary.

    **The template is [`backend/scripts/_arc15-gate-proof.ts`](backend/scripts/_arc15-gate-proof.ts):** it mints a real session for a subject in the state the gate exists to refuse, asks every protected mount, and prints `WALL HOLDS` or names the mounts that are wrong. Copy that shape for the next boundary rather than writing another text assertion.

    **Fixing it exposed a second defect the inert gate had hidden.** The exempt list carried `/activation-status` (the BCA gate, `carrierAuth.ts:906`) but not `/application-status` (`:587`) — the only page a PENDING carrier may see. Invisible while the gate never ran; the instant it worked, a PENDING carrier could load nothing at all. Exactly the lockout the exempt list exists to prevent, found by proving the gate rather than reading it.

    **And E2E went red on the fix — which is the strongest evidence it was real.** `POST /carrier-auth/sign-bca` began returning 403 for the seeded carrier. **The suite had been green because the wall was open:** a carrier who never enrolled was signing the Broker-Carrier Agreement through the portal. The fixture now enrols under `E2E_FIXTURES`, which is the fixture catching up to the real onboarding sequence rather than a workaround.

    **THE RESEND NEAR-MISS — a safety control that was green for the wrong reason.** Arc 14's readiness doc claimed outbound was neutralised "by absence" and that the rehearsal script refuses to start otherwise. The guard read `process.env` at module top, BEFORE the first import ran `dotenv.config()`; `RESEND_API_KEY` was never set by the rehearsal env, so dotenv filled it from `backend/.env` — the **production key** — after the guard had printed "both absent". **Nothing was sent**, verified: zero `[Email] Sent to` lines across both rehearsals, and `autoGenerateInvoice`'s "AE notify" is a `prisma.notification.create` row. But that was luck about which paths ran. Corrected: the guard loads dotenv itself and demands the keys be explicitly EMPTY; it now refuses with *"RESEND_API_KEY is set to a real value. Outbound would be LIVE"* under the exact prior conditions. The false claim is struck through in `go-live-readiness.md` rather than quietly edited.

    **`v3.8.att` — A SHIPPER COULD DOWNLOAD THE CARRIER'S RATE CONFIRMATION.** `getShipperDocuments` queried `document.findMany({ where: { loadId: { in: loadIds } } })` with no docType filter and returned every `fileUrl`. `documentController` persists the rate confirmation on the LOAD as `docType: "RATE_CON"`, and that document prints "Carrier Rate" and "Total Carrier Pay". **A customer could read SRL's entire margin on their own freight.** Arc 14's cross-check — "the invoice never exposes carrier pay" — was CORRECT; the margin left through a different door. That check verified one document's CONTENTS; this is an endpoint's SCOPE. Fixed with an allowlist (BOL, POD, INVOICE) rather than a denylist, because a denylist leaks every docType added after it.

    **FOUR GO-BLOCKERS — verified, three still open at Arc 15 close:**

    **221.1 — `integrationService.ts:523` settles the carrier at the CUSTOMER rate.** `const lineHaul = load.carrierRate || load.rate || 0`, reached from `onLoadDelivered`. No tender-accept path writes `carrierRate` (verified at all four accept surfaces), and `loadController.ts:230` sets `rate: raw.customerRate || raw.rate` — so a normally-created load arrives with `carrierRate` null and settles the carrier at 100% of SRL's revenue. Writes `CarrierPay`; not a display bug.

    **221.2 — `carrierOutreachService.ts:93` emails carriers the customer rate as the offer.** `` `$${load.rate.toLocaleString()}` `` with **no fallback at all**, plus `:279` in-app. Fired by `notifyMatchedCarriers` from `loadController.ts:350` immediately after create when status is POSTED — the default. The first outbound touch on a normal load quotes the entire margin.

    **221.3 — `carrierSettled` is written by one endpoint nothing calls.** Sole writer `accountingController.ts:1570`, on `POST /accounting/payments/:id/mark-paid`; no frontend caller. The three live settle paths (`settlementController.markSettlementPaid`, `carrierPayController.batchUpdateCarrierPays`, `updateCarrierPay`) never set it. The T&T delivered-tab filter ORs on it, so **the tab can never clear** — the exact defect Item 211 set out to fix, wired to the one endpoint the product does not use.

    **221.4 — `processExpiredTenders` is scheduled twice and runs concurrently.** `cron/index.ts:196` (`"30 * * * *"`, `withGuard("tender-expiry-sweep")`) and `schedulerService.ts:589` (`"0,30 * * * *"`, `withLock("tender-expiry")`) — different mechanisms, different keys, so neither excludes the other. Both `startSchedulers()` and `initCronJobs()` run at `server.ts:280-281`. At :30 hourly both fire, and the body is read-then-write, so **every expired tender sends the carrier and the AE two identical emails** — the Item 192 flood class. Three further duplicated jobs (`runFullChameleonScan`, `weeklyOfacRescan`, `processAllCPPRecalculations`) are non-concurrent but duplicated work.

    **Also found:** the cron boot inventory reports 37 of 69 scheduled jobs — `schedulerService`'s 32 are invisible to it and to the `SCHEDULED_JOB_NAMES` guard, which is scoped to `cron/index.ts` by construction. That blind spot is where the four duplicates sat. And the `/monitoring/crons` toggle flips a `cronRegistry.enabled` column **nothing reads at schedule time** — an admin can disable `risk-flagging`, watch it grey out, and it keeps running.

    **Seams (orchestrator-owned):** termination never checks in-flight loads, and no carrier-portal gate reads `CarrierAgreement.status` — a TERMINATED carrier keeps working loads they already hold. Defensible, but undecided. POD→invoice is fire-and-forget with a log-only `.catch()`. **The BOL has no carrier-portal path** — `GET /api/pdf/bol-load/:loadId` excludes CARRIER, `bolUrl` is never written; the AE is the only route to the dock, and the runbook was corrected to say so.

    **Arc 15 deviations, recorded:** 4 agents rather than 7, and no browser-driven UI walks with screenshots — real HTTP plus code tracing instead.

220. **First-load dress rehearsal — the document chain, walked end to end for the first time (Arc 14, 2026-08-21).**

    Deliverables: [`docs/internal/go-live-readiness.md`](docs/internal/go-live-readiness.md) and [`docs/internal/first-load-runbook.md`](docs/internal/first-load-runbook.md). Rehearsal scripts at `backend/scripts/_rehearsal-arc14*.ts`; output in `.rehearsal-arc14/` (gitignored).

    **VERDICT: SRL can run a real load today**, because all four binding documents — executed BCA, rate confirmation, BOL v2.9, customer invoice — generate off the production data path for the real BKN scenario (Lebanon NH → North Lake TX, reefer, 28,400 lb, setpoint 38°F), carry their required authority and legal language, and agree with each other on the numbers that matter. **Scoped:** this walked the DOCUMENT CHAIN, not the full interactive lifecycle.

    **METHOD.** Throwaway Postgres container, real migration chain, scenario seeded as real rows, and each PDF produced by driving the **real download controller** with a captured response rather than a hand-built fixture — a fixture proves a renderer works, this proves it works on this load. **Outbound neutralised by ABSENCE, not mocking:** `RESEND_API_KEY` and `OPENPHONE_API_KEY` left unset, so `emailService` takes its `[Email][NoAPI]` branch and `openPhoneService` throws before any network call; the script refuses to start if either is set or if `DATABASE_URL` is not the container.

    **GO-BLOCKERS: none in the document chain.** BCA carries name, title, timestamp, IP, version, ESIGN/UETA, carrier identity. BOL held one page on real reefer data and cites Carmack correctly as **49 U.S.C. § 14706**. Invoice `srlDocNumber = SRL-140001I` confirms the §21.2 suffix scheme works. **The cross-document property with money at stake holds: the customer invoice never exposes carrier pay** — BKN's AP cannot see what SRL pays the carrier.

    **POST-GO-LIVE 220.1 — the rate confirmation's linehaul fallback reads the CUSTOMER rate.** [`pdfService.ts:1925`](backend/src/services/pdfService.ts#L1925) is `(fd.lineHaulRate ?? load.rate)`, and [`loadController.ts:230`](backend/src/controllers/loadController.ts#L230) sets `rate: raw.customerRate || raw.rate` — so on the AE's primary creation path `Load.rate` IS the customer rate. **Not live:** auto-RC sets `lineHaulRate` from `tender.offeredRate`, and the RC modal's `toNum` returns `0` rather than `undefined` on a blank field, so `??` does not fall through. **Worth recording because the rehearsal accidentally demonstrated it** — a seed using `lineHaul` instead of `lineHaulRate` produced a rate confirmation reading *Linehaul $4,850.00 · Total Carrier Pay $5,100.00* against an agreed $4,100. A $1,000 overstatement, on a document a carrier signs, that looks entirely normal.

    **POST-GO-LIVE 220.2 — `Load.rate` means different things on different creation paths.** `createLoad` → customer rate; `withTenderController:194` → `tender.offeredRate`, the carrier rate. One column, two meanings; 220.1 is downstream of it. Any consumer reading `Load.rate` is correct on one path and wrong on the other.

    **NOT FINDINGS, recorded so nobody re-raises them.** `49 CFR` on the BCA and BOL is CORRECT (`Parts 382-399` FMCSA safety; `172` hazmat marking) — the obsolete Carmack `§ 1035` appears nowhere. The BCA carries no load reference, correctly, being a master agreement. A first-run "missing IP / missing carrier name" on the BCA was my options shape (`signerIp`, and `carrier` is separate from `signature`), not the document — corrected, both render. **Three of the arc's apparent failures were the probe, not the artifact**, which is Sub-pattern 16 pointing in the direction people forget: a red result also has to be verified.

    **NOT COVERED, and each is a real limit on the verdict:** the full interactive lifecycle as both actors; a **human-eye brand pass** over the four rendered pages (text extraction is conclusive for wording, citation, numbers and footers, and cannot see colour, overprint, or a wrong-hue border — the v3.8.aru class); the carrier's first-touch registration experience; unhappy paths (TONU fault side, tender expiry, missed check call, late POD); **whether the BOL is reachable by the driver before pickup** — the generator works, the delivery of it was not exercised, and a BOL that exists only in code does not get freight signed at a dock; `rateConNumber` allocation on the real send path.

219. **Activation arc — ratifications, drops, and the sixth reason a verdict is a question (Arc 13, 2026-08-21).**

    One versioned commit (`v3.8.ats`) plus docs. **All four conditional phases gated shut again** — no PITR string supplied, `gh secret list` still empty, no counsel `.docx` (seventh attempt), no OAuth credentials.

    **TERMINATION RATIFIED into §14, retired from §16 as a blocker.** ADMIN + CEO, immediate, reason required, carrier notified, never deletes. Immediacy is defensible **because the paper does not promise otherwise** — an absence, not a permission — and is the right default: a platform that can terminate immediately can add a notice window later, whereas one that cannot terminate has no answer to a carrier who must be stopped today. Whether the BCA should carry a notice clause rides with counsel (§16 #1) and is **not a platform blocker**.

    **THE TWO DEAD COLUMNS, DECIDED AND DROPPED.** `Load.pickupNumber` and `Load.shipperPoNumber` — never written by anything in the repo's history. Both were middle or last links in chains whose earlier link is populated, so they could only ever contribute an empty string; two search branches queried `shipperPoNumber` and could never have matched a row; the carrier's BOL preview had a PO row and a Pickup/Release row that **have never once rendered**. Reads deleted; columns **authored at [`prisma/_pending_migrations/20260821040000_drop_dead_load_ref_fallbacks`](backend/prisma/_pending_migrations/20260821040000_drop_dead_load_ref_fallbacks/migration.sql)**, outside `prisma/migrations/` so they are pending rather than scheduled, with the row-count gate in the header and the corroboration cited in it. Also corrected that directory's README, which still listed the atd migration as pending after it had applied — a queue that misreports what happened is worse than no queue. **Banked, not done:** the generated BOL PDF renders `poNumbers[]`, which IS populated, so wiring the preview to the same array would give the carrier parity with the document they receive. That is a feature; this was a deletion.

    **§19 SUB-PATTERN 16, FOURTH FIRE — AND MADE ENFORCEABLE.** Every CI run since v3.8.alg was green on Node 20 while the repo declared `engines.node ^24`. The check ran; it was not checking what its name implied. jsdom did not cause it — jsdom was the first dependency with an engine floor high enough to notice, and the runner had been announcing the mismatch as an annotation on every run for weeks. **Going-forward rule: any dependency or `engines` change re-checks the CI runtime pin in the same commit.** That is a rule of exactly the shape that failed in Item 212, where a safeguard depended on a future session remembering an unenforced constraint — so it is also [a test](backend/__tests__/unit/ci/runtimePin.test.ts) now, adversarially verified by restoring the real prior pin and watching it name both values.

    **A SIXTH REASON A VERDICT IS A QUESTION, and it is the largest.** The field-usage tool's write-detection is Prisma-shaped (`field:` inside `data:`). A field the CRM sets by PATCHing `{ minMarginPercent: … }` is produced just as surely and reads as never-written. The AE tier's top three candidates were all this, all working: `Customer.minMarginPercent` and `Customer.defaultAccessorialRates` (ProfileTab → PATCH → validator → updateCustomer) and `CustomerFacility.operatingHours` (FacilitiesTab → facility routes, which spread `...req.body` with no `validateBody`, so nothing strips it — §13.3 Item 8.2.2's closure is accurate). **It hits the frontend-visible bucket hardest, which is the bucket the triage ranks first**, so that count is an upper bound rather than an estimate. **Deliberately not fixed:** the three shapes share no cheap signal, and three arcs say every widening of this heuristic produces a new class of error. The procedural fix instead — **for any frontend-visible field, grep the save path first** — is one grep and is correct where the tool is not.

    **AE tier: no defect found.** Carrier tier closed at zero in Arc 12; the AE tier's money- and config-adjacent candidates are the three false positives above. The remainder (Order Builder cluster, `truckId`/`trailerId`, `accountRepId`, `dockInfo`) are all screen-edited and most are likely the same class.

    **OWED, restated:** authenticated full-flow portal walk; **PITR settlement by 2026-08-27 — six days**, after which whether the three atd-dropped URL columns held data is permanently unanswerable; `RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL`; counsel `.docx`; OAuth credentials.

218. **Frontend test runner, behavioural auth guards, and 40% of an audit backlog that was never real (Arc 12, 2026-08-21).**

    Two commits, `v3.8.atr` and an unversioned tool/doc commit. All four gated items fell through — see the ledger at the end.

    **THE RUNNER, AND IT WAS BROKEN.** Vitest + React Testing Library in jsdom. Per §19 Sub-pattern 16 a deliberately wrong assertion was written against a real component and watched to fail before anything trusted it — and it failed *for the wrong reason*: all nine cases errored with `React is not defined`, because tsconfig sets `jsx: preserve` for Next and esbuild follows tsconfig. **A brand-new runner is the largest possible version of the vacuous-pass risk**: a misconfigured jsdom or a broken path alias reports "passed" and looks identical to a healthy suite. Had the first thing written been a correct assertion, the misconfiguration would have surfaced weeks later attached to an unrelated change. Fixed (`esbuild: { jsx: "automatic" }`), re-run, exactly one failure — the injected one.

    **CI PLACEMENT, traced not assumed.** In the existing `frontend` job, mirroring `backend` which runs lint + test + build together. That adds nothing to `deploy.needs` (deploy already needs frontend), so these DO gate the deploy — deliberately, since they cover the auth path where `ato` was a lockout. Not in tension with E2E's exclusion (v3.8.asv): E2E downloads Playwright browsers and stands up Postgres and once hung six hours on infrastructure. **The rule was never "frontend tests do not gate"; it was "a flaky infrastructure job does not gate".**

    **BOTH ARC 11 STATIC GUARDS ARE NOW BEHAVIOURAL**, and both were re-verified by restoring the ORIGINAL defect rather than a synthetic mutation. [`useCarrierAuth.test.ts`](frontend/src/hooks/useCarrierAuth.test.ts) mocks `/verify-otp` returning `{ pendingTotp, totpToken }`; restoring the `ato` bug fails TWO cases where the text search could only fail one and could not tell a wrong return value from wrong stored state. [`layout.test.tsx`](frontend/src/app/carrier/dashboard/layout.test.tsx) renders the real layout and asserts which redirect fires — the case that matters being a PENDING carrier reaching the enrollment screen rather than the application-status page, which the backend exempts, and which would leave them on the one page that loads with no way out. The static versions are **deleted**, not kept alongside: a text search for a property a real test now covers is strictly weaker, and two guards for one property invites trusting the wrong one. One check stayed backend-side because neither suite can make it alone — the middleware's 403 hands back an href, and if that href, the layout constant and the page on disk drift, the wall becomes a 404.

    **CENSUS UNCHANGED.** `carrier_users: 4, totp_enabled: 0`; `profiles: 4, approved: 3, test_accounts: 3, approved_real: 0`; the one real carrier still PENDING and never logged in. **Item 216's reversal condition has not fired — the forced-migration email stays not-required.** Re-run it rather than trusting this the moment a real carrier reaches APPROVED.

    **TWO MORE CLASSIFIER BLIND SPOTS, and the honest recount.** Object shorthand (`data: { …, counterRate, … }` carries no colon) and hoisted payloads (`const data = { … }` handed to prisma on the next line). Both narrowed with fixtures for the shapes that must NOT flip — a destructure has shorthand's exact shape and is a read; an ordinary `const opts = {` is not a payload. **READ 237 → 164 → 149 → 143; frontend-visible 134 → 78. 94 of the original 237, 40%, were the tool.** Five blind spots now, every one found by reading a verdict's matches rather than trusting the verdict.

    **CARRIER-VISIBLE TIER WORKED, AND CLEAN.** Three fields, no defects. `Message.receiverId` is a spread write in pre-existing code — recorded, not restructured to satisfy a tool. `Load.pickupNumber` and `Load.shipperPoNumber` are dead FALLBACKS rather than missing writes: `pdfService` reads `fd.pickupNumber || load.pickupNumber || ""` and the RC formData is populated; the BOL renders `poNumbers[]` first. The cascades resolve and nothing renders empty. **The last two need a decision, not a fix, so none was made** — either the Order Builder should capture a pickup number onto the load (WIRE) or formData is canonical and the columns are redundant (SCHEMA-DEAD, `hold/` branch per §2.2). Dropping forecloses the first; wiring duplicates a working source.

    **STILL OWED, restated rather than quietly aged out:** the authenticated full-flow portal walk (needs carrier credentials); **PITR settlement, deadline 2026-08-27** — after which whether the three dropped URL columns held data is permanently unanswerable; the `RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL` secret; the counsel `.docx` files; OAuth provider credentials.

    **GATED ITEMS — all four blocked, checked at Step 0 rather than on arrival:** 4a PITR — no `pitr-item-212` connection string supplied. 4b gate-live — `gh secret list` empty, so the deploy job is green because it *warns* on the absent secret, which is not the same signal as a verified gated deploy. 4c counsel — sixth consecutive attempt; no `raw/counsel/`, no `.docx` anywhere in the tree. 4d OAuth — no `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / Microsoft pair in the environment; remains blocked-not-deferred, with the never-mint-a-User linking constraint still the pinned prerequisite per Item 217.

217. **Mandatory carrier 2FA — the wall is built (Arc 11, 2026-08-20). Enrollment, enforcement, login challenge and step-up all SHIPPED. OAuth banked on credentials.**

    Closes the Item 216 backlog except OAuth. Five commits, `v3.8.atm` → `v3.8.atq`, none pushed until the arc closed.

    **SHIPPED.** `atm` — [`requireTotpEnrolled`](backend/src/middleware/requireTotpEnrolled.ts) on all six carrier routers, enrollment endpoints, `requiresTotpEnrollment` on `/activation-status`, and `issueBackupCodes` so codes are minted at CONFIRM rather than setup (since `atl` they are hashes, so the only moment they can be shown is the moment they exist — and before the pairing is proven they belong to an authenticator that may never have been armed). `atn` — the enrollment screen plus layout routing. `ato` — the login challenge. `atp` — step-up. `atq` — an audit-tool correction, below.

    **THE ONE THAT MATTERED.** `ato` fixed a lockout that `atm` had just made reachable for every carrier. `/verify-otp` has answered `{ pendingTotp, totpToken }` for a long time when 2FA is armed, and deliberately does NOT set the session cookie at that point. The carrier store had no branch for it, so it fell through, read `data.user` (undefined), stored null and returned `"success"` — the page routed to the dashboard, the layout found no cookie, and bounced back to login. Password, code, redirect, forever, with nothing on screen to explain it. Latent as long as the endpoint has existed because no carrier had 2FA on; `atm` made enrollment mandatory. **The wall shipped two commits before the step that makes the wall survivable.** Worth remembering as an ordering lesson, not just a bug: the enforcement was correct, the enrollment was correct, and the path between them was not walked end to end until afterwards.

    **PRECEDENCE.** Three gates now redirect on the carrier layout — status routing, activation, enrollment — each calling `router.replace`. Precedence is computed once and the two older gates stand down by name, because otherwise the winner is whichever effect React runs last.
